meta.title: The Symbol Word List of Scripture
meta.note: Word-level companion to the Symbol Lexicon. Every symbol word found in Scripture, Genesis to Revelation, each with its Old Testament root and the meaning Scripture itself assigns. Entries tied to a Symbol Lexicon page or queue candidate carry that code under lexicon (M = master, Q = queue).

changelog: 1014 V1 — first build: 855 words swept from all of Scripture in eight sections, merged by word, checked against the master (229) and queue (126).

1014 V2 — 22 words held back for editorial review removed; 11 breastplate and foundation stones with no meaning of their own folded into one entry, The Twelve Stones; six loose Lexicon links removed (Cart, Oxen, Oracle, Unicorn, Planting, Tree).
1014 V3 — Tree rewritten: primary meaning now the tree as a man and the trees as people and rulers (Deut 20:19; Judg 9:8-15; Dan 4:20-22; Isa 61:3); the Marah tree moved to the further uses.
changes: Tree rewritten: the primary meaning is now the tree as a man and the trees as people and rulers, rooted in Deuteronomy 20:19 and Jotham's parable in Judges 9:8-15.
The tree at Marah, formerly the primary meaning, now stands first among the further uses.

words.meaning: Adam, formed from the ground, is "the figure of him that was to come" (Rom 5:14); as in Adam all die, so in Messiah, the last Adam, shall all be made alive (1 Cor 15:22, 45).

The adder is the poison of the wicked: deaf to the charmer (Ps 58:4), with adders' poison under their lips (Ps 140:3; Rom 3:13); wine at last bites like an adder (Prov 23:32), and the faithful tread on the adder (Ps 91:13).

also.meaning: Dan shall be "a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that biteth the horse heels"; the adder pictures hidden venom (Ps 58:4; Prov 23:32), and Dan leads Israel's idolatry (Judg 18:30) and is missing from the sealed tribes (Rev 7).

words.meaning: Belonging and life restored: "bone of my bones" (Gen 2:23), members of his body, of his flesh and bones (Eph 5:30); dry bones are the whole house of Israel made to live (Ezek 37:11), and no bone of the Pesach lamb broken (John 19:36).

also.meaning: Not a bone of the Pesach lamb was to be broken; John quotes it of Messiah on the stake (John 19:36).
The sufferer's bones are out of joint and can be counted (Ps 22:14, 17), yet Yahuah "keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken" (Ps 34:20), fulfilled in Messiah (John 19:36).
"These bones are the whole house of Israel" saying "our hope is lost" (Ezek 37:11) - a dead people raised by the word and Yahuah's breath, graves opened and brought into the land.

words.meaning: Bread is man's daily life; Scripture lifts it to the word and commandments: "man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Yahuah" (Deut 8:3), and Messiah is the bread of life (John 6:35).

also.meaning: Bread is the daily provision tied to the word: not by bread alone but by every word of Yahuah (Deut 8:3); bread pictures the commandments walked out daily and Messiah the bread of life.

The word and commandments by which man lives: "man doth not live by bread only, but by every word" of Yahuah (Deut 8:3; Matt 4:4); Messiah is the bread from heaven (John 6:35), and leaven of bread means doctrine (Matt 16:12).

lexicon.title: Bread and Wine of the Covenant Meal

words.meaning: Yahuah's breath makes dust a living soul (Gen 2:7); the same breath raises the dry bones (Ezek 37:9-10) and the slain witnesses (Rev 11:11), His spirit giving life.

also.meaning: "Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain" (Ezek 37:9) - Yahuah's own life-giving spirit: "I shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live" (37:14).

words.meaning: The crushing of the promised Seed (Gen 3:15): "it pleased Yahuah to bruise him" (Isa 53:10) - Yahuah laying iniquity on His Servant, who in turn crushes the serpent's head (Rom 16:20).

Guardians of Yahuah's presence (Eden, the mercy seat) and bearers of His throne - Ezekiel's living creatures "were the cherubims" (Ezek 10:20); proud Tyre is the fallen "anointed cherub that covereth" (Ezek 28:14).
Cherubim guard the way to the tree of life, then overshadow the mercy seat (Exod 25:20) and bear Yahuah's throne (Ezek 10:20); they mark the guarded holy presence of Yahuah.

also.meaning: Guardians of the way to the tree of life (Gen 3:24) and attendants of Yahuah's throne, who "dwellest between the cherubims" (Ps 80:1); Ezekiel identifies them with the living creatures (Ezek 10:20).

Guardians of Yahuah's holiness and His throne: they kept the way to the tree of life (Gen 3:24), overshadowed the mercy seat where He met Israel (Exod 25:22; Heb 9:5), and bore His glory in Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 10).

words.meaning: Darkness is the state before Yahuah speaks and the realm of ignorance, sin and judgment; the called are brought "out of darkness into his marvellous light" (1 Pet 2:9; Col 1:13).

also.meaning: Separation from Yahuah: the darkness of Egypt (Exod 10:21), the people in darkness who see great light (Isa 9:2); the unfaithful are cast into outer darkness (Matt 8:12) and believers delivered from its power (Col 1:13).

Darkness that could be felt fell on Egypt while Israel had light in their dwellings; darkness covers the earth but Yahuah's glory rises on His people (Isa 60:2); the fifth bowl repeats it (Rev 16:10).

lexicon.title: Fifth Bowl: Darkness on the Beast's Throne

words.meaning: The deep is the formless, watery void over which Yahuah's spirit moved; Scripture reuses it for overwhelming trouble (Ps 42:7; Jonah 2:5) and for the abyss from which judgment and the beast rise (Rev 9:1-2).

A door is an opening for entry or temptation: "if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar" (Song 8:9); the everlasting doors lift up for the King of glory (Ps 24:7), and Messiah is the door of the sheep (John 10:9).

also.meaning: Sin lies at the door (Gen 4:7); the ark had one door and Yahuah shut it (Gen 7:16), and the door shut on the foolish virgins (Matt 25:10) shows a set time, while Messiah is "the door" of the sheep (John 10:9).

lexicon.title: Standing at the Door and Knocking

words.meaning: Dust is man's frail origin and end (Gen 3:19; Ps 103:14), the serpent's food under the curse (Gen 3:14), and also Abraham's countless seed (Gen 13:16); the first man is "of the earth, earthy" (1 Cor 15:47).

also.meaning: Man's origin and mortality, "dust thou art" (Gen 3:19; Ps 103:14), and Abraham's countless seed (Gen 13:16); shaking off the dust of the feet testifies against a city that rejects the message (Matt 10:14).
Those who "sleep in the dust of the earth" are the dead awaiting resurrection, some to everlasting life and some to shame (Dan 12:2) — the same twofold rising Yahushua describes (John 5:28-29).

words.meaning: The garden lies eastward and man is driven out eastward (Gen 3:24); Cain and Babel's builders move east, away from Yahuah (Gen 4:16; 11:2), and the glory returns "from the way of the east" (Ezek 43:2).

also.meaning: The way out from Yahuah's presence (east of Eden, Babel) - elders turn their backs on the temple to worship the sun eastward (Ezek 8:16); the glory departs east and returns by the east (Ezek 11:23; 43:2).

words.meaning: The fig tree pictures Israel: Yahuah found her fathers "as the firstripe in the fig tree" (Hos 9:10), Jeremiah's baskets of good and bad figs are the exiles and the remnant (Jer 24), and the barren fig tree faces judgment.

also.meaning: Israel as Yahuah's fig tree: good and bad figs are the exiles and the remnant left behind (Jer 24:5-8); the barren and cursed fig tree shows leaves without fruit (Luke 13:6-9; Matt 21:19), and its budding marks the season (Matt 24:32).
Interpreted by Yahuah: the good figs are the captives sent to Chaldea for their good, the naughty figs are Zedekiah and the remnant left in the land or fled to Egypt (Jer 24:5, 8).

lexicon.title: Fig Leaves and Tunics of Skin

words.meaning: Fig leaves are the covering man sews for himself; Scripture shows such self-made coverings fail ("their webs shall not become garments," Isa 59:6), and a fig tree with leaves but no fruit is cursed (Matt 21:19).

lexicon.title: Fig Leaves and Tunics of Skin

words.meaning: The expanse over the creatures' heads "as the colour of the terrible crystal" with the throne above it (Ezek 1:22, 26) - the heaven Yahuah spread, His throne set over all creation.
Eden's river parts into four heads to reach the whole land; Scripture uses four for the full reach of the earth: four corners and four winds (Isa 11:12; Rev 7:1).

Every tree yields after its kind (Gen 1:11), so "by their fruits ye shall know them" (Matt 7:20); the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace (Gal 5:22), and the Father is glorified when much fruit is borne (John 15:8).

Eden is Yahuah's planted dwelling with man; the prophets promise Zion's wilderness made "like Eden" (Isa 51:3), the bride is a garden enclosed (Song 4:12), and the overcomer eats in the paradise of Elohim (Rev 2:7).

also.meaning: "A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse" (Song 4:12): the bride kept for her beloved alone; the restored people are a watered garden (Isa 58:11; Jer 31:12), recalling Eden.
The restored soul "like a watered garden" (Isa 58:11; Jer 31:12); the desolate land made "like the garden of Eden" (Ezek 36:35) - Eden recovered.

Eden, the first sanctuary (Gen 2:8); the beloved is a garden enclosed (Song 4:12), the obedient a watered garden (Isa 58:11); Messiah was taken in a garden and laid in a new tomb in a garden (John 18:1; 19:41).

words.meaning: Adam was put in the garden to dress and keep it (Gen 2:15); Mary, at the garden tomb, supposed the risen Messiah to be the gardener (John 20:15), the last Adam standing where the first had failed.

"The gold of that land is good"; gold pictures what is precious and tried: tested belief (1 Pet 1:7), Yahuah's judgments "more to be desired than gold" (Ps 19:10), and the pure gold of the holy city (Rev 21:18).

also.meaning: Pure gold covered everything within the holy places (Exod 25:11); tried gold pictures proven trust (Job 23:10; 1 Pet 1:7), Yahushua counsels "buy of me gold tried in the fire" (Rev 3:18), and the city is pure gold (Rev 21:18).
"How is the gold become dim!" - Zion's precious sons, "comparable to fine gold", now esteemed as earthen pitchers (Lam 4:1-2); trial brings the faithful forth as gold (Job 23:10).

Tried belief: "when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold" (Job 23:10); the trial of belief is more precious than gold tried with fire (1 Pet 1:7), and works of gold survive the fire (1 Cor 3:12-13).
The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon: "Thou art this head of gold" (Dan 2:38); Babylon is "a golden cup" in Yahuah's hand (Jer 51:7), and the harlot keeps the gold (Rev 17:4).

words.meaning: Man was made in Yahuah's image to show His likeness (Gen 1:27); Messiah is the image of the invisible Elohim (Col 1:15), while Babylon and the beast set up counterfeit images to be worshipped (Dan 3:1; Rev 13:14).

also.meaning: Man made in Elohim's image (Gen 1:27); Messiah is the image of the invisible Elohim, the visible reflection of the unseen Father (Col 1:15), believers conformed to his image (Rom 8:29), and the beast's image is the counterfeit (Rev 13:14).

The great image is the line of world kingdoms from Babylon onward, shown as one man-shaped body (Dan 2:37-40); Nebuchadnezzar's golden image in Dura shows the same power demanding worship, the pattern of the image of the beast (Rev 13:15).

words.meaning: Light comes first by Yahuah's word; Scripture names Yahuah Himself the light (Ps 27:1; 1 John 1:5), His word a lamp (Ps 119:105), and the Lamb the lamp that bears that light (Rev 21:23).

also.meaning: Yahuah is light and the source of it (Gen 1:3; Ps 27:1; 1 John 1:5); Messiah bears that light into the world (John 1:9; 8:12), and believers, once darkness, are light in the Master (Eph 5:8).
Yahuah is the everlasting light (Isa 60:19); He gives His Servant "for a light to the Gentiles" (Isa 49:6) - the bearer who carries Yahuah's light to the nations (Luke 2:32).

words.meaning: Above the throne "the likeness as the appearance of a man" - "the likeness of the glory of Yahuah" (Ezek 1:26, 28): the glory shown in the form man was made in (Gen 1:26), borne by the Son of Man (Dan 7:13; Heb 1:3).

The lesser light rules the night and marks appointed times; Jacob reads it as the mother of the house (Gen 37:10), it is a faithful witness in heaven (Ps 89:37), and it lies under the woman's feet (Rev 12:1).

lexicon.title: Sun Black as Sackcloth, Moon as Blood

words.meaning: Innocent nakedness becomes shame after sin (Gen 3:7); nakedness pictures a soul exposed without Yahuah's covering, and Messiah counsels white raiment "that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear" (Rev 3:18).

Stone of Eden's Havilah (Gen 2:12), engraved with the twelve names "according to their birth" on the ephod's shoulders and set eleventh in the breastplate (Exod 28:9-10,20) — Israel carried on shoulder and heart.

A day's wage paid alike to every laborer (Matt 20:2-15), the good Samaritan's payment (Luke 10:35), and a famine price for grain (Rev 6:6); its image and superscription raise whose image man bears (Matt 22:20).

The river out of Eden waters the garden and parts to the world; it returns as the river that makes glad the city of Elohim (Ps 46:4), Ezekiel's healing river, and the river of water of life (Rev 22:1).

also.meaning: Waters issuing from under the threshold become a river that heals the sea - "every thing shall live whither the river cometh" (Ezek 47:9); the river of the water of life (Rev 22:1).
Egypt's river is the source of its boast and the place of death for the sons; Ezekiel names Pharaoh the dragon lying in his rivers (Ezek 29:3), and the serpent's flood echoes it (Rev 12:15).
The man in linen standing above the river's waters lifts both hands to heaven and swears by Him that lives forever (Dan 12:7), the pattern of the mighty angel's oath over sea and land (Rev 10:5-6).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life
One Foot on Sea and Land (the Oath)

words.meaning: The seventh day blessed and set apart (Gen 2:3), a sign "that ye may know that I am Yahuah that doth sanctify you" (Exod 31:13) and first of the appointed times (Lev 23:3); "there remaineth therefore a rest" (Heb 4:9).

also.meaning: "I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am Yahuah that sanctify them" (Ezek 20:12) - the standing mark of His people, polluted by Israel and still kept for the nations who join (Isa 56:6).

words.meaning: The woman's seed is promised to crush the serpent's head; Paul shows the seed of the promise is singular, "which is Messiah" (Gal 3:16), and the dragon wars with "the remnant of her seed" (Rev 12:17).

also.meaning: Two uses: the promised Seed, singular, which is Messiah (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16), and the seed that is the word of Elohim sown in hearts (Luke 8:11), the incorruptible seed of the new birth (1 Pet 1:23).

words.meaning: The subtle serpent is the deceiver, "that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan" (Rev 12:9); yet the bronze serpent lifted up for healing pictures Messiah lifted up (Num 21:9; John 3:14).

also.meaning: Two uses: the subtle deceiver of Eden (Gen 3:1), the ancient serpent called the Devil (Rev 12:9); yet Messiah's disciples are to be wise as serpents (Matt 10:16), and the bronze serpent lifted up is a figure of Messiah (John 3:14).
The rod-become-serpent swallowing the magicians' serpents shows Yahuah's power over Egypt's serpent-power; the serpent pictures the adversary, the old serpent of Rev 12:9.

words.meaning: On the seventh day Yahuah finished His work, rested and sanctified it (Gen 2:2-3); seven marks what Yahuah completes and sets apart, the Sabbath rest that remains for His people (Heb 4:9), and the full sevens of Revelation.

also.meaning: Seven sprinklings, seven days of consecration, seven weeks and sevens of years (Lev 4:6; 8:33; 25:8) — Yahuah's completed count from creation's week; covenant breaking brings punishment "seven times" (Lev 26:18).

Completion of Yahuah's work and rest: the seventh day blessed and set apart (Gen 2:3); seven sevens to the jubilee (Lev 25:8); the seven assemblies, spirits, seals, trumpets and bowls of Revelation each mark a complete set (Rev 1:20).

lexicon.title: Seven Spirits (Seven Lamps and Seven Eyes)

words.meaning: The lights are set "for signs"; Scripture's signs are visible tokens of Yahuah's word and covenant: the bow (Gen 9:13), circumcision (Gen 17:11), the Sabbath (Exod 31:13), and the wonders in heaven (Rev 12:1).

Yahuah Himself clothes the man and woman with skins, a covering that cost a life; Scripture continues the picture with the garments of deliverance and robe of righteousness Yahuah puts on His people (Isa 61:10).

lexicon.title: Fig Leaves and Tunics of Skin

words.meaning: Stars picture Abraham's countless seed (Gen 15:5), Joseph's brothers (Gen 37:9-10), the coming ruler out of Jacob (Num 24:17), the wise who turn many (Dan 12:3), and the messengers of the assemblies (Rev 1:20).

also.meaning: Two uses: faithful ones who shine as stars (Dan 12:3), the seven stars that are the angels of the seven assemblies (Rev 1:20), the Star out of Jacob (Num 24:17); and wandering stars reserved for the blackness of darkness (Jude 13).
A star out of Jacob and a scepter out of Israel is the coming ruler; Yahushua is the bright and morning star, the light-bearer Yahuah raised (Rev 22:16).

The wise who turn many to righteousness shine "as the brightness of the firmament ... as the stars for ever" (Dan 12:3) — light-bearers reflecting Yahuah's light, as the righteous "shine forth as the sun" (Matt 13:43).

lexicon.title: Stars Falling and Sky Rolled Up

words.meaning: The greater light rules the day; in Joseph's dream Jacob reads the sun as the father of the house (Gen 37:10), Yahuah is called "a sun and shield" (Ps 84:11), and the woman is clothed with it (Rev 12:1).

also.meaning: At Joshua's word the sun stood still and the moon stayed until Israel had avenged itself (Josh 10:13), the lights serving Yahuah's battle; Judah's kings later gave horses to the sun (2 Kgs 23:11), worship Scripture condemns (Ezek 8:16).

lexicon.title: Sun Black as Sackcloth, Moon as Blood

words.meaning: The flaming sword bars the way to life; Scripture names the sword the word of Yahuah (Eph 6:17; Heb 4:12), which goes out of Messiah's mouth in judgment (Rev 1:16).

also.meaning: The word of Elohim: Messiah's mouth made like a sharp sword (Isa 49:2), the sword of the spirit which is the word (Eph 6:17), quick, powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword, discerning the heart (Heb 4:12).
The angel standing with drawn sword opposes the prophet who loved the wages of unrighteousness; Messiah fights Pergamos' Balaamites with the sword of His mouth (Rev 2:16).

The captain of Yahuah's host met Joshua with sword drawn (Josh 5:13), and the destroying messenger held a drawn sword over Jerusalem until it was sheathed at the altar (1 Chr 21:16, 27); the sword is Yahuah's word and judgment (Eph 6:17).
Covenant vengeance by invading armies - "a sword is sharpened, and also furbished" (Ezek 21:9); and Yahuah's word from the mouth of His Servant, "like a sharp sword" (Isa 49:2; Eph 6:17).

lexicon.title: Sharp Two-Edged Sword from His Mouth

words.meaning: Counterfeit grain sown by the enemy among the wheat: "the tares are the children of the wicked one" (Matt 13:38), the serpent's seed growing beside the woman's seed until the harvest separates them (Gen 3:15).

Thorns are the fruit of the cursed ground; Scripture uses them for enemies left in the land (Num 33:55), the cares that choke the word (Matt 13:22), and the crown pressed on Messiah, who bore the curse (Matt 27:29).

also.meaning: Thorns came with the curse (Gen 3:18) and mark the way of the froward and the field of the slothful (Prov 22:5; 24:31); they choke the sown word (Matt 13:7), and the cursed thorns were pressed on Messiah's head (John 19:2).

The fruit of the curse (Gen 3:18) - rebellious people around the prophet are briers and thorns (Ezek 2:6); thorns choke the word (Matt 13:7); in the restoration the fir tree replaces the thorn (Isa 55:13).

The fruit of the curse (Gen 3:18): thorns choke the word as cares and riches (Matt 13:22), land bearing thorns is near to cursing (Heb 6:8), and Messiah wore the curse as a crown of thorns (Matt 27:29).

words.meaning: The woman's sorrow in bearing becomes the picture of Zion laboring to bring forth (Isa 66:8; Mic 4:10), of sorrow that turns to joy (John 16:21), and of the woman crying in birth for the male child (Rev 12:2).

also.meaning: Zion's pangs that bring forth a nation at once (Isa 66:8); the distress before deliverance, whose sorrow turns to joy (Jer 30:6; John 16:21).

words.meaning: The tree of knowledge of good and evil is the one commandment of restraint in Eden; taking it pictures man seizing the right to decide good and evil for himself rather than receiving it from Yahuah (Gen 3:5).
The tree of life is access to endless life with Yahuah, barred after the fall (Gen 3:24); wisdom is "a tree of life" (Prov 3:18) and the overcomers regain it in the holy city (Rev 22:2, 14).
Scripture interprets the waters as "peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues" (Rev 17:15; Isa 17:12-13); restless water also pictures instability (Gen 49:4 "unstable as water").

also.meaning: Two uses: life and cleansing, the pouring of Yahuah's spirit like water on the thirsty (Isa 44:3; John 7:39), the washing of water by the word (Eph 5:26); and "the waters... are peoples, and multitudes" (Rev 17:15).
Water from the rock satisfies a thirsting people; Yahushua cries, if any man thirst let him come, speaking of the spirit Yahuah pours out (John 7:37-39; Isa 44:3).
The noise of the wings "like the noise of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty" (Ezek 1:24); Yahuah's glory from the east with "a voice like a noise of many waters" (Ezek 43:2).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: The cherubim kept the way of the tree of life (Gen 3:24); "ask for the old paths, where is the good way" (Jer 6:16); Messiah is the way (John 14:6), a new and living way, and the believers were called "the Way" (Acts 9:2).

also.meaning: There are two ways: Yahuah knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly perishes (Ps 1:6); a way may seem right yet end in death (Prov 14:12), and Israel is called back to the old paths, the good way (Jer 6:16).

words.meaning: The breath and power of Yahuah moving unseen: born of the spirit is like the wind blowing where it will (John 3:8), the rushing mighty wind at Shavuot (Acts 2:2); also unstable doctrine, "every wind of doctrine" (Eph 4:14).

also.meaning: The east wind brings judgment (locusts) and also deliverance (dividing the sea); the strong west wind carries the plague away, showing the winds as Yahuah's servants (Ps 104:4).
The four winds of heaven striving on the great sea are the forces Yahuah stirs among the nations, out of which the four kingdoms rise (Dan 7:2-3); held back in Rev 7:1.

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: The woman taken from man is his bride; Scripture uses the woman for Yahuah's covenant people, married to Him (Isa 54:5; Jer 3:14), bearing the promised seed (Rev 12:1-5), and finally the bride, the holy city (Rev 21:2).

Noah's first act after the flood is an altar; the fathers build altars wherever Yahuah appears (Gen 12:7), and Scripture keeps the altar as the place of offering and of the souls of the slain (Rev 6:9).

also.meaning: The place of offering and drawing near: reconciliation must come before the gift at the altar (Matt 5:23-24); "we have an altar" (Heb 13:10), and the souls of the slain witnesses lie under the altar (Rev 6:9).
An altar of earth or uncut stone, for a tool lifted on it pollutes it: man's workmanship adds nothing to what Yahuah provides (Exod 20:25).

The bronze altar at the court's entrance where blood was given "to make an atonement for your souls" (Lev 17:11); the first thing met on the way in, and the place under which slain souls cry out (Rev 6:9).

Elijah repaired Yahuah's broken-down altar with twelve stones 'according to the number of the tribes' (1 Kgs 18:31), restoring all Israel's worship; Jeroboam's rival altar at Bethel split and poured out its ashes as a sign against it (1 Kgs 13:5).

lexicon.title: Fire from the Altar Cast to the Earth

words.meaning: Mordecai was clothed in the king's apparel and led on the king's horse with the cry 'thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour' (Esth 6:11), as Joseph was arrayed before Pharaoh; Yahuah removes filthy garments and clothes His servant with change of raiment (Zech 3:4).

The ark carries the righteous through judgment; the same word is used for Moses' basket on the Nile (Exod 2:3), and Peter makes the ark and its eight souls a figure of immersion that saves (1 Pet 3:20-21).

also.meaning: The bulrush ark daubed with pitch carries the child through the waters of death, the same word as Noah's ark; deliverance comes through the waters in a vessel Yahuah preserves (Heb 11:23; 1 Pet 3:20).

The chest holding the tablets of the testimony, where Yahuah promised "there I will meet with thee" (Exod 25:22); it went before Israel to search out rest (Num 10:33) and is seen in the temple in heaven (Rev 11:19).
In restored Zion the ark is no longer sought, for "they shall call Jerusalem the throne of Yahuah" (Jer 3:16-17); the ark of His covenant is seen in the heavenly temple (Rev 11:19).

lexicon.title: Ark of the Covenant (Temple Opened in Heaven)
Ark and Eight Souls Through Water

words.meaning: The archers sorely grieved Joseph and shot at him; Scripture uses arrows for bitter words (Ps 64:3), Yahuah's chastening (Ps 38:2), children in a mighty man's hand (Ps 127:4), and the fiery darts of the wicked (Eph 6:16).

also.meaning: Yahuah's arrows are His judgments, spent upon the rebellious and made drunk with blood (Deut 32:23, 42).

Jonathan's arrows were the agreed sign, 'the arrows are beyond thee' meaning David must flee (1 Sam 20:22); Elisha's arrow out the window was 'the arrow of Yahuah's deliverance' (2 Kgs 13:17), and children are 'as arrows in the hand of a mighty man' (Ps 127:4).

Hostile, wounding attack: the wicked bend their bows to shoot bitter words as arrows (Ps 64:3); the believer's shield quenches the fiery darts of the wicked (Eph 6:16); children are arrows in a mighty man's hand (Ps 127:4).
"He made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me" (Isa 49:2) - the Servant kept hidden in Yahuah's hand until sent forth to the mark.

words.meaning: Mourning and repentance; Yahuah gives "beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning" (Isa 61:3); proud Tyre turned to ashes upon the earth (Ezek 28:18).

also.meaning: Heifer ashes mixed with running water made the water of purification for those defiled by death (Num 19:9,17); Yahuah gives "beauty for ashes" to mourners (Isa 61:3).
"Ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet" (Mal 4:3) — the burned-up end of the wicked, the serpent bruised under the saints' feet (Rom 16:20).

words.meaning: Issachar is "a strong ass couching down between two burdens," bowing his shoulder to bear; the firstling of an ass must be redeemed with a lamb (Exod 13:13), and the King comes riding on an ass (Zech 9:9).

also.meaning: The humble mount of Judah's king: binding his foal to the vine (Gen 49:11) and riding lowly on an ass (Zech 9:9) is fulfilled when Messiah enters Jerusalem on a colt (Matt 21:5).
The dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbade the madness of the prophet (2 Pet 2:16): a beast saw the angel the hireling seer could not.
"Thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass" (Zech 9:9) — Messiah's humble entry, fulfilled in Jerusalem (Matt 21:5).

lexicon.title: Colt the Foal of an Ass

words.meaning: Babel means confusion (Gen 11:9); Babylon becomes Scripture's name for man's proud world-system, "a golden cup... that made all the earth drunken" (Jer 51:7), Mystery Babylon the Great (Rev 17:5).

Babylon is the place of exile and the proud enemy of Zion: "O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us" (Ps 137:8), echoed in Revelation's "reward her even as she rewarded you" (Rev 18:6).

also.meaning: The proud city of confusion (Gen 11:9), "the glory of kingdoms" brought down like Sodom (Isa 13:19); Yahuah's golden cup that made the nations drunk (Jer 51:7) - the name of the great harlot (Rev 17:5).

words.meaning: "Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there?" (Jer 8:22) - the healing Yahuah provides, left unused by a people who will not be healed; Babylon cannot be healed with it (Jer 51:8-9).
"Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear" (Isa 54:1) - desolate Zion given more children than the married, as Sarah was; applied to Jerusalem above (Gal 4:27).

Joseph interprets the baker's three baskets as three days, ending in death (Gen 40:18); Scripture's baskets carry signs from Yahuah: Jeremiah's good and bad figs (Jer 24) and Amos' basket of summer fruit, "the end is come" (Amos 8:2).

also.meaning: Scripture interprets baskets: the baker's three baskets are three days (Gen 40:18), two baskets of figs are the two parts of Judah (Jer 24), the summer fruit basket is "the end" (Amos 8:2); leftover baskets show abundance remaining (Matt 14:20).

words.meaning: Bethel, "the house of Elohim," is where Yahuah meets Jacob; later Jeroboam sets a calf there and Hosea calls it Beth-aven, house of vanity (Hos 4:15), while the true house is His people (Heb 3:6).

lexicon.title: Temple of God (Naos) and Its Worshipers

words.meaning: 'House of bread': Rachel's burial place, home of Boaz, Ruth and David, from which Micah says the ruler in Israel shall come forth (Mic 5:2; Matt 2:6); the one born there called himself the bread of life (John 6:35).

also.meaning: Bethlehem, "house of bread," little among Judah's thousands, is where the ruler of Israel comes forth "whose goings forth have been from of old" (Mic 5:2, of His appointed line) — Yahushua's birthplace (Matt 2:6).

words.meaning: Two uses: fowls that snatch away the sown word are the wicked one (Matt 13:4, 19), as Abram drove the birds from the covenant pieces (Gen 15:11); fowls lodging in the tree picture nations sheltering under the kingdom (Ezek 17:23).

lexicon.title: Dwelling of Demons, Cage of Unclean Birds
Great Supper of Yahuah (Feast of the Birds)

words.meaning: Esau despises the birthright for one meal; Scripture warns against any "profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright" (Heb 12:16), and Reuben loses his to Joseph (1 Chr 5:1).

Abel's blood cries from the ground for justice; Scripture holds the life is in the blood and gives it on the altar to make atonement (Lev 17:11), and the souls of the slain cry "How long?" (Rev 6:10).

also.meaning: "The life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls" (Lev 17:11); without shedding of blood is no remission (Heb 9:22; Rev 12:11).
The Nile turned to blood strikes Egypt's life-source and repays the blood of the drowned sons; the bowls repeat it because they shed the blood of saints (Rev 16:6).
Life given on the altar for atonement (Lev 17:11); Yahuah said "Live" over the foundling in her blood (Ezek 16:6); bloodguilt required at the silent watchman's hand (Ezek 3:18; 33:6).

The life given for atonement: "the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar" (Lev 17:11); without shedding of blood is no remission (Heb 9:22); overcomers prevail by the blood of the Lamb (Rev 12:11).

lexicon.title: Bread and Wine of the Covenant Meal

words.meaning: Hagar the bondwoman and Sarah the freewoman are, Paul writes, an allegory of two covenants: the bondwoman's son born after the flesh, the freewoman's by promise (Gal 4:24-31).

Jacob makes booths at Succoth; Yahuah commands Israel to dwell in booths at Sukkot to remember the wilderness (Lev 23:42-43), and promises to raise up "the tabernacle (sukkah) of David that is fallen" (Amos 9:11).

also.meaning: Seven days dwelling in booths "that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths" (Lev 23:43); the tabernacle of David rebuilt (Amos 9:11) and the Word dwelling among men (John 1:14) answer it.

Israel dwelt in booths of olive, pine, myrtle and palm branches to remember that Yahuah made them dwell in booths out of Egypt (Lev 23:43); the returned remnant kept Sukkot as not since Joshua (Neh 8:17), and the nations will come up to keep it (Zech 14:16).

Israel dwelt in booths at Sukkot to remember Yahuah's sheltering in the wilderness (Lev 23:43); the Word dwelt (tabernacled) among men (John 1:14), the fallen booth of David is raised (Acts 15:16), and Yahuah's tabernacle is with men (Rev 21:3).

words.meaning: The bow in the cloud is the token of the covenant never to flood the earth again (Gen 9:13); it circles Yahuah's throne (Ezek 1:28; Rev 4:3), while the warrior's bow pictures conquest (Gen 49:24; Rev 6:2).

also.meaning: Two uses: the bow set in the cloud as covenant token of mercy (Gen 9:13), and the bow of war and judgment Yahuah bends (Ps 7:12; Hab 3:9), carried by the rider on the white horse (Rev 6:2).
"They are like a deceitful bow" (Hos 7:16) that will not shoot straight — a people whose turning misses the mark (Ps 78:57).

words.meaning: Joseph interprets the three branches of the vine as three days (Gen 40:12); Joseph himself is "a fruitful bough... whose branches run over the wall" (Gen 49:22), and disciples are branches in the vine (John 15:5).

also.meaning: Six branches going out of the one shaft of the lampstand, all drawing from it (Exod 25:32); Yahushua uses the image of branches abiding in the vine and bearing fruit (John 15:5).
The righteous Branch raised to David who reigns and executes judgment (Jer 23:5) - Messiah, the Netzer of Isa 11:1, whose dwelling at Nazareth fulfilled the prophets (Matt 2:23).

Two uses: Messiah the Branch raised to David (Isa 11:1; Jer 23:5); and believers as branches in the vine, which bear fruit by abiding or are cast forth and burned (John 15:5-6), natural and grafted alike (Rom 11:17-21).

words.meaning: Yahuah rains brimstone and fire on Sodom; Scripture makes it the standing picture of His final judgment on the wicked (Ps 11:6; Luke 17:29-30) and the lake of fire (Rev 20:10).

also.meaning: The land of the apostate becomes brimstone, salt and burning like Sodom; brimstone is Yahuah's fire of judgment (Rev 14:10).

lexicon.title: Lake of Fire and the Second Death

words.meaning: Issachar bows under two burdens and becomes a servant unto tribute; Scripture contrasts the heavy burdens men bind (Matt 23:4) with Messiah's light burden (Matt 11:30) and "cast thy burden upon Yahuah" (Ps 55:22).

The offering wholly given to Yahuah, ascending as "a sweet savour" (Lev 1:9); a broken spirit is what He desires with it (Ps 51:17), and believers present their bodies "a living sacrifice" (Rom 12:1).
Covenant cut by passing between the parts (Gen 15:10, 17); the princes who broke the release of servants become as the calf they cut in two (Jer 34:18-20).

also.meaning: The molten calf is worship of Yahuah's name through a made image ("a feast to Yahuah", Exod 32:5); they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox (Ps 106:20).

The molten calf proclaimed with "a feast to Yahuah" (Exod 32:5) — Yahuah's name put on an idol; Jeroboam repeated it (1 Kgs 12:28), and Stephen names it the turning point of Israel's idolatry (Acts 7:41).

The sin offering for the priest (Lev 9:2) whose blood Messiah's surpasses (Heb 9:12); the fatted calf is the Father's feast for the returning son (Luke 15:23), and the "calves of our lips" are offered praise (Hos 14:2; Heb 13:15).

words.meaning: Circumcision is "a token of the covenant" in the flesh (Gen 17:11); Moses and the prophets already call for circumcision of the heart to love Yahuah (Deut 30:6), which Paul names the true circumcision (Rom 2:29).

also.meaning: The covenant sign in the flesh (Gen 17:11) always pointed to the heart: "circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart" (Deut 10:16), which Yahuah Himself performs (Deut 30:6), circumcision of the heart in the spirit (Rom 2:29).

"Circumcise yourselves to Yahuah, and take away the foreskins of your heart" (Jer 4:4) - the inward covenant sign the outward one always called for; none uncircumcised in heart enter His sanctuary (Ezek 44:9).

words.meaning: Cain builds the first city and Babel builds another; Scripture sets man's city against the city "whose builder and maker is Elohim" (Heb 11:10), the great city Babylon against the holy city New Jerusalem.

also.meaning: The city of Elohim made glad by the river (Ps 46:4): Abraham sought a city with foundations (Heb 11:10), believers are come to the city of the living Elohim (Heb 12:22), and the holy city, new Jerusalem, is the bride (Rev 21:2).

lexicon.title: The Great City (Spiritually Sodom and Egypt)

words.meaning: The cloud carries the bow of the covenant and later Yahuah's presence leading Israel (Exod 13:21); the Son of man comes with the clouds of heaven (Dan 7:13; Rev 1:7).

also.meaning: The cloud on the tabernacle by day and fire by night; "at the commandment of Yahuah they rested, and at the commandment of Yahuah they journeyed" (Num 9:18-23) — guidance and presence.
Yahuah "rideth upon a swift cloud" into Egypt for judgment (Isa 19:1); the cloud of His glory filling the inner court (Ezek 10:4).

Clouds and wind without rain picture empty boasting (Prov 25:14); false teachers are clouds without water carried about of winds (Jude 12), whereas the bright cloud overshadowed Messiah with the Father's voice (Matt 17:5).

lexicon.title: Pillar of Cloud and Fire Reused

words.meaning: Joseph's coat marks the beloved son set over his brothers; it is stripped and dipped in blood and brought to the father (Gen 37:31), as the rider is "clothed with a vesture dipped in blood" (Rev 19:13).

also.meaning: The priest's linen tunic "for glory and for beauty" (Exod 28:40), echoing the coats of skin Yahuah made to cover Adam (Gen 3:21); Messiah's seamless coat was divided by lot (John 19:23).

lexicon.title: Fig Leaves and Tunics of Skin

words.meaning: Corn and wine are the blessing of the land (Gen 27:28) and the life stored in Joseph's hand in famine; a corn of wheat must die to bear much fruit (John 12:24).

lexicon.title: Grain of Wheat Falling into the Ground

words.meaning: Pharaoh's cup is restored to the butler's hand; Scripture's cup is a portion given by Yahuah, "the cup of salvation" (Ps 116:13) or "the wine cup of this fury" (Jer 25:15), and the covenant cup (Matt 26:27).

also.meaning: A cup is a person's appointed portion: the righteous drink the cup of deliverance that runs over (Ps 23:5; 116:13), the wicked drain the cup of Yahuah's wrath (Ps 75:8; Rev 14:10), and Messiah accepted the cup given Him (Matt 26:39).
The cup of Yahuah's fury drunk to the dregs by the nations (Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15); Babylon was a golden cup in His hand that made the earth drunk (Jer 51:7).

A portion appointed by Yahuah: the cup of deliverance and blessing (Ps 116:13; 1 Cor 10:16), the wine cup of His fury given to the nations (Jer 25:15), and the cup of suffering Messiah accepted (Matt 26:39).

lexicon.title: Bread and Wine of the Covenant Meal

words.meaning: "The dew of heaven" is Isaac's blessing; Moses says "my speech shall distil as the dew" (Deut 32:2), and Yahuah promises "I will be as the dew unto Israel" (Hos 14:5).

also.meaning: Yahuah's blessing and teaching coming down quietly: 'my speech shall distil as the dew' (Deut 32:2), 'I will be as the dew unto Israel' (Hos 14:5); dew withheld is a curse (2 Sam 1:21; 1 Kgs 17:1).
Yahuah's life-giving blessing; "thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead" (Isa 26:19) - resurrection; the remnant is as dew among many peoples (Mic 5:7).
Moses' doctrine distills as the dew; Yahuah will be as the dew unto Israel (Hos 14:5), the quiet blessing on Zion (Ps 133:3).

Dew is short-lived goodness (Hos 6:4), but Yahuah says "I will be as the dew unto Israel" (Hos 14:5) — His quiet, life-giving word (Deut 32:2), and the remnant as dew from Yahuah among peoples (Mic 5:7).

words.meaning: The clean dove finds no rest until the waters abate and returns with the olive leaf; Scripture uses the dove for innocence (Matt 10:16), the beloved bride (Song 2:14), a silly Ephraim (Hos 7:11), and Yahuah's spirit resting on Messiah (Matt 3:16).

also.meaning: The dove is gentle, innocent and longs for rest (Gen 8:9; Ps 55:6; Matt 10:16); in the Song the beloved bride is "my dove, my undefiled," hidden in the clefts of the rock (Song 2:14; 5:2).

The harmless messenger of rest after judgment (Gen 8:11) and the poor man's offering (Lev 12:8; Luke 2:24); the spirit descends like a dove on Messiah (Matt 3:16), and disciples are to be harmless as doves (Matt 10:16), unlike silly Ephraim (Hos 7:11).

"Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart" (Hos 7:11), flitting between Egypt and Assyria; restored, they come "as a dove out of the land of Assyria" (Hos 11:11); the dove at the immersion marks Yahuah's anointing.

words.meaning: Yahuah speaks to the fathers and Joseph through dreams: "I will speak unto him in a dream" (Num 12:6); the interpretation belongs to Elohim (Gen 40:8), and He pours out His spirit so that old men dream dreams (Joel 2:28).
Wine poured out with the daily lambs "in the holy place" (Num 28:7); Paul calls his own life "poured out" (spendomai) on the sacrifice and service of belief (Phil 2:17; 2 Tim 4:6).

also.meaning: Wine poured out with the sacrifices (Num 15:5-10); Paul counts his own life as poured out upon the sacrifice and service of belief, "I am now ready to be offered" (Phil 2:17; 2 Tim 4:6).

words.meaning: The pledge given as surety for full payment, as Judah's signet, bracelets and staff (Gen 38:18); Yahuah gives the earnest of the spirit in hearts as the down payment of the inheritance until the redemption (2 Cor 1:22; Eph 1:14).
The seven full and seven thin ears are interpreted as years: "the seven good ears are seven years" (Gen 41:26); the ear grows to the full corn as the kingdom grows (Mark 4:28).

also.meaning: The servant's bored ear marked lifelong willing service (Exod 21:6); "mine ears hast thou opened" (Ps 40:6) is the obedient Servant who delights to do Yahuah's will (Ps 40:8; Isa 50:5).

Hearing as obedience: the bored ear of the willing servant (Exod 21:6), "mine ears hast thou opened" (Ps 40:6); "he that hath an ear, let him hear what the spirit saith unto the assemblies" (Rev 2:7), while dull ears mark hardening (Isa 6:10).
As a shepherd snatches two legs or a piece of an ear from the lion, so a scrap of Israel is taken out (Amos 3:12) — a pitiful remnant, proof of what was devoured.

words.meaning: The east wind blasts the thin ears; Scripture uses it as Yahuah's instrument of judgment and deliverance: it brings the locusts, parts the sea (Exod 14:21), and withers proud Ephraim (Hos 13:15).

also.meaning: The vehement east wind "prepared" to scorch Jonah is Yahuah's withering wind, the scorching blast of judgment (Hos 13:15) that also parted the sea (Exod 14:21).

words.meaning: Egypt is first a refuge in famine and then "the house of bondage" (Exod 20:2); Scripture uses it for the world of slavery Yahuah calls His son out of (Hos 11:1) and for the great city spiritually called Sodom and Egypt (Rev 11:8).

lexicon.title: The Great City (Spiritually Sodom and Egypt)
Out of Egypt Called My Son

words.meaning: Eight souls are carried through the waters (1 Pet 3:20), the covenant sign is cut on the eighth day (Gen 17:12), and the eighth day closes Sukkot as Shemini Atzeret (Lev 23:36).

lexicon.title: Ark and Eight Souls Through Water

words.meaning: Circumcision, priestly service, the leper's restoration and Shemini Atzeret all fall on the eighth day (Lev 9:1; 14:10; 23:36) — after a completed seven, a new beginning before Yahuah.
Jacob names the place Peniel, the face of El, after striving with the messenger (Hos 12:4); Yahuah's face shining is His blessing (Num 6:25), and His servants "shall see his face" (Rev 22:4).

also.meaning: "Yahuah make his face shine upon thee" (Num 6:25); Moses spoke face to face yet no man may see His face and live (Exod 33:20), his own face shone from it (Exod 34:29), and the redeemed "shall see his face" (Rev 22:4).
Moses' face shone from speaking with Yahuah, and he veiled it; believers with unveiled face behold and are changed into the same image (2 Cor 3:18).

Each creature has the face of a man, lion, ox and eagle (Ezek 1:10) - Scripture does not decode the four; elsewhere it uses lion for royal strength, ox for service, eagle for Yahuah's swift bearing; Ezek 10:14 gives a cherub's face for the ox.

words.meaning: Famine drives the fathers to Egypt and exalts Joseph; Yahuah sends "a famine... not a famine of bread... but of hearing the words of Yahuah" (Amos 8:11), and famine rides with the black and pale horses.
Cain slays Abel in the field, and Abraham buys a field as pledge of the land; Messiah interprets: "the field is the world" (Matt 13:38), and the kingdom is treasure hid in a field (Matt 13:44).

also.meaning: "The field is the world" (Matt 13:38), where the treasure is hidden and bought (Matt 13:44); believers are Elohim's husbandry (1 Cor 3:9); purchased fields signal hope in Yahuah's promise (Gen 23; Jer 32:9).
Jeremiah redeems his kinsman's field while Babylon besieges the city - the right of redemption made a pledge that "houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again" (Jer 32:15).

words.meaning: Genesis repeatedly passes over the natural firstborn for the younger; Yahuah calls Israel "my firstborn" (Exod 4:22), says of David's seed "I will make him my firstborn" (Ps 89:27), and Messiah is firstborn from the dead (Col 1:18).

also.meaning: Israel is Yahuah's firstborn son, so Egypt's firstborn die; the firstborn belongs to Yahuah and is redeemed, fulfilled in Messiah the firstborn from the dead and the assembly of the firstborn (Heb 12:23).
Every firstborn belonged to Yahuah since Egypt and was redeemed; the Levites were taken in their place (Num 3:12-13), and the assembly is "the church of the firstborn" (Heb 12:23).
"I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn" (Jer 31:9) - the place of inheritance Yahuah grants, often passing over the elder (Gen 48:14); Messiah the firstborn from the dead (Col 1:18).

words.meaning: Abel brings the firstlings of his flock, a blood offering Yahuah accepts (Heb 11:4); the firstling belongs to Yahuah (Exod 13:2) and pictures the offering whose blood "speaketh better things than that of Abel" (Heb 12:24).

The flood is Yahuah's judgment that sweeps away the ungodly (2 Pet 2:5) and the pattern of the end (Matt 24:39); the enemy comes in "like a flood" (Isa 59:19), as the serpent's flood after the woman (Rev 12:15).
Judah binds his foal unto the vine; Zechariah's king comes "lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass" (Zech 9:9), fulfilled when Yahushua rides into Jerusalem (Matt 21:5).

lexicon.title: Colt the Foal of an Ass

words.meaning: Forty days of rain begin a pattern Scripture repeats for testing and judgment: forty years in the wilderness "to prove thee" (Deut 8:2), Nineveh's forty days (Jonah 3:4), Messiah's forty days of temptation (Matt 4:2).

also.meaning: A set period of testing and preparation: forty days of rain (Gen 7:12), forty years in the wilderness, a year for each day (Num 14:34), forty days of Messiah's fast (Matt 4:2), and forty days of his showing himself alive (Acts 1:3).
Forty days of spying became forty years of wandering, each day for a year; forty marks the full time of testing (Deut 8:2; Matt 4:2).
Bearing iniquity forty days, "each day for a year" (Ezek 4:6; Num 14:34) - the measure of trial and judgment, as in the wilderness years.

words.meaning: A smoking furnace passes between the pieces; Scripture calls Egypt "the iron furnace" (Deut 4:20), Yahuah tests His people in "the furnace of affliction" (Isa 48:10), and the day comes "burning as an oven" (Mal 4:1).

also.meaning: Egypt was the iron furnace from which Yahuah took Israel (Deut 4:20); "I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction" (Isa 48:10) - trial that refines or consumes.
Two uses: the furnace of affliction that refines (Egypt the iron furnace, Deut 4:20; Isa 48:10), and the furnace of fire into which the angels cast the wicked at the end of the age (Matt 13:42, 50).

The furnace is the persecution that tests Yahuah's servants for refusing the image; Israel's deliverance from "the iron furnace" (Deut 4:20) and "the furnace of affliction" (Isa 48:10) show it as the place where He walks with and refines His own.

words.meaning: The gate is the seat of authority and judgment: elders sat in it (Ruth 4:1-11), and to 'possess the gate of his enemies' is to rule over them (Gen 22:17); Samson carried off Gaza's gates (Judg 16:3), and the gates of hades shall not prevail (Matt 16:18).

also.meaning: Gates are the place of entry, judgment and rule: "this gate of Yahuah, into which the righteous shall enter" (Ps 118:20); the gates of death and the gates of Zion stand opposite (Ps 9:13-14), and the holy city has twelve gates (Rev 21:12).
The words of Yahuah written on the doorposts and gates claim house and city for His law; blessed are they that do His commandments, to enter by the gates into the city (Rev 22:14).

The single embroidered entrance on the east of the court (Exod 27:16), the one way in; "enter into his gates with thanksgiving" (Ps 100:4), and Yahushua calls himself the door of the sheep (John 10:9).

"This gate of Yahuah, into which the righteous shall enter" (Ps 118:20): the strait gate leads to life and few find it (Matt 7:14); those who do His commandments enter in through the gates into the city (Rev 22:14).
Twelve city gates named after the tribes of Israel, three on each side (Ezek 48:31-34) - entry into Yahuah's city through Israel, as in New Jerusalem (Rev 21:12).

words.meaning: The goat is part of the covenant offering and of the Yom Kippur pair (Lev 16); kids' skins and blood serve deceit in Jacob's house (Gen 27:16; 37:31), the he-goat is Greece (Dan 8:21), and goats stand on the left at judgment (Matt 25:33).

also.meaning: The Yom Kippur goats bear away and atone for sin (Lev 16:21-22), yet their blood could not finally take sin away (Heb 10:4); at the judgment the goats are set on the left (Matt 25:33).

words.meaning: Judah washes his clothes "in the blood of grapes"; Scripture joins wine and blood in the covenant cup (Matt 26:28) and in the winepress of wrath where Yahuah treads the grapes of the earth (Isa 63:3; Rev 14:19-20).

also.meaning: The cluster carried on a staff between two is the proof of the good land Yahuah promised; Isaiah's cluster with new wine in it is the preserved remnant (Isa 65:8).

Fruit showing the vine's nature: Eshcol's cluster showed the land's goodness (Num 13:23), Israel brought forth wild grapes (Isa 5:4), men do not gather grapes of thorns (Matt 7:16), and the earth's ripe grapes go to the winepress (Rev 14:18).
"I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness" (Hos 9:10) — Yahuah's delight in His people at first, before they went to Baal-peor.

lexicon.title: Blood to the Horses' Bridles (1,600 Stadia)
Vine of the Earth and the Winepress

words.meaning: The hoary head is a crown of glory if found in the way of righteousness (Prov 16:31; 20:29); the Ancient of Days has hair like pure wool (Dan 7:9), seen again on the glorified Son of man (Rev 1:14).

also.meaning: "Gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not" (Hos 7:9) — decline and decay spreading unnoticed in a nation drained by strangers.

words.meaning: The heifer is among the beasts divided for the covenant; Scripture later uses the heifer for cleansing from death (Num 19; Heb 9:13) and for nations and tribes: Egypt "a very fair heifer," Ephraim a taught heifer (Hos 10:11).

also.meaning: Ephraim is "an heifer that is taught, and loveth to tread out the corn" (Hos 10:11) — easy work and unmuzzled eating; Yahuah puts the yoke on to plow, and Israel "slideth back as a backsliding heifer" (Hos 4:16).

words.meaning: Naphtali is "a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words"; Yahuah makes His servant's feet like hinds' feet to stand on high places (Ps 18:33; Hab 3:19), and the hart panting for water is the soul thirsting for Elohim (Ps 42:1).

The ram is caught by its horns; Scripture interprets horns as power and rulers: "the ten horns... are ten kings" (Dan 7:24), Yahuah is "the horn of my salvation" (Ps 18:2), and the Lamb has seven horns (Rev 5:6).

also.meaning: Four corner projections daubed with atoning blood (Lev 4:7); horn is Scripture's word for strength, the altar's horns were grasped for refuge (1 Kgs 1:50), and Judah's sin is graven on them (Jer 17:1).

Strength and kingship: Hannah's horn exalted in Yahuah, who 'shall exalt the horn of his anointed' (1 Sam 2:10); David was anointed from a horn of oil, Yahuah makes the horn of David to bud (Ps 132:17; Luke 1:69), and Zedekiah's iron horns were a false sign (1 Kgs 22:11).

A horn is strength and kingly power: Yahuah exalts the horn of His anointed (1 Sam 2:10) and makes the horn of David to bud (Ps 132:17), the "horn of deliverance" raised in the house of David (Luke 1:69); He cuts off the horns of the wicked (Ps 75:10).
A horn is a king or ruling power: "the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise" (Dan 7:24); the ram's horns "are the kings of Media and Persia" (Dan 8:20).

lexicon.title: Voice from the Horns of the Altar

words.meaning: Dan's adder bites the horse so the rider falls backward; Scripture warns "an horse is a vain thing for safety" (Ps 33:17) and interprets Zechariah's horses as Yahuah's agents walking to and fro through the earth (Zech 1:10; 6:5).

also.meaning: The horse and his rider thrown into the sea show that a horse is a vain thing for safety (Ps 33:17); the horse is warfare and power, given to the true rider in Rev 19.

words.meaning: Yahuah's blessing on sown seed: Isaac reaped a hundredfold because Yahuah blessed him (Gen 26:12); the good-ground hearer who understands the word brings forth thirty, sixty, a hundredfold (Matt 13:23).

Jacob is renamed Israel, one who strives and prevails with El; Scripture applies the name to Yahuah's servant (Isa 49:3) and teaches "they are not all Israel, which are of Israel" (Rom 9:6), the Israel of Elohim (Gal 6:16).
Pharaoh's seven fat and seven lean kine are interpreted by Scripture itself: "the seven good kine are seven years" of plenty and the lean ones seven years of famine (Gen 41:26-27).

Jacob's ladder joins earth to heaven with messengers ascending and descending; Messiah applies it to Himself: "ye shall see heaven open, and the angels... ascending and descending upon the Son of man" (John 1:51).
Isaac asks "where is the lamb?" and Abraham answers "Elohim will provide himself a lamb" (Gen 22:8); Yahuah provides the Pesach lamb and at last His own Son, "the Lamb of Elohim" (John 1:29).

also.meaning: A lamb without blemish offered every morning and evening (Exod 29:38-39); "Elohim will provide himself a lamb" (Gen 22:8), and Yahushua is "the Lamb of Elohim, which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29).
The offering Yahuah Himself provides (Gen 22:8): the Pesach lamb without blemish (Exod 12:5) points to Messiah, the Lamb of Elohim (John 1:29), whose precious blood redeems (1 Pet 1:19).
The unblemished lamb of Pesach, whose blood shields the house, is Yahuah's provision; Messiah is the Lamb that Yahuah provided, our Pesach sacrificed (1 Cor 5:7; 1 Pet 1:19).

"Brought as a lamb to the slaughter" (Isa 53:7) - the Servant offered as the Pesach lamb; Jeremiah also was "like a lamb or an ox brought to the slaughter" (Jer 11:19); the Lamb as though slain (Rev 5:6).

words.meaning: Joseph is arrayed in fine linen when raised to rule; Scripture interprets it: "the fine linen is the righteousness of saints" (Rev 19:8), and the priests minister in linen (Ezek 44:17).

also.meaning: Fine twined linen of curtains, court and priestly garments, and plain linen for Yom Kippur (Lev 16:4); Scripture interprets it: "the fine linen is the righteousness of saints" (Rev 19:8).

The holy garment of the high priest's Yom Kippur service (Lev 16:4) - worn by the heavenly scribe who marks and scatters coals (Ezek 9:2; 10:2) and by priests in the inner court (44:17); "fine linen is the righteousness of saints" (Rev 19:8).
The holy linen garments of the Yom Kippur high priest (Lev 16:4); Messiah's linen grave clothes left lying show the body risen (John 20:5-7), and fine linen is the righteousness of saints (Rev 19:8).

The man clothed in linen is Yahuah's heavenly messenger in priestly dress (Lev 16:4), the one who marks the faithful (Ezek 9:2) and swears by Him that lives forever (Dan 12:7); linen is righteousness (Rev 19:8).

lexicon.title: Seven Angels in White Linen with Golden Sashes

words.meaning: Judah is a lion's whelp who couches and none dares rouse him; Messiah is "the Lion of the tribe of Juda" (Rev 5:5), Yahuah roars as a lion in judgment (Hos 5:14), and the adversary walks about as a roaring lion (1 Pet 5:8).

also.meaning: The lion is both the Messiah from Judah (Gen 49:9; Rev 5:5) and the adversary and persecutor who tears the soul (Ps 7:2; 22:13; 1 Pet 5:8); the righteous are bold as a lion (Prov 28:1).

Judah's royal strength (Gen 49:9) - Judah's mother a lioness, her princes young lions caught in pits (Ezek 19); Babylon the lion from the thicket (Jer 4:7); the Lion of Judah, and the adversary as a roaring lion (1 Pet 5:8).

Two uses: Judah's lion, fulfilled in Messiah the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Gen 49:9; Rev 5:5); and the devouring adversary, who walks about as a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour (1 Pet 5:8; Ezek 22:25).
Israel rising as a lion and couching as a lion that none dare stir is Balaam's blessing; it echoes Judah's lion and points to the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:5).

The first beast, a lion with eagle's wings, is Babylon (Jer 4:7; 50:17); the plucked wings and man's heart recall Nebuchadnezzar humbled (Dan 4); elsewhere the lion is Messiah of Judah (Rev 5:5) and the devouring adversary (1 Pet 5:8).

lexicon.title: Lion of the Tribe of Judah

words.meaning: Yahuah sets a mark on Cain to spare him; Scripture's marks identify who belongs to whom: the mark on the foreheads of those who sigh (Ezek 9:4), Yahuah's seal (Rev 7:3), and the counterfeit mark of the beast (Rev 13:16).

also.meaning: "Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations" (Ezek 9:4) - the sign that spares Yahuah's grieving faithful from the slaughter (9:6; Rev 7:3).

words.meaning: Melchizedek, king of righteousness and king of Salem, brings bread and wine and receives the tithe; Scripture makes him the pattern of Messiah's everlasting priesthood "after the order of Melchizedek" (Ps 110:4; Heb 7).

also.meaning: Yahuah swears to Messiah, "Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek" (Ps 110:4): king of righteousness and peace who brought bread and wine, a priesthood older than Levi (Heb 7).

words.meaning: Judah's teeth are white with milk, the abundance of a land "flowing with milk and honey" (Exod 3:8); Scripture uses milk for the first nourishment of the word: "desire the sincere milk of the word" (1 Pet 2:2).

also.meaning: Plenty of the promised land (Exod 3:8), offered freely "without money and without price" (Isa 55:1); the first word for newborn believers (1 Pet 2:2).
The land flowing with milk (Exod 3:8); first nourishment of the word for babes, "desire the sincere milk of the word" (1 Pet 2:2), though those who should be teachers still need milk (Heb 5:12).

words.meaning: On Moriah Abraham offers his only son and names the place "in the mount of Yahuah it shall be seen" (Gen 22:14); Solomon later builds the house of Yahuah on mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1).

also.meaning: Where Abraham offered Isaac and named the place Yahuah-jireh, 'in the mount of Yahuah it shall be seen' (Gen 22:14); Solomon built the house of Yahuah 'in mount Moriah', on Ornan's threshing floor where the plague was stayed (2 Chr 3:1).

words.meaning: Babel says "let us make us a name"; Yahuah instead gives Abraham a great name (Gen 12:2) and renames the fathers, and the overcomers bear the Father's name on their foreheads (Rev 14:1).

also.meaning: In the priestly blessing "they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them" (Num 6:24-27); the overcomers bear the Father's name (Rev 14:1; 22:4).

words.meaning: Jacob pours oil on the pillar to set it apart; Scripture uses oil for anointing kings and priests with Yahuah's spirit (1 Sam 16:13), Messiah anointed by Yahuah (Acts 10:38), and the oil the wise virgins keep (Matt 25:4).

also.meaning: Pure beaten olive oil that keeps the lamps burning "continually" (Lev 24:2); Zechariah shows the oil-fed lamp as "not by might... but by my spirit" (Zech 4:6), and Yahuah anointed Yahushua "with the holy spirit and with power" (Acts 10:38).

Kings were made 'anointed' by oil from a horn, and 'the spirit of Yahuah came upon David from that day forward' (1 Sam 16:13); the oil pictures Yahuah's own spirit poured on His chosen, as Elohim anointed Yahushua with holy spirit and power (Acts 10:38).

Anointing oil marks the one Yahuah sets apart (Exod 29:7; Ps 89:20); His Anointed is anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows (Ps 45:7), and oil running down Aaron's beard pictures brethren dwelling in unity (Ps 133:2).

The anointing of Yahuah's spirit and power: David anointed and the spirit came upon him (1 Sam 16:13; Isa 61:1); the wise virgins carry oil (Matt 25:4), and believers have an anointing from the Holy One (1 John 2:20).

words.meaning: The olive leaf announces life after judgment; Yahuah called Israel "a green olive tree" (Jer 11:16), the nations are grafted into it (Rom 11:17), and the two olive trees are the anointed witnesses (Zech 4:14; Rev 11:4).

also.meaning: The olive leaf announces judgment ended (Gen 8:11); Yahuah called Israel's name "a green olive tree" (Jer 11:16), into which wild branches are grafted (Rom 11:17), and the two olive trees are the two witnesses (Rev 11:4).
Israel's beauty shall be "as the olive tree" (Hos 14:6), the green olive of Jer 11:16 into which the nations are grafted (Rom 11:17).

words.meaning: Jacob sets up a stone pillar as a memorial of Yahuah's meeting; Scripture calls faithful elders pillars (Gal 2:9), the assembly "the pillar and ground of the truth" (1 Tim 3:15), and the overcomer a pillar in the temple (Rev 3:12).

also.meaning: Jeremiah made "a defenced city, and an iron pillar, and brasen walls" against the land (Jer 1:18) - one Yahuah makes immovable; pillars in the assembly and in Elohim's temple (Gal 2:9; Rev 3:12).
The pillar of cloud by day and fire by night is Yahuah's presence leading His people; it is darkness to Egypt and light to Israel (Exod 14:20), promised again over Zion (Isa 4:5).
Twelve pillars by the altar stand for the twelve tribes entering the covenant; the overcomer is made a pillar in the temple of Elohim (Rev 3:12).

Pillars bearing veil and court hangings (Exod 26:32; 27:10); faithful men are called pillars (Gal 2:9), the assembly is "the pillar and ground of the truth" (1 Tim 3:15), and the overcomer is made a pillar in the temple (Rev 3:12).

Samson pulled down the two middle pillars of Dagon's house and slew more at his death than in his life (Judg 16:30); Absalom raised a pillar to keep his name, having no son (2 Sam 18:18), but Yahuah gives 'a place and a name better than of sons' (Isa 56:5) and makes the overcomer a pillar (Rev 3:12).

The bearing supports of Yahuah's house, Jachin and Boaz (1 Kgs 7:21): James, Cephas and John seemed to be pillars (Gal 2:9), the assembly is the pillar and ground of the truth (1 Tim 3:15), and the overcomer is made a pillar (Rev 3:12).

lexicon.title: Pillar of Cloud and Fire Reused

words.meaning: Joseph is cast into a pit "empty, there was no water in it"; Scripture uses the pit for death and the grave (Ps 88:4) and for the prison from which Yahuah frees captives "out of the pit wherein is no water" by the blood of the covenant (Zech 9:11).

also.meaning: The pit is the grave and the place of death (Ps 28:1); the wicked fall into the pit they dig (Ps 7:15; Prov 26:27), and Yahuah draws His own up out of the horrible pit (Ps 40:2; Zech 9:11).

Joseph and Jeremiah cast into the pit and drawn up (Gen 37:24; Jer 38:6, 13) - deep affliction and the place of death; prisoners loosed from the waterless pit by the blood of the covenant (Zech 9:11).
The earth opening her mouth to swallow Korah's company shows rebellion against Yahuah's appointed order going down alive into the pit; Jude names the gainsaying of Korah.

words.meaning: The pitcher broken at the fountain is the clay body shattered at death (Eccl 12:6-7); Gideon's broken pitchers released the light hidden in them (Judg 7:20), and the sons of Zion are counted as earthen pitchers (Lam 4:2).

also.meaning: The sign that leads to the appointed place, as with Rebekah (Gen 24:14) and the man bearing a pitcher to the Pesach room (Mark 14:13); Gideon's broken pitchers released hidden lamps, an earthen vessel holding light (Judg 7:20; 2 Cor 4:7).

Gideon's men hid lamps inside empty pitchers and broke them so the light shone out (Judg 7:20); Paul uses the same picture of the light of Yahuah's glory held as 'treasure in earthen vessels' (2 Cor 4:7).

words.meaning: "I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward" (Gen 15:1): Paul presses toward the mark for the prize of the high calling (Phil 3:14), warned not to be beguiled of the reward (Col 2:18); Messiah's reward is with him (Rev 22:12).

"As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud... This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahuah" (Ezek 1:28) - covenant mercy surrounding the throne of judgment (Gen 9:13; Rev 4:3).

The ram is cut for Abram's covenant and given in Isaac's place (Gen 22:13); it is the ram of consecration for priests (Lev 8:22), and in vision Scripture interprets the two-horned ram as "the kings of Media and Persia" (Dan 8:20).

also.meaning: The ram caught in the thicket offered "in the stead of" Isaac (Gen 22:13); rams served for burnt, trespass and "ram of consecration" offerings that filled the priests' hands (Exod 29:22; Lev 8:22).
"The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia" (Dan 8:20), the higher horn coming up last — Persia over Media.

words.meaning: The unclean raven goes to and fro and never returns to the ark (Lev 11:15); yet Yahuah feeds the ravens (Luke 12:24) and used them to feed Elijah, showing His care for all He made.

also.meaning: Unclean birds Yahuah commanded to bring Elijah bread and flesh morning and evening by the brook (1 Kgs 17:6); Scripture uses them for Yahuah's care of the helpless: 'Consider the ravens... and Elohim feedeth them' (Luke 12:24).
An unclean bird Yahuah nonetheless feeds (Job 38:41; Ps 147:9) and uses to feed Elijah (1 Kgs 17:4-6); "consider the ravens" teaches trust in the Father's provision (Luke 12:24).

lexicon.title: Dwelling of Demons, Cage of Unclean Birds

words.meaning: Esau sells his birthright for red pottage and is called Edom, red (Gen 25:30); red marks sin "red like crimson" (Isa 1:18), the one coming from Edom in garments red from the winepress (Isa 63:2), the red horse and red dragon.
Noah's name means rest (Gen 5:29) and the ark "rested" on the mountains (Gen 8:4); Scripture points to the rest Yahuah gives His people and "a rest to the people of Elohim" that remains (Heb 4:9).

Rachel's son is renamed Benjamin, "son of the right hand," and Jacob crosses his right hand onto the younger (Gen 48:14); the right hand is the place of honor and power where Messiah is seated (Ps 110:1; Acts 7:55).

also.meaning: The right hand is Yahuah's strength and the place of highest honor: His right hand dashed the enemy (Exod 15:6), and He seats the "man of thy right hand" there (Ps 80:17; 110:1), where Yahushua was exalted (Acts 2:33).

words.meaning: Scripture shows what Yahuah looks for in the offering: thanksgiving and paid vows (Ps 50:14), a broken and contrite spirit (Ps 51:17), and "the sacrifice of praise... the fruit of our lips" (Heb 13:15).

Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt for looking back, a warning Messiah repeats ("Remember Lot's wife," Luke 17:32); salt also seals the covenant (Num 18:19) and pictures disciples as the salt of the earth (Matt 5:13).

also.meaning: Required on every offering as "the salt of the covenant of thy Elohim" (Lev 2:13) — a lasting, incorruptible covenant (Num 18:19); "have salt in yourselves" (Mark 9:50), "speech... seasoned with salt" (Col 4:6).

Salt is the sign of a lasting covenant, 'a covenant of salt' (Num 18:19; 2 Chr 13:5); Elisha cast salt from a new cruse into Jericho's spring and the waters were healed, 'there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land' (2 Kgs 2:21); the disciples are 'the salt of the earth' (Matt 5:13).
Salt of the covenant on every offering (Lev 2:13; Ezek 43:24); the miry places not healed by the river "shall be given to salt" (Ezek 47:11) - barrenness left outside the life of the waters.

The preserving sign of an everlasting covenant (Lev 2:13; Num 18:19): disciples are the salt of the earth (Matt 5:13), every sacrifice is salted (Mark 9:49), and speech is to be seasoned with salt (Col 4:6).

words.meaning: Abraham's seed shall be as the sand of the sea for multitude (Gen 22:17); Paul notes only a remnant of that sand shall be saved (Rom 9:27), and Gog's armies are "as the sand of the sea" (Rev 20:8).

also.meaning: Two uses: the countless seed of Abraham as the sand of the sea (Gen 22:17; Rom 9:27), and an unstable footing, the house built by one who hears and does not do (Matt 7:26-27).

words.meaning: Yahuah smells a sweet savour from Noah's offering; Scripture applies it to Messiah's offering of Himself (Eph 5:2) and to the obedient people who are "a sweet savour of Messiah" (2 Cor 2:15).

A scarlet thread marks the firstborn hand at Perez's birth; Scripture uses scarlet for the cord of Rahab's deliverance (Josh 2:18), cleansing rites (Lev 14:4; Heb 9:19), sins "as scarlet" (Isa 1:18), and the harlot's dress (Rev 17:4).

also.meaning: Worm-dyed crimson in the sanctuary hangings and cleansing rites (Lev 14:4); "I am a worm (tola'ath)" (Ps 22:6) is the sufferer's cry, and sins "as scarlet" are made white (Isa 1:18); the harlot counterfeits it (Rev 17:3).

Two uses: the scarlet line that marked Rahab's deliverance (Josh 2:18) and scarlet wool in cleansing (Lev 14:4; Heb 9:19); and sin itself, "though your sins be as scarlet" (Isa 1:18), worn by the harlot's beast (Rev 17:3).
"Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow" (Isa 1:18) - the deep stain of sin; also the cord of Rahab's deliverance (Josh 2:18) and the harlot's array (Rev 17:4).

words.meaning: "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah" until Shiloh comes; the same word means rod and tribe, and the sceptre rising out of Israel (Num 24:17) becomes the rod of iron with which Messiah rules (Ps 2:9; Rev 19:15).

also.meaning: Royal authority: 'the sceptre shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh come' (Gen 49:10); in Persia none could come to the king uncalled 'except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live' (Esth 4:11), and Esther touched its top and was received.
Judah's royal rule "until Shiloh come" (Gen 49:10); Judah's vine is left "no strong rod to be a sceptre to rule" (Ezek 19:14) - overturned "until he come whose right it is" (Ezek 21:27).

Royal rule that shall not depart from Judah until Shiloh come (Gen 49:10); the sceptre of righteousness of the king anointed by his Elohim above his fellows (Ps 45:7; Heb 1:8-9); the extended golden sceptre grants life (Esth 4:11).

words.meaning: A seal is the owner's mark of possession and pledge: "Set me as a seal upon thine heart" (Song 8:6); Zerubbabel is made Yahuah's signet (Hag 2:23), and His servants are sealed in their foreheads (Rev 7:3).

also.meaning: Ownership and authentication: Messiah "hath Elohim the Father sealed" (John 6:27); believers are sealed with the holy spirit of promise (Eph 1:13), and "Yahuah knoweth them that are his" is the seal of His foundation (2 Tim 2:19).

words.meaning: The brothers' sheaves bow to Joseph's sheaf; the firstfruits sheaf is waved at Bikkurim (Lev 23:10-11), and Scripture pictures the harvest of the faithful as sheaves brought home with rejoicing (Ps 126:6).

also.meaning: Joseph's sheaf rose and stood upright while his brothers' sheaves bowed (Gen 37:7); the waved sheaf (omer) of firstfruits accepted for Israel (Lev 23:11) is fulfilled in the risen Messiah (1 Cor 15:20).

words.meaning: Flocks are the fathers' wealth; Scripture interprets: "ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men" (Ezek 34:31), sheep that go astray (Isa 53:6) and hear the Shepherd's voice (John 10:27).

also.meaning: "All we like sheep have gone astray" (Isa 53:6) - Yahuah's people scattered by false shepherds (Jer 50:6; Ezek 34:6); the Servant Himself is a sheep dumb before her shearers (Isa 53:7).

Yahuah's people who need a shepherd (Num 27:17): all have gone astray like sheep (Isa 53:6), yet His sheep hear Messiah's voice and follow (John 10:27); a sheep's covering can disguise a wolf (Matt 7:15).

words.meaning: Sheol is the grave, never full (Prov 27:20), cruel as jealousy (Song 8:6); Yahuah would not leave His Holy One's soul in it (Ps 16:10; Acts 2:27) and redeems His own from its power (Ps 49:15; Hos 13:14).

Abel is a keeper of sheep and the fathers are shepherds, "an abomination unto the Egyptians" (Gen 46:34); Jacob calls Elohim the one who fed (shepherded) him (Gen 48:15), and Yahuah sets up one shepherd, David (Ezek 34:23).

also.meaning: Yahuah is the Shepherd of Israel who feeds, leads and restores His flock (Ps 23:1; 80:1); He sets one shepherd, His servant David, over them (Ezek 34:23), fulfilled in Yahushua the good shepherd (John 10:11).

Yahuah feeds His flock like a shepherd (Isa 40:11); the shepherds who feed themselves are judged (Ezek 34:2); He sets up one shepherd, "my servant David" (Ezek 34:23) - Messiah the good shepherd (John 10:11).
Yahuah is Israel's shepherd (Ps 23:1; Gen 49:24) who sets up one shepherd, His servant David (Ezek 34:23): Messiah the good, great and chief Shepherd (John 10:11; Heb 13:20; 1 Pet 5:4).

words.meaning: Yahuah Himself is the shield of those who trust Him (Gen 15:1; Ps 3:3; Prov 30:5); in the assembly the shield is trust in Him, quenching the fiery darts of the wicked (Eph 6:16).

also.meaning: Yahuah is the shield of those who trust Him (Gen 15:1; Prov 30:5); the believer takes the shield of belief to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked (Eph 6:16).

words.meaning: Zebulun dwells at the haven of the sea, a haven for ships; Scripture brings ships to Yahuah's desired haven (Ps 107:30) and to carry Zion's sons home (Isa 60:9), while Babylon's shipmasters mourn her fall (Rev 18:17).

also.meaning: Proud commerce of the nations, broken in the day of Yahuah (Isa 2:16) - Tyre pictured as a splendid ship sunk in the seas (Ezek 27); yet ships of Tarshish bring Zion's sons home (Isa 60:9).
A great ship is turned by a very small helm, as the small tongue directs the life (Jas 3:4); some have made shipwreck of belief (1 Tim 1:19), as Jonah's flight brought the storm (Jonah 1:4).

lexicon.title: Tyre's Mourners: Kings, Merchants and Mariners

words.meaning: Judah's signet is his identity and pledge (Gen 38:18), Pharaoh's ring gives Joseph his authority (Gen 41:42); Yahuah makes Zerubbabel "as a signet" (Hag 2:23), and the seal of the living Elohim marks His servants (Rev 7:2).

also.meaning: The king's ring passed his authority, from Pharaoh to Joseph and from Ahasuerus to Haman then Mordecai, and what was sealed with it 'may no man reverse' (Esth 8:8); Yahuah makes Zerubbabel 'as a signet' (Hag 2:23), and believers are sealed with the holy spirit of promise (Eph 1:13).
Though Coniah were the signet on Yahuah's right hand, He would pluck him off (Jer 22:24); Zerubbabel, of the same line, is made a signet - chosen and sealed (Hag 2:23).
The king's signet sealed the stone on the den "that the purpose might not be changed" (Dan 6:17), the pattern of the sealed tomb (Matt 27:66) — a seal men set that Yahuah's deliverance breaks.

lexicon.title: The Prodigal's Robe, Ring and Sandals

words.meaning: Joseph is sold by his brothers for twenty pieces of silver; Scripture shows the shepherd valued at thirty pieces (Zech 11:12) and Yahushua betrayed for that price (Matt 26:15).

also.meaning: The half-shekel atonement money that became the tent's sockets (Exod 30:16; 38:27); the words of Yahuah are silver purified seven times (Ps 12:6), and the Messiah was priced at thirty pieces (Matt 26:15).

Ransom money for souls (Exod 30:12-16) and words purified seven times (Ps 12:6); yet believers are not redeemed with corruptible silver and gold but with Messiah's precious blood (1 Pet 1:18-19); thirty pieces priced the Shepherd (Zech 11:12).
The breast and arms of silver are the kingdom "inferior to thee" that rose after Babylon (Dan 2:39), shown in Dan 5:28 and 8:20 to be the Medes and Persians, two arms joined in one breast.

words.meaning: Abraham sees the smoke of Sodom rise "as the smoke of a furnace"; Scripture uses rising smoke as the lasting witness of judgment (Isa 34:10; Rev 14:11; 18:9).

also.meaning: Sinai smoked as a furnace because Yahuah descended in fire; smoke marks His presence and judgment, filling the temple in Revelation (Rev 15:8).
The house filled with smoke at the seraphim's cry (Isa 6:4) - the veiling of Yahuah's holy presence, as at Sinai (Exod 19:18) and the heavenly temple none could enter (Rev 15:8).

words.meaning: Sodom is wickedness ripe for judgment, "set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire" (Jude 7); the prophets call apostate Jerusalem Sodom (Isa 1:10), and the great city is spiritually called Sodom (Rev 11:8).

also.meaning: Jerusalem's rulers addressed as rulers of Sodom (Isa 1:10) - pride, fulness of bread and neglect of the poor (Ezek 16:49); the great city "spiritually called Sodom" (Rev 11:8).

lexicon.title: The Great City (Spiritually Sodom and Egypt)

words.meaning: Judah's staff identifies him; the same word names a tribe, and the tribal rods are laid up before Yahuah until Aaron's buds (Num 17); Jacob worshipped "leaning upon the top of his staff" (Heb 11:21), and Yahuah's rod and staff comfort (Ps 23:4).

also.meaning: Staff in hand at Pesach marks the pilgrim ready to leave Egypt; the staff is the traveler's support and the shepherd's comfort (Ps 23:4).

Poles that never left the ark's rings (Exod 25:15), so the holy things were carried on Levite shoulders, not carts (Num 7:9); Uzzah's death shows Yahuah's holiness is carried His way, not man's (2 Sam 6:6-7; 1 Chr 15:13-15).
The staff is what a person leans on: Yahuah's staff comforts His sheep (Ps 23:4), while Egypt is a "staff of this broken reed" that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it (Isa 36:6).
The shepherd's two staves Beauty and Bands are Yahuah's covenant with the peoples and the brotherhood of Judah and Israel, both broken when the flock rejects him (Zech 11:10, 14).
