words.meaning: Jacob's pillow stone becomes "Elohim's house" (Gen 28:22); Jacob calls Yahuah's help "the shepherd, the stone of Israel" (Gen 49:24), and Scripture builds the rejected cornerstone and living stones on this (1 Pet 2:4-8).

also.meaning: The stone of Israel (Gen 49:24): Messiah the living stone, rejected by men, chosen of Elohim, a cornerstone to believers and a stone of stumbling to the disobedient; believers are living stones built into a spiritual house (1 Pet 2:4-8).

Twelve stones lifted from the Jordan's bed and set up at Gilgal were 'a sign among you' and a memorial for children who ask (Josh 4:6-7), one per tribe, as Elijah's altar later and the living stones of 1 Pet 2:5.

David chose five smooth stones from the brook and one sank into the giant's forehead (1 Sam 17:49); Daniel's stone cut without hands likewise strikes the image and becomes a mountain (Dan 2:34-35), the stone that falls and grinds to powder (Matt 21:44).

The stone cut out without hands is the kingdom the Elohim of heaven sets up, which breaks the image and stands forever (Dan 2:44-45); Yahushua applies the stone that grinds to powder to Himself (Matt 21:44).

words.meaning: Abraham calls himself "a stranger and a sojourner"; Scripture makes this the posture of all Yahuah's people, who "confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth" (Heb 11:13; 1 Pet 2:11).

The fathers dwell in tents as strangers looking for a lasting city (Heb 11:9-10); the body is an earthly tent (2 Cor 5:1), Messiah tabernacled among men (John 1:14), and Yahuah's tabernacle comes to dwell with men (Rev 21:3).

also.meaning: How goodly are your tents, O Jacob, spread as valleys and gardens by the river; Israel's pilgrim tents are Yahuah's blessed planting (Num 24:5-6).
"Enlarge the place of thy tent... lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes" (Isa 54:2) - Zion spreading to the nations; a ruined tent with broken cords is Judah's desolation (Jer 10:20).

The mortal body as a temporary dwelling, removed like a shepherd's tent (Isa 38:12): if this earthly house of the tabernacle is dissolved, there is a building of Elohim eternal in the heavens (2 Cor 5:1).

words.meaning: On the third day Abraham sees the place of offering, and Isaac is received back; Scripture makes the third day the day of raising up ("in the third day he will raise us up," Hos 6:2; 1 Cor 15:4).

also.meaning: "After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up" (Hos 6:2) — Yahuah's revival of His people, pictured in Messiah raised the third day "according to the scriptures" (1 Cor 15:4).

lexicon.title: Sign of Jonah (Three Days and Nights)

words.meaning: "The tithe... is holy unto Yahuah" (Lev 27:30), given to Levi for service since they had no inheritance (Num 18:21-24); Abraham gave it to Melchizedek, showing the greater priesthood (Heb 7:5-9).
One lip is confounded at Babel to scatter man's rebellion; Yahuah promises to turn to the people "a pure language" to call on His name (Zeph 3:9), shown in the tongues of Shavuot (Acts 2:4-11).

also.meaning: Two uses: the deceitful tongue like a sharp razor (Ps 52:2), an unruly evil full of deadly poison (Jas 3:8); and the tongue of the learned given by Yahuah (Isa 50:4), the tongues as of fire at Shavuot (Acts 2:3).

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: The burning lamp passed between Abram's pieces (Gen 15:17); in Gideon's hand the torch revealed the attack, Jerusalem's deliverance goes forth 'as a lamp that burneth' (Isa 62:1), and seven lamps of fire burn before the throne (Rev 4:5).

lexicon.title: Seven Spirits (Seven Lamps and Seven Eyes)

words.meaning: The servant's girding: Messiah girds himself with a towel to wash feet as a servant (John 13:4-5), the hospitality of Abraham (Gen 18:4) made an example, "ye also ought to wash one another's feet" (John 13:14).
Babel's tower reaches for heaven in man's strength; Scripture answers that "the name of Yahuah is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

also.meaning: Men built a tower to make themselves a name (Gen 11:4), but "the name of Yahuah is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10; Ps 61:3).
Built in the midst of the vineyard for its watch and keeping (Isa 5:2); "the name of Yahuah is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

words.meaning: The offering allowed to the poor (Lev 5:7; 12:8), the very offering Joseph and Mary brought for Yahushua's birth (Luke 2:24) — the anointed born among the poor.

also.meaning: The turtledove is the offering of the poor (Lev 12:8; Luke 2:24) and the voice of returning spring (Song 2:12); it keeps its appointed time while Israel does not (Jer 8:7), and it pictures the defenseless people (Ps 74:19).

words.meaning: Jacob's twelve sons become the twelve tribes (Gen 49:28); twelve marks Yahuah's whole covenant people, carried on the breastplate (Exod 28:21), judged by the twelve apostles (Matt 19:28), and written on the gates and foundations (Rev 21:12-14).

also.meaning: The full people of Yahuah: the twelve tribes of Israel (Gen 49:28) and the twelve apostles who judge them (Matt 19:28); the city's gates bear the tribes' names and its foundations the apostles' (Rev 21:12-14).

words.meaning: Rebekah veils herself on meeting her bridegroom, while Tamar's veil disguises (Gen 38:14); Scripture speaks of a veil spread over all nations that Yahuah will destroy (Isa 25:7) and one taken away when the heart turns (2 Cor 3:16).

also.meaning: Moses' veil hid the fading glory; Paul says the veil remains on the heart in reading Moses until it turns to the Master (2 Cor 3:15-16).
The cherub-worked veil dividing the holy from the most holy (Exod 26:33), behind which the high priest alone went yearly; Yahushua as forerunner has entered "within the veil" (Heb 6:19-20).

The dividing curtain of the sanctuary; the outer (Holy Place) veil tore at Messiah's death (Matt 27:51), the way opened "through the veil, that is to say, his flesh" (Heb 10:20); a veil remains over hearts until they turn (2 Cor 3:16).
"The covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations" destroyed on Yahuah's mountain (Isa 25:7) - blindness and death swallowed up in victory (1 Cor 15:54).

words.meaning: The butler's vine buds and brings forth grapes; Scripture names Israel the vine brought out of Egypt (Ps 80:8; Hos 10:1), and Messiah "the true vine" with His Father the husbandman (John 15:1).

also.meaning: Israel planted as Yahuah's vine (Ps 80:8; Isa 5:7, "the vineyard of Yahuah... is the house of Israel"), which bore wild grapes; Messiah is the true vine and the Father the husbandman (John 15:1).
Israel planted a noble vine that turned degenerate (Jer 2:21); vine wood is good only for fire when fruitless (Ezek 15); Zedekiah's spreading vine (Ezek 17:6); Messiah the true vine (John 15:1).

lexicon.title: Vine of the Earth and the Winepress

words.meaning: Noah plants the first vineyard; Scripture interprets it: "the vineyard of Yahuah of hosts is the house of Israel" (Isa 5:7), and Messiah's parables of the vineyard and its husbandmen build on this.

also.meaning: "The vineyard of Yahuah of hosts is the house of Israel" (Isa 5:7); the bride confesses "mine own vineyard have I not kept" (Song 1:6), and the sluggard's vineyard grown over with thorns is a life neglected (Prov 24:30-31).

"The vineyard of Yahuah of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant" (Isa 5:7); many pastors tread it down (Jer 12:10); Yahushua retells it against the husbandmen (Matt 21:33).

words.meaning: The fathers' wells give water in the wilderness and are fought over and reopened (Gen 26:18); Scripture draws water "out of the wells of salvation" (Isa 12:3), and Messiah offers living water from a well (John 4:14).

also.meaning: The source of life-giving water: Israel forsook the fountain for broken cisterns (Jer 2:13); at Jacob's well Messiah offers water springing up into everlasting life (John 4:14), while false teachers are wells without water (2 Pet 2:17).

words.meaning: Ishmael shall be "a wild man" (literally a wild-ass man), every hand against him (Gen 16:12); Scripture uses the wild ass for the untamed and for Israel running after lovers (Jer 2:24; Hos 8:9).

also.meaning: Israel as a wild ass in heat snuffing the wind - unrestrained lust after idols that will not be turned back (Jer 2:23-24); Ephraim "a wild ass alone by himself" (Hos 8:9).
Ephraim gone up to Assyria is "a wild ass alone by himself" (Hos 8:9) — stubborn, untamed independence, the beast in heat of Jer 2:24.

words.meaning: Wine shames Noah, yet Melchizedek brings it with bread (Gen 14:18); Scripture uses wine both for the cup of the covenant in Messiah's blood (Matt 26:28) and for Babylon's intoxicating fornication (Rev 17:2).

also.meaning: Judah washes his garments in wine, the blood of grapes (Gen 49:11): wine is the blood of the covenant shed for remission of sins (Matt 26:28), the entry into the covenant, and the good wine kept until last (John 2:10).

lexicon.title: Bread and Wine of the Covenant Meal

words.meaning: Jacob and Laban raise Galeed, "the heap of witness," to stand between them; Scripture calls stones and people as witnesses (Josh 24:27), Israel Yahuah's witnesses (Isa 43:10), Messiah the faithful witness (Rev 1:5).

also.meaning: The eastern tribes' altar was named Ed, 'a witness between us that Yahuah is Elohim' (Josh 22:34), not for sacrifice; Joshua's great stone under the oak at Shechem 'heard' the covenant and stood as witness against denial (Josh 24:27).
At the mouth of two or three witnesses a matter is established; heaven and earth, the song and the book are also called as witnesses (Deut 31:26; 32:1), and Revelation's two witnesses testify.
"Ye are my witnesses, saith Yahuah... that I am he: before me there was no El formed" (Isa 43:10) - Israel called to testify that Yahuah alone is Elohim and Savior (Isa 43:11).

lexicon.title: The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness

words.meaning: Benjamin "shall ravin as a wolf"; Scripture uses the wolf for rulers who devour (Ezek 22:27) and false prophets in sheep's clothing (Matt 7:15; Acts 20:29), while in the restored world the wolf dwells with the lamb (Isa 11:6).

also.meaning: Ravening princes and false prophets who devour the flock (Ezek 22:27; Matt 7:15); the wolf dwelling with the lamb pictures enmity ended in Yahuah's holy mountain (Isa 11:6; 65:25).

The devouring predator of the flock: Jerusalem's princes are wolves ravening the prey (Ezek 22:27); false prophets come as wolves in sheep's clothing (Matt 7:15) and grievous wolves enter the assembly (Acts 20:29).

words.meaning: Isaac carries the wood of his own offering up the mount; one hanged on a tree is under the curse (Deut 21:23), and Messiah bore "our sins in his own body on the tree" (1 Pet 2:24; Gal 3:13).

Jacob wrestled and prevailed, receiving the name Israel (Gen 32:28); the believer wrestles not against flesh and blood but against spiritual wickedness (Eph 6:12) and must strive lawfully to be crowned (2 Tim 2:5).
"I have broken the bands of your yoke, and made you go upright" (Lev 26:13) — release from Egypt's bondage; the heifer bore no yoke (Num 19:2), and Yahushua offers his easy yoke (Matt 11:29-30).

also.meaning: Serving enemies under a yoke of iron is the curse of refusing Yahuah's service; He broke Egypt's yoke, and Yahushua offers an easy yoke (Lev 26:13; Matt 11:30).

Bondage to a foreign master which Yahuah breaks (Lev 26:13; Isa 10:27); Jeremiah wore a wooden yoke for submission to Babylon, and breaking it brought one of iron (Jer 27:2; 28:13); Messiah's yoke is easy (Matt 11:29).

words.meaning: Satan means adversary, the accuser who stands against the righteous before Yahuah (Job 1:6-12; Zech 3:1); the psalmist prays that an adversary stand at the wicked man's right hand (Ps 109:6), and the accuser is cast down (Rev 12:10).

also.meaning: The adversary standing to resist the high priest is the accuser rebuked by Yahuah who has chosen Jerusalem (Zech 3:1-2) — "the accuser of our brethren" cast down (Rev 12:10).

words.meaning: Aaron's dead rod that budded, blossomed and yielded almonds marks the one Yahuah chose; the almond ("watcher") shows Yahuah watching over His word to perform it (Jer 1:11-12).

also.meaning: Lampstand cups shaped like almond blossoms (Exod 25:33); Aaron's rod budded almonds to show Yahuah's chosen priest (Num 17:8), and the almond (shaqed) answers "I will hasten (shoqed) my word" — the watching tree (Jer 1:11-12).

The almond is the first tree to wake: its cups shape the lampstand (Exod 25:33), Aaron's rod budded almonds to show Yahuah's chosen (Num 17:8), it means Yahuah watching over His word (Jer 1:11-12), and its white blossom marks old age (Eccl 12:5).

"A rod of an almond tree... I will hasten my word to perform it" (Jer 1:11-12) - shaqed/shoqed, the wakeful tree: Yahuah watching over His word; Aaron's rod bore almonds as sign of His chosen priest (Num 17:8).

words.meaning: Israel's tents as lign aloes that Yahuah planted (Num 24:6); with myrrh it scents the anointed king's garments (Ps 45:8), and a hundred pounds weight was brought for Messiah's burial as a king (John 19:39).
Amalek attacked the faint and weary at the rear and is the enemy Yahuah wars with from generation to generation (Exod 17:16; Deut 25:18).

also.meaning: The first nation to strike Israel in the wilderness, with whom Yahuah has war 'from generation to generation' (Exod 17:16); Saul spared Agag and lost the kingdom (1 Sam 15:23), and Haman 'the Agagite' rose again against Mordecai's people (Esth 3:1).

words.meaning: Israel kept as the apple of His eye shows Yahuah's tender guarding; he that touches His people touches the apple of His eye (Zech 2:8).

also.meaning: The pupil, the most guarded part of the body: Yahuah keeps Israel as the apple of His eye (Deut 32:10; Ps 17:8), whoever touches His people touches it (Zech 2:8), and His law is to be kept the same way (Prov 7:2).

words.meaning: Yahuah's own power to deliver, made bare before the nations (Isa 52:10) and revealed in His Servant (Isa 53:1; John 12:38); He breaks the arm of Pharaoh (Ezek 30:21).
The avenger of blood is the near kinsman who pursues the slayer; the same word is the kinsman-redeemer, showing that the next of kin both avenges and redeems.
The servant who loves his master has his ear bored at the door to serve for ever; "mine ears hast thou opened" marks the willing servant who delights to do Yahuah's will (Ps 40:6-8).

'Master, husband': the Canaanite name Israel served instead of Yahuah; at Carmel the choice was 'if Yahuah be Elohim, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him' (1 Kgs 18:21), and Yahuah promises to take 'the names of Baalim out of her mouth' (Hos 2:17).
Israel joined to Baal-peor through Moab's women by Balaam's counsel; Revelation names the doctrine of Balaam who taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock (Rev 2:14).
Yahuah-nissi, Yahuah my banner; the same word is the pole of the brazen serpent and the ensign of the root of Jesse to which the nations seek (Isa 11:10).

also.meaning: A banner is the rallying sign of whom a people belong to: Yahuah-nissi, "Yahuah my banner" (Exod 17:15); "his banner over me was love" (Song 2:4), and the root of Jesse stands as an ensign to the nations (Isa 11:10).

words.meaning: Bashan, rich pastureland of fat cattle and great oaks, stands for proud strength: its high hill envies the hill Elohim chose for His dwelling (Ps 68:15-16), and its oaks are brought low in the day of Yahuah (Isa 2:13).
Bees are swarming, stinging enemies: the Amorites chased Israel as bees (Deut 1:44), and "they compassed me about like bees" — but in Yahuah's name they are cut off (Ps 118:12).

also.meaning: Hostile armies swarming at Yahuah's call - the Amorites chased Israel as bees (Deut 1:44); Yahuah hisses for the fly of Egypt and the bee of Assyria (Isa 7:18).

words.meaning: Bitter herbs eaten with the lamb recall lives made bitter with hard bondage (Exod 1:14); deliverance is remembered together with the bitterness it ended.

Neither offering nor serving priest might have a blemish (Lev 21:17; 22:20); Messiah is "a lamb without blemish and without spot" (1 Pet 1:19), and the assembly is to be presented "holy and without blemish" (Eph 5:27).
Judgment of a heart made fat so it cannot see (Isa 6:10); opening blind eyes is the Servant's mark (Isa 35:5; 42:7) - "who is blind, but my servant?" (Isa 42:19).

also.meaning: Spiritual blindness: groping at noonday under the curse (Deut 28:29), the god of this world blinding minds (2 Cor 4:4), Laodicea blind without knowing it (Rev 3:17); Messiah opens blind eyes (Isa 42:7; John 9:39).

words.meaning: Blood sprinkled on the people ratifies the covenant; Yahushua says "this is my blood of the new covenant" (Matt 26:28), the blood of sprinkling (Heb 12:24).
The cord of blue in the fringe ties remembrance of the commandments to the color of the high priest's robe, a holy people marked as belonging to Yahuah.

also.meaning: Blue yarn in veil, curtains and priestly robe, and on the ark's outer cloth (Num 4:6); the blue cord of the fringe was given "that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of Yahuah" (Num 15:39).

words.meaning: Boils from the furnace ashes struck even the magicians; the botch of Egypt is promised to a disobedient Israel (Deut 28:27), and the first bowl repeats it on the beast's worshippers (Rev 16:2).
Moses asks to be blotted out of Yahuah's book; whoever sins, him will He blot out (Exod 32:33), the book of life of Revelation.

also.meaning: Laid beside the ark as a witness (Deut 31:26), the book of the Torah was lost in the house of Yahuah and found in Josiah's repairs; the king rent his clothes and the covenant was renewed (2 Kgs 22:11; 23:3), the Torah recovered, not set aside.
Moses asked to be blotted from Yahuah's book; "whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book" (Exod 32:33), the book of life opened at the judgment (Rev 20:12).
The words shut up and sealed "to the time of the end" (Dan 12:4) are prophecy not yet opened to understanding; Revelation is told the opposite, "Seal not" (Rev 22:10).

words.meaning: The place of closeness and carrying: the shepherd carries lambs in his bosom (Isa 40:11), Lazarus rests in Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22), and the only begotten Son in the Father's bosom declares Him (John 1:18).

Judgment-strength - heavens of brass (Deut 28:23), the serpent of brass for sin's judgment (Num 21:9); the creatures' feet sparkle like burnished brass (Ezek 1:7); the measuring man "like the appearance of brass" (Ezek 40:3).

also.meaning: Metal of the outer altar, laver and sockets of the court, where sin is judged (Exod 27:2-6); the brazen serpent bore the curse (Num 21:9), and Messiah's feet are "like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace" (Rev 1:15).
The belly and thighs of brass are the third kingdom "which shall bear rule over all the earth" (Dan 2:39), named Grecia in Dan 8:21; brass nails mark the fourth beast's grip (Dan 7:19).

words.meaning: Whoever looked on the brass serpent lifted on the pole lived; so must the Son of man be lifted up (John 3:14). When later worshipped as Nehushtan it was broken (2 Kgs 18:4).
Bricks made under the taskmaster picture the hard bondage of Egypt, man-made labor without rest, set against the uncut stone Yahuah builds with (Exod 20:25; Isa 9:10).
The bulrush is the fragile river reed that cradled Moses; Isaiah uses the bowing bulrush for empty, outward fasting (Isa 58:5).
The thorn bush burning yet not consumed shows Yahuah's presence dwelling among a lowly people without destroying them; Yahushua cites it for the resurrection (Mark 12:26).

The household measuring vessel of daily trade; putting the lamp under a bushel pictures light hidden by ordinary concerns, when it should be set on a lampstand to give light to all in the house (Matt 5:15).
Korah's censers, offered without calling, became plates covering the altar as a sign; Aaron's censer stopped the plague (Num 16:46-48); the angel's censer fills with altar fire (Rev 8:5).

also.meaning: The firepan carrying altar coals and incense within the veil (Lev 16:12); Aaron's censer stood between the dead and the living to stay the plague (Num 16:48), and an angel's censer casts fire to the earth (Rev 8:5).

words.meaning: Pharaoh's chariots are the strength man trusts in; Yahuah took off their wheels. Some trust in chariots, but we will remember the name of Yahuah (Ps 20:7).

also.meaning: Chariots are worldly military trust: "some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah" (Ps 20:7); Yahuah's own chariots are the hosts of heaven (Ps 68:17; 2 Kgs 6:17).

A chariot and horses of fire parted Elijah and Elisha, and the servant's eyes were opened to see the mountain 'full of horses and chariots of fire' (2 Kgs 6:17), Yahuah's unseen host; 'my father, the chariot of Israel' named the prophet as Israel's true defense (2 Kgs 13:14).
The four chariots "are the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the Adon of all the earth" (Zech 6:5) — Yahuah's agents to all quarters, horses red, black, white, grisled.

words.meaning: The manslayer fled to the city of refuge and lived there until the high priest's death; Hebrews speaks of those who have fled for refuge to the hope set before them (Heb 6:18).
Moses hidden in a cleft of the rock and covered by Yahuah's hand sees His glory pass by; the rock is the place of shelter before His face.

also.meaning: Yahuah put Moses "in a clift of the rock" and covered him with His hand while His glory passed by (Exod 33:22); "that Rock was Messiah" (1 Cor 10:4), the hiding place of the one who sees His goodness.

words.meaning: "Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it" (Isa 65:8) - the remnant for whose sake Yahuah spares the whole.
The enemy sank into the depths like a stone and lead; Micah applies it to sin: Yahuah will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea (Mic 7:19).

also.meaning: Measured every thousand cubits: waters to the ankles, the knees, the loins, then "waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed over" (Ezek 47:3-5) - life from the sanctuary ever deepening; Scripture gives no separate meaning for each depth.

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: The destroyer passes over the houses marked with blood; Paul names the destroyer who struck the murmurers (1 Cor 10:10), and Revelation names Abaddon.

"I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce" (Jer 3:8) - Yahuah's sending away of adulterous Israel, while still calling "Turn, O backsliding children... for I am married unto you" (Jer 3:14).

Dogs are the unclean and the godless enemies: they compass the pierced sufferer (Ps 22:16); a fool returning to his folly is a dog returning to its vomit (Prov 26:11), and dogs are outside the holy city (Rev 22:15).

also.meaning: Israel's blind watchmen are "dumb dogs, they cannot bark", greedy and never satisfied (Isa 56:10-11); dogs stand outside the city (Rev 22:15).

The unclean and shameless outsider: the price of a dog is barred from Yahuah's house (Deut 23:18); dogs encircle the sufferer (Ps 22:16), return to vomit (Prov 26:11; 2 Pet 2:22), and stand outside the city (Rev 22:15).

words.meaning: Blood on the two side posts marks the house the destroyer passes over; later the words of Yahuah are written on the same doorposts, the blood first, then the commandments (Deut 6:9).

The firstborn's right was 'a double portion of all that he hath' (Deut 21:17); Elisha asked a double portion of Elijah's spirit as the heir of the prophet, granted if he saw him taken (2 Kgs 2:9-10); Yahuah promises 'double' in place of shame (Isa 61:7).
A nation swift as the eagle is the invading judgment on covenant breakers; yet Yahuah bore Israel on eagles' wings and stirs the nest (Exod 19:4; Deut 32:11).

also.meaning: Yahuah bearing His people on eagles' wings out of Egypt (Exod 19:4); those who wait on Him mount up as eagles (Isa 40:31); one face of the living creatures (Ezek 1:10).

lexicon.title: Two Wings of a Great Eagle

words.meaning: Elim's twelve wells and seventy palm trees are rest and abundance after Marah; the righteous flourish like the palm (Ps 92:12), and the redeemed hold palms by living fountains (Rev 7:9, 17).
A banner lifted high for the nations to rally to (Isa 11:12) - Messiah standing as an ensign of the peoples; the same word is the pole on which the bronze serpent was lifted (Num 21:8; John 3:14).
The eternal Elohim is a refuge and underneath are the everlasting arms; He carries His people from the womb to old age (Isa 46:4).

Yahuah's all-seeing watch: His eyes are on the land (Deut 11:12) and run through the whole earth (2 Chr 16:9; Zech 4:10); all things are naked to His eyes (Heb 4:13), and the Lamb's seven eyes are the seven spirits of Elohim (Rev 5:6).

also.meaning: Rims, bodies and wings "full of eyes round about" (Ezek 1:18; 10:12) - "the eyes of Yahuah run to and fro throughout the whole earth" (2 Chr 16:9); nothing hidden from His sight.
The little horn's man's eyes show human insight and oversight in place of Yahuah's — "the lofty looks of man" that He brings low (Isa 2:11), the number of a man (Rev 13:18).

lexicon.title: Seven Spirits (Seven Lamps and Seven Eyes)
Eyes Like a Flame of Fire

words.meaning: Fiery serpents sent among the murmuring people are the bite of sin and death; Yahuah's remedy was not to remove the serpents but to give a sign to look upon (Num 21:8).
The finger of Elohim wrote the tables and is confessed in the plagues; Yahushua cast out demons by the finger of Elohim (Luke 11:20), meaning by Yahuah's own power.

also.meaning: Yahuah's direct power: the magicians confessed the plague "the finger of Elohim" (Exod 8:19), the tables were written with it (Exod 31:18), and Yahushua casts out devils by the finger of Elohim (Luke 11:20).

words.meaning: Yahuah's word "as a burning fire shut up in my bones" (Jer 20:9), and a fire in the prophet's mouth devouring the people as wood (Jer 5:14); Yahuah Himself a consuming fire (Deut 4:24).

also.meaning: Yahuah's presence that purifies or consumes: the bush burning but not consumed (Exod 3:2), the refiner's fire (Mal 3:2), immersion with fire (Matt 3:11), fire trying every work (1 Cor 3:13); "our Elohim is a consuming fire" (Heb 12:29).

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: The fleshpots, leeks and onions of Egypt picture appetite that looks back to bondage; in their hearts they turned back again into Egypt (Acts 7:39).
"I set my face like a flint" (Isa 50:7) - the Servant's unbending resolve (Luke 9:51); Yahuah made Ezekiel's forehead harder than flint (Ezek 3:9) and turned the flint rock into water (Deut 8:15).
The swarm falls on Egypt but not on Goshen, the first plague marking a division between Yahuah's people and Egypt (Exod 8:22-23); Isaiah's fly from Egypt is an invading army (Isa 7:18).
Circumcise the foreskin of your heart and be no more stiffnecked; Yahuah Himself will circumcise the heart to love Him (Deut 30:6; Rom 2:29).
"Assemble yourselves... to my sacrifice" - birds summoned to eat the flesh of the mighty (Ezek 39:17) - the shame of unburied enemies, answered in the great supper of Rev 19:17.

lexicon.title: Great Supper of Yahuah (Feast of the Birds)

words.meaning: Fringes on the borders of garments are to be looked on to remember all the commandments and not go after one's own heart and eyes (Num 15:39); the sick touched the hem of Yahushua's garment.
Frogs swarming out of the river into bedchambers and ovens picture an unclean plague issuing from Egypt's own source; Revelation names three unclean spirits like frogs (Rev 16:13).
The sign upon the hand and frontlets between the eyes keep Yahuah's deliverance and law in deed and thought; the counterfeit is the beast's mark on hand and forehead (Rev 13:16).
"They gave me also gall for my meat" (Ps 69:21): bitter poison given to the suffering righteous one, fulfilled when Yahushua was offered vinegar mingled with gall (Matt 27:34).

also.meaning: Bitter poison of apostasy, a root bearing gall and wormwood (Deut 29:18); given to Messiah for meat (Ps 69:21; Matt 27:34); Simon the sorcerer was "in the gall of bitterness" (Acts 8:23).

words.meaning: The blessing is set on Gerizim and the curse on Ebal, two mountains facing each other: life and death set before Israel to choose (Deut 30:19).
Giants in the land are the great obstacle unbelief magnifies; Caleb, who wholly followed Yahuah, took the Anakim's mountain (Josh 14:12).

also.meaning: Giants made the spies 'as grasshoppers' (Num 13:33); Goliath stood six cubits and a span with a 600-shekel spearhead, his kin had six fingers and six toes (2 Sam 21:20), man's measure set against Yahuah and felled by one stone.

words.meaning: Yahuah's glory filled the finished tabernacle so Moses could not enter (Exod 40:34-35); it departed the temple in Ezekiel (Ezek 10:18), was beheld in the Son (John 1:14), and lights the city (Rev 21:23).
Goshen is the land set apart where the plagues do not fall, the picture of Yahuah putting a division between His people and the world under judgment (Exod 8:23).
The ten spies saw themselves as grasshoppers before the giants; Isaiah reverses it: the inhabitants of the earth are as grasshoppers before Yahuah (Isa 40:22).

also.meaning: The grasshopper is smallness and frailty: the spies saw themselves as grasshoppers (Num 13:33), earth's inhabitants are grasshoppers before Yahuah (Isa 40:22), and in old age even a grasshopper is a burden (Eccl 12:5).
The grasshoppers eating the latter growth are the first threatened judgment; at Amos's plea "Yahuah repented for this" (Amos 7:3) — intercession standing in the breach.

words.meaning: Hail mingled with fire is Yahuah's weapon from His storehouse (Job 38:22-23); it sweeps away the refuge of lies (Isa 28:17) and returns in the trumpets and bowls.

The Nazirite's uncut hair was the sign of separation to Yahuah (Num 6:5); Samson's strength left when the seven locks were shaved and returned as it 'began to grow again' (Judg 16:22), while Absalom's heavy hair became his snare in the oak (2 Sam 18:9).

also.meaning: Yahuah's minute care: "there shall not one hair of his head fall" (1 Sam 14:45; Acts 27:34), the very hairs of the head are all numbered (Matt 10:30); the Nazirite's uncut hair marked separation (Num 6:5).

Shaved and divided by weight: a third burned, a third struck with the sword, a third scattered to the wind (Ezek 5:12) - the city's people by pestilence, sword and exile; a few hairs bound in the skirts as the remnant.

words.meaning: He that is hanged is accursed of Elohim; Messiah redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, hanged on a tree (Gal 3:13).
The feast of harvest (Exod 23:16) becomes the gathering of people: the harvest is plenteous (Matt 9:37), and "the harvest is the end of the world; the reapers are the angels" (Matt 13:39).

Authority and order: Israel made the head and not the tail (Deut 28:13); "the head of every man is Messiah... and the head of Messiah is Elohim" (1 Cor 11:3); Messiah is head of the body, the assembly (Col 1:18).

also.meaning: The leopard's four heads are the empire divided "toward the four winds of heaven" (Dan 11:4), the four kingdoms of Dan 8:22; Rev 17:10 likewise reads heads as kings.

words.meaning: The new covenant writes Yahuah's Torah "in their inward parts" and "in their hearts" (Jer 31:33) - the stony heart replaced with a heart of flesh so they walk in His statutes (Ezek 36:26-27).

also.meaning: The beast stood upright and given a man's heart shows a kingdom humbled from beastly pride to sense (Dan 7:4), as Nebuchadnezzar's understanding returned (Dan 4:34); the reverse of the beast's heart given in Dan 4:16.

words.meaning: The fringe with a cord of blue given to look upon and remember all the commandments of Yahuah to do them (Num 15:39); the sick touched the hem of Messiah's garment and were healed (Matt 14:36).

also.meaning: The robe's lower edge carrying bells and pomegranates (Exod 28:33); the anointing runs "down to the skirts of his garments" (Ps 133:2), and the unclean woman was healed touching the hem of Yahushua's garment (Matt 9:20).

words.meaning: Honey from the rock and oil from the flint is Yahuah's abundance from unlikely places; His judgments are sweeter than honey (Ps 19:10).

also.meaning: Honey in the lion's carcase gave Samson's riddle, 'out of the strong came forth sweetness' (Judg 14:14); Yahuah's judgments are 'sweeter also than honey' (Ps 19:10), and the eaten scroll is sweet as honey in the mouth (Ezek 3:3; Rev 10:9).

Honey is sweetness and plenty: Yahuah's judgments are "sweeter also than honey" (Ps 19:10; 119:103), yet the strange woman's lips also drip as a honeycomb (Prov 5:3), and too much honey brings vomiting (Prov 25:16).

The sweetness of the good land (Exod 3:8) and of Yahuah's judgments and words, "sweeter also than honey" (Ps 19:10; 119:103); the eaten scroll is sweet as honey in the mouth and bitter in the belly (Ezek 3:3; Rev 10:9-10).
The eaten roll was "in my mouth as honey for sweetness" (Ezek 3:3) - Yahuah's word sweet to the one who takes it in, though its message is woe (Ps 19:10; Rev 10:10).

words.meaning: The lowly hyssop bundle applies the blood; it becomes the cleansing plant of purification (Ps 51:7), and hyssop lifts the vinegar to Messiah at His death (John 19:29).

also.meaning: The humble plant dipped to apply blood and water (Exod 12:22; Num 19:18); "purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean" (Ps 51:7), and hyssop lifted vinegar to Yahushua's mouth (John 19:29).
Hyssop applied the blood at Pesach and the water of cleansing (Exod 12:22; Num 19:18); "purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean" (Ps 51:7) asks for that cleansing for sin.

words.meaning: An idol set at the north gate of the altar "which provoketh to jealousy" (Ezek 8:3-5) - idolatry planted in Yahuah's own house, driving Him far from His sanctuary (8:6).
Unbreakable hardness of judgment - a yoke of iron for those who refuse Yahuah's service (Deut 28:48; Jer 28:14); the iron pan of siege (Ezek 4:3); the rod of iron (Rev 2:27).

also.meaning: The iron legs are the fourth kingdom, "strong as iron" that "breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things" (Dan 2:40), the same power as the fourth beast with great iron teeth (Dan 7:7), read historically as Rome.

words.meaning: Egypt is the iron furnace from which Yahuah took Israel to be His inheritance; the furnace is affliction that refines (Isa 48:10).
Yahuah's covenant people are a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; Revelation applies it to those washed in the Lamb's blood (Rev 1:6).

"Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set" (Prov 22:28): the boundary of inheritance Yahuah gave; moving it is theft from the fatherless (Prov 23:10) and a curse on Israel's princes (Hos 5:10).

Forbidden in altar offerings (Lev 2:11); Yahushua interprets leaven as teaching that corrupts (Matt 16:12), Paul as "malice and wickedness" that spreads (1 Cor 5:8) — yet leavened loaves were waved at Shavuot (Lev 23:17).

also.meaning: Spreading corruption put out at Hag HaMatzot (Exod 12:15): leaven is the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees (Matt 16:12), malice and wickedness (1 Cor 5:8); a little leaven leavens the whole lump (Gal 5:9).

lexicon.title: Unleavened Bread of Sincerity and Truth

words.meaning: Leprosy on Moses' hand and on Miriam for speaking against Yahuah's servant pictures sin's defilement that only Yahuah can cleanse; Yahushua touched and cleansed lepers (Matt 8:3).

also.meaning: A spreading uncleanness that put a man outside the camp crying "Unclean, unclean" (Lev 13:45-46); Scripture shows it striking Miriam, Gehazi and Uzziah for sin, and Yahushua's touch cleansing it (Matt 8:3).

The defiling disease that put a man outside the camp (Lev 13:46); Naaman's leprosy left him in Jordan while Gehazi's covetousness brought it on him (2 Kgs 5:27), and it rose on Uzziah's forehead when he burned incense against the Torah (2 Chr 26:19).

Uncleanness that puts a man outside the camp (Lev 13:46), sent as judgment on pride (Num 12:10); Naaman washed and was cleansed (2 Kgs 5:14), and Messiah touched the leper and made him clean (Matt 8:3).

words.meaning: Lice from the dust were the sign the magicians could not copy, forcing them to confess "this is the finger of Elohim" (Exod 8:19), the limit of counterfeit power.

The creatures "ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning" (Ezek 1:14) - the speed and blaze of Yahuah's presence, as at Sinai (Exod 19:16); Messiah's coming as lightning (Matt 24:27).

also.meaning: A face "as the appearance of lightning" shows the brightness of Yahuah's messenger, the same look as the angel at the tomb (Matt 28:3).

words.meaning: Blood on the upper doorpost completes the marked doorway; the house under the blood is the only safe place on the night of judgment (Exod 12:22-23).
Locusts that cover the face of the earth and eat every green thing are Yahuah's devouring army (Joel 2:25); Revelation's locusts from the pit carry the same image.

also.meaning: Plague of judgment on Egypt (Exod 10:4) yet listed clean to eat (Lev 11:22), food of John the Immerser (Matt 3:4); as a swarm it pictures devouring armies (Joel 1:4; Rev 9:3).
The locust is Yahuah's invading army stripping the land (Joel 2:25), the eighth plague of Egypt reused for judgment on His own people, and the locusts of the fifth trumpet (Rev 9:3).

words.meaning: Loins girded at the Pesach meal show readiness to march; Yahushua says let your loins be girded, and the believer's loins are girded with truth (Luke 12:35; Eph 6:14).

Bread from heaven, gathered daily, teaches that man lives by every word out of Yahuah's mouth (Deut 8:3); Yahushua names Himself the bread from heaven, and the overcomer receives hidden manna (Rev 2:17).
Bitter waters three days into the wilderness test Israel; where Yahuah is obeyed He heals: I am Yahuah that heals you (Exod 15:26).
Moses struck the rock twice when told to speak to it and so did not hallow Yahuah before the people; the rock, smitten once, is afterward spoken to.
At midnight Yahuah passed through Egypt; midnight marks the sudden hour of judgment and of the bridegroom's cry (Matt 25:6).
A land flowing with milk and honey is the promised rest of abundance; Isaiah invites all to buy wine and milk without price (Isa 55:1).

A man's means of life, not to be taken as pledge (Deut 24:6); a great millstone about the neck pictures the judgment on one who stumbles a little one (Matt 18:6), and Babylon cast down like a millstone (Rev 18:21).

also.meaning: A woman cast a piece of millstone from the tower and broke Abimelech's skull (Judg 9:53); Scripture uses the millstone for sudden, total overthrow, as Babylon thrown down 'like a great millstone' cast into the sea (Rev 18:21).
The silencing of the millstones and the candle marks a land laid waste (Jer 25:10); a stone bound to the book and sunk in Euphrates: "thus shall Babylon sink" (Jer 51:63-64; Rev 18:21).

words.meaning: Sinai, the mountain of the covenant, burned with fire; Hebrews contrasts the mount that might be touched with Mount Zion and the heavenly Jerusalem (Heb 12:18-22).

also.meaning: Yahuah's house exalted above the hills, all nations flowing to it (Isa 2:2) - His kingdom that fills the earth (Dan 2:35); Babylon is the destroying mountain made a burnt mountain (Jer 51:25).

The stone "became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth" (Dan 2:35) — Yahuah's kingdom; the mountain of Yahuah's house exalted above the hills (Mic 4:1) is the same Zion that believers have come to (Heb 12:22).

A kingdom: the mountain of Yahuah's house exalted (Isa 2:2), the stone becoming a great mountain (Dan 2:35); "the seven heads are seven mountains" (Rev 17:9), and belief removes mountains (Matt 17:20).

lexicon.title: Burning Mountain Cast into the Sea
Mount Sinai That Might Be Touched

words.meaning: The murrain on Egypt's livestock is Yahuah's hand on their wealth and gods; pestilence becomes a standing covenant curse (Deut 28:21) and one of the sore judgments (Ezek 14:21; Rev 6:8).
The ox that treads out the corn is not muzzled; Paul applies it to the laborer in the word being worthy of his reward (1 Cor 9:9; 1 Tim 5:18).

The bronze serpent lifted up for healing became an idol Israel burned incense to, and Hezekiah broke it in pieces, calling it Nehushtan, 'a piece of brass' (2 Kgs 18:4); the lifting up itself points to Messiah lifted up (John 3:14).
As an eagle stirs her nest and bears the young on her wings, so Yahuah alone led Israel; the hen gathering her chickens carries the same care (Matt 23:37).

lexicon.title: Two Wings of a Great Eagle

words.meaning: The patient laborer whom Torah protects, applied to those who labor in the word (Deut 25:4; 1 Cor 9:9); "the ox knoweth his owner" while Israel does not (Isa 1:3); one face of the living creatures (Ezek 1:10).

also.meaning: The working beast whose mouth must not be muzzled (Deut 25:4), a command Paul applies to those who labor in the word, "for our sakes, no doubt, this is written" (1 Cor 9:10), showing the Law still teaching.

words.meaning: Palms at Elim mark the oasis of rest; palm branches mark rejoicing and victory, the righteous flourishing like the palm tree (Ps 92:12; Rev 7:9).

also.meaning: Palm fronds taken to rejoice before Yahuah at Sukkot (Lev 23:40); "the righteous shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps 92:12), palms greeted Yahushua (John 12:13), and the great multitude holds them (Rev 7:9).

The rejoicing branch of Sukkot (Lev 23:40): the righteous flourish like the palm (Ps 92:12); palms greet Messiah entering Jerusalem (John 12:13) and fill the hands of the great multitude before the throne (Rev 7:9).
"I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands" (Isa 49:16) - Zion never forgotten, more surely remembered than a nursing child by its mother (Isa 49:15).

words.meaning: "I am Yahuah that healeth thee" (Exod 15:26); "is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there?" (Jer 8:22); Messiah came as physician to the sick, calling sinners to repentance (Matt 9:12-13).
The ten plagues are Yahuah's judgments on Egypt and all its gods (Exod 12:12); Revelation's seven last plagues repeat the pattern on Babylon, and the call is to come out lest you receive her plagues.
Yahuah plants His people in the mountain of His inheritance, the place He made to dwell in; every plant He has not planted will be rooted up (Matt 15:13).
The golden pot of manna kept before the testimony as a memorial of Yahuah's wilderness bread (Exod 16:33; Heb 9:4); the overcomer is promised the hidden manna (Rev 2:17).

also.meaning: A seething pot facing from the north: "Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land" (Jer 1:13-14); in that day every pot in Jerusalem is holy (Zech 14:21).

words.meaning: Yahuah raises a prophet like Moses and puts His words in his mouth; Peter identifies Him as Yahushua, and whoever will not hear Him is cut off (Acts 3:22-23).
Quail given to lusting Israel came with a plague; He gave them their request but sent leanness into their soul (Ps 106:15), the graves of craving at Kibroth-hattaavah.
Rain in its season follows obedience and is shut up for idolatry; the early and latter rain picture Yahuah's coming and the outpouring (Hos 6:3; Joel 2:23; Jas 5:7).

also.meaning: Yahuah's word and teaching coming down: "my doctrine shall drop as the rain" (Deut 32:2); as rain does not return void, neither does His word (Isa 55:10-11); "showers of blessing" (Ezek 34:26).

Yahuah's timely blessing on obedience (Deut 11:14): He comes as the latter and former rain (Hos 6:3), and the husbandman waits patiently for the early and latter rain as believers wait for the Master's coming (Jas 5:7-8).

Yahuah's coming "as the rain, as the latter and former rain" (Hos 6:3) is His refreshing of the land and people; in Joel the rains lead into the pouring out of His spirit (Joel 2:23, 28), fulfilled at Shavuot.

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: Passing through the Red Sea is Israel's immersion unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea (1 Cor 10:2): death left behind, the enemy drowned, a new life on the far shore.

lexicon.title: Immersed unto Moses in Cloud and Sea

words.meaning: Six appointed cities where the manslayer fled from the avenger of blood and lived until the high priest's death (Josh 20:6); Heb 6:18 uses the picture for those who 'fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us'.
Yahuah is the Rock whose work is perfect (Deut 32:4); the rock smitten at Horeb gave water, and that spiritual Rock that followed them was Messiah, smitten once (1 Cor 10:4).

also.meaning: Yahuah is the Rock: 'who is a rock, save our Elohim?' (2 Sam 22:32); David names Him rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn and high tower (2 Sam 22:2-3), and the rock that gave water in the wilderness is applied to Messiah (1 Cor 10:4).
Yahuah is the Rock, perfect in His work (Deut 32:4), and "who is a rock save our Elohim?" (Ps 18:31); the smitten rock that gave Israel water in the wilderness pictured Messiah (1 Cor 10:4).
Yahuah is the Rock, "his work is perfect" (Deut 32:4); "in Yah Yahuah is everlasting strength" (Isa 26:4); "the rock whence ye are hewn" is Abraham (Isa 51:1-2).

Yahuah is the Rock whose work is perfect (Deut 32:4); the smitten rock in the wilderness gave water and "that Rock was Messiah" (1 Cor 10:4); the wise build on the rock of hearing and doing his sayings (Matt 7:24).

words.meaning: Moses' rod becomes the rod of Elohim, the sign of delegated authority by which Yahuah works; the rod of His strength is sent out of Zion (Ps 110:2).

also.meaning: Yahuah's delegated authority: Moses' rod of signs (Exod 4:17), Aaron's rod that budded proving the chosen priesthood (Num 17:8; Heb 9:4), the shepherd's comforting rod (Ps 23:4), and the rod of Messiah's mouth (Isa 11:4).

The shepherd's rod comforts and guards the sheep (Ps 23:4); the king's rod of iron breaks the rebellious nations like a potter's vessel (Ps 2:9; Rev 2:27); the father's rod corrects a son (Prov 13:24).

Assyria is "the rod of mine anger" (Isa 10:5), a chastening tool in Yahuah's hand; Messiah smites the earth "with the rod of his mouth" (Isa 11:4); Israel passes under the rod into the covenant (Ezek 20:37).

words.meaning: A root that bears gall and wormwood is the one turning to other gods; Hebrews warns against any root of bitterness springing up (Heb 12:15).

also.meaning: Two uses: the root bearing gall and wormwood, a heart turned from Yahuah (Deut 29:18; Heb 12:15 root of bitterness), and the holy root that bears the branches (Rom 11:16-18), Messiah the root of Jesse and of David (Isa 11:10; Rev 22:16).
"A root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek" (Isa 11:10) - Messiah, "the root and the offspring of David" (Rev 22:16).

words.meaning: Shoes removed on holy ground (Exod 3:5), worn for the Pesach departure (Exod 12:11), handed over to confirm redemption (Ruth 4:7); the returning son is given shoes (Luke 15:22), and feet are shod with the gospel of peace (Eph 6:15).

lexicon.title: The Prodigal's Robe, Ring and Sandals

words.meaning: Under the feet of the Elohim of Israel was a paved work of sapphire, as the body of heaven; the sapphire throne appears in Ezekiel and the stone in the new city's foundations.

also.meaning: The "paved work of a sapphire stone" under the feet of the Elohim of Israel (Exod 24:10) and the throne's likeness (Ezek 1:26), set in the breastplate (Exod 28:18); Zion's foundations are laid with sapphires (Isa 54:11; Rev 21:19).
The pavement under Yahuah's feet seen at Sinai (Exod 24:10) and the throne above the firmament (Ezek 1:26); redeemed Zion's foundations laid with sapphires (Isa 54:11; Rev 21:19).

The pavement under the feet of the Elohim of Israel (Exod 24:10) and the appearance of the throne (Ezek 1:26); Yahuah lays the afflicted city's foundations with sapphires (Isa 54:11), the second foundation of the new city (Rev 21:19).

words.meaning: The scepter rising out of Israel is the royal rod of the promised King who smites the corners of Moab; it is the scepter of righteousness of Ps 45.
The wilderness of fiery serpents and scorpions is the place of danger Yahuah led them through; Yahushua gives power to tread on serpents and scorpions (Luke 10:19).

also.meaning: "Thou dost dwell among scorpions" (Ezek 2:6) - the stinging hostility of a rebellious house; power given over scorpions (Luke 10:19).

The stinging power of hostile people and spirits: the wilderness of scorpions (Deut 8:15), Ezekiel dwelling among scorpions, a rebellious house (Ezek 2:6); Messiah gives power to tread on serpents and scorpions (Luke 10:19).

words.meaning: Seventy elders shared Moses' spirit (Num 11:25) and seventy were sent ahead of Messiah (Luke 10:1); Daniel's seventy weeks were fulfilled in Messiah (Dan 9:24), and forgiveness is to be seventy times seven (Matt 18:22).

also.meaning: The set term of Babylon's rule and Judah's captivity while the land kept its sabbaths (Jer 25:11; 2 Chr 36:21); Daniel's prayer at their close received the seventy weeks, now fulfilled (Dan 9:2, 24).

words.meaning: Shoes removed mark holy ground before Yahuah; shoes on the feet mark readiness to go out at Pesach, and the feet shod with the gospel of peace (Eph 6:15).

also.meaning: Loosed on holy ground in Yahuah's presence (Josh 5:15), and plucked off and handed over to confirm the transfer of a redemption right (Ruth 4:7); the feet are later shod with the preparation of the good news of peace (Eph 6:15).

lexicon.title: The Prodigal's Robe, Ring and Sandals

words.meaning: The horn heard at Sinai (Exod 19:16), blown on Yom Teruah (Lev 23:24) and on Yom Kippur to proclaim jubilee (Lev 25:9); "the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised" (1 Cor 15:52).

also.meaning: The ram's-horn trumpet heard at Sinai went before the ark at Jericho, brought the walls down at the long blast (Josh 6:5) and sounded Gideon's attack; it is the alarm of the day of Yahuah (Joel 2:1) and the trumpet of the gathering (1 Thes 4:16).

words.meaning: "The light of the body is the eye": a single (generous, undivided) eye fills the body with light, an evil (grudging) eye with darkness (Matt 6:22-23), as the evil eye begrudges the poor brother (Deut 15:9).

A snare is a hidden trap: foreign gods are a snare to Israel (Exod 23:33), the fear of man brings a snare (Prov 29:25), and Yahuah delivers His people from the snare of the fowler like an escaped bird (Ps 91:3; 124:7).

also.meaning: The gods of the nations become a snare (Exod 23:33); the Stone is "for a gin and for a snare" to Jerusalem (Isa 8:14) - sudden capture of the unwatchful (Luke 21:35).

The hidden trap: the nations' gods will be a snare to Israel (Exod 23:33); their table made a snare (Ps 69:22; Rom 11:9), the snare of the devil (1 Tim 3:7), and the desire to be rich falls into a snare (1 Tim 6:9).

words.meaning: "What is man... and the son of man" (Ps 8:4-6): made a little lower than the angels and given all things under his feet, which Hebrews applies to Yahushua the man (Heb 2:6-9); Yahuah strengthens the son of man at His right hand (Ps 80:17).

also.meaning: One like a son of man comes with clouds to the Ancient of Days and is given dominion (Dan 7:13-14); Yahushua takes the title (Matt 26:64), and the kingdom is shared with "the saints of the most High" (Dan 7:27).

lexicon.title: Son of Man on the White Cloud

words.meaning: The song of the sea praises Yahuah as deliverer; the song of Deut 32 is a witness against Israel; the victors sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb (Rev 15:3).

also.meaning: A new song answers a new deliverance: Moses' song at the sea (Exod 15:1), the new song Yahuah puts in the mouth of the one drawn from the pit (Ps 40:3), and the new song of the redeemed before the throne (Rev 5:9; 14:3).

lexicon.title: Song of Moses and the Lamb

words.meaning: "I hid not my face from shame and spitting" (Isa 50:6) - the deepest public contempt, willingly borne by the Servant (Matt 26:67).

Covenant cleansing applied: Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant (Exod 24:8); Messiah's servant shall sprinkle many nations (Isa 52:15), clean water is sprinkled (Ezek 36:25), and believers come to the blood of sprinkling (Heb 12:24).

also.meaning: Blood sprinkled seven times before the veil and on the mercy seat (Lev 4:6; 16:14) to cleanse; the servant "shall sprinkle many nations" (Isa 52:15), and believers come to "the blood of sprinkling" (Heb 12:24).
"So shall he sprinkle many nations" (Isa 52:15); "then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean" (Ezek 36:25) - priestly cleansing extended to the nations.

words.meaning: What fire consumes: Yahuah's wrath consumes enemies as stubble (Exod 15:7), the proud are stubble in the burning day (Mal 4:1), and works of wood, hay and stubble are burned while the builder is saved "so as by fire" (1 Cor 3:15).

also.meaning: "The house of Jacob shall be a fire ... and the house of Esau for stubble" (Obad 18) — the proud burned with nothing left, as in Mal 4:1.

words.meaning: Tables of stone written by Yahuah's finger hold the covenant words; the new covenant writes the same law on fleshy tables of the heart (Jer 31:33; 2 Cor 3:3).

also.meaning: The tables of the covenant written with the finger of Elohim (Exod 31:18) kept in the ark (Heb 9:4); under the new covenant the same Law is written in fleshy tables of the heart (2 Cor 3:3; Jer 31:33).

The gold-covered table bearing bread before Yahuah's face; Scripture uses His table for fellowship He provides (Ps 23:5) and contrasts "the table of Yahuah" with the table of devils (Mal 1:7; 1 Cor 10:21).

Lame Mephibosheth, of a fallen house, 'did eat continually at the king's table' for Jonathan's covenant (2 Sam 9:13), and captive Jehoiachin was raised to eat before the king (2 Kgs 25:29); the poor, maimed and lame are brought in to the supper (Luke 14:21).

"Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it" (Hab 2:2) — the vision set down plainly for an appointed time, which "will surely come, it will not tarry" (Hab 2:3; Heb 10:37).

words.meaning: The commandments once written on tables of stone (Exod 24:12) are to be written "upon the table of thine heart" (Prov 3:3; 7:3), the new-covenant law within (Jer 31:33; 2 Cor 3:3).

Scripture interprets it: "the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail" (Isa 9:15); the locusts' and horses' tails hurt with stings and serpents' heads (Rev 9:10, 19), and the dragon's tail draws a third of the stars (Rev 12:4).
Several uses shown in Scripture: the ten words of the covenant (Exod 34:28), ten days of testing (Dan 1:12; Rev 2:10), and ten horns, which "are ten kings" (Dan 7:24; Rev 17:12).

Scripture uses a thousand for a full, unbounded measure: the cattle on a thousand hills, the word commanded to a thousand generations (Ps 50:10; 105:8; Deut 7:9), and a thousand years as a day before Yahuah (Ps 90:4; 2 Pet 3:8).
Thunders, lightnings and voices at Sinai are Yahuah's voice in giving the covenant; the same set issues from the throne and the opened temple (Rev 4:5; 11:19).
Miriam's timbrel marks the women's song of deliverance after the sea; the restored virgin of Israel takes up her tabrets again (Jer 31:4).

lexicon.title: Song of Moses and the Lamb

words.meaning: Israel obeying the covenant is Yahuah's peculiar treasure; Peter and Paul apply it to the redeemed, a people for His own possession (Titus 2:14; 1 Pet 2:9).

also.meaning: Israel is Yahuah's peculiar treasure if they keep His covenant (Exod 19:5; Mal 3:17); where a man's treasure is, his heart is (Matt 6:21); the treasure of light is carried in earthen vessels (2 Cor 4:7).

words.meaning: Scripture uses the tree for a man and the trees for people and their rulers: "the tree of the field is man's life" (Deut 20:19); in Jotham's parable "the trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them," and the olive, fig, vine and bramble are men offered the rule (Judg 9:8-15); the great tree is the king himself, "It is thou, O king" (Dan 4:20-22), and the faithful are "trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahuah" (Isa 61:3).

also.meaning: The tree Yahuah showed Moses, cast into the bitter waters of Marah, made them sweet (Exod 15:25), at the place where He gave Israel a statute and named Himself their healer (Exod 15:26).

The place of the curse: "he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim" (Deut 21:23); Messiah was made a curse for us, hanged on a tree (Gal 3:13), bearing sins in his own body on the tree, the price Yahuah gave (1 Pet 2:24).
The one who delights in Yahuah's law is a tree planted by rivers of water that bears fruit in season (Ps 1:3; Jer 17:8); wisdom is a tree of life to those who lay hold on her (Prov 3:18).
"Blessed is the man that trusteth in Yahuah... he shall be as a tree planted by the waters" that does not cease yielding fruit (Jer 17:7-8); the trees by Ezekiel's river (Ezek 47:12).

The great tree reaching heaven, sheltering beasts and birds, is the king and his kingdom: "It is thou, O king" (Dan 4:22); Assyria is the same cedar in Ezek 31, and the mustard tree's birds echo it (Matt 13:32).

words.meaning: The trumpet exceeding loud at Sinai announces Yahuah's coming down and the giving of the covenant; trumpets call assemblies and announce judgment throughout Scripture (Rev 8:2).

also.meaning: The watchman's warning (Ezek 33:3-6) and the prophet's cry: "lift up thy voice like a trumpet" (Isa 58:1); the great trumpet gathers the outcasts to worship in Jerusalem (Isa 27:13).

Yahuah's summons and alarm: the shofar at Sinai (Exod 19:16) and Yom Teruah (Lev 23:24), the alarm of war (Joel 2:1); the last trump raises the dead (1 Cor 15:52), and the seven trumpets sound through the assembly age (Rev 8-11).

Two silver trumpets to gather the assembly, move the camps and sound alarm for war, "and ye shall be remembered before Yahuah" (Num 10:9); seven trumpets sound through the assembly age in Revelation (Rev 8:2).

words.meaning: Not plowing with an ox and an ass together, nor sowing mixed seed, teaches separation; Paul applies it: be not unequally yoked with unbelievers (2 Cor 6:14).
The strength of the wild ox is the strength Yahuah gives Israel out of Egypt; Joseph's horns are the horns of the wild ox pushing the peoples (Deut 33:17).

also.meaning: The re'em (wild ox) is untamable strength: Yahuah gives Israel such strength (Num 23:22), its horns threaten the suffering one in Ps 22:21, and the righteous man's horn is exalted like the unicorn's (Ps 92:10).

words.meaning: Bread without leaven, eaten in haste, is the bread of affliction (Deut 16:3); Paul makes it the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, the walk cleansed of malice (1 Cor 5:8).

also.meaning: Seven days of Hag HaMatzot eaten in remembrance of leaving Egypt (Lev 23:6; Deut 16:3); Paul keeps the feast "with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth" (1 Cor 5:8).

lexicon.title: Unleavened Bread of Sincerity and Truth

words.meaning: The enemy's vine is of Sodom and its grapes are gall, the fruit of a corrupt root, gathered for the winepress of wrath (Rev 14:19).

lexicon.title: Vine of the Earth and the Winepress

words.meaning: The night divided into watches: Yahuah looked on Egypt in the morning watch (Exod 14:24); "watchman, what of the night?" (Isa 21:11); servants watch, not knowing whether the master comes at even, midnight, cockcrowing or morning (Mark 13:35).
The commandment is not in heaven nor beyond the sea but very nigh, in the mouth and heart, that you may do it; Paul applies it to the word of belief (Rom 10:8).
Bitterness of idolatry and its judgment - "I will feed them... with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink" (Jer 9:15); the star Wormwood turns the waters bitter (Rev 8:11).

The golden altar before the veil where incense burned continually and atoning blood touched its horns yearly (Exod 30:10); in Revelation it stands before the throne, mingling incense with prayers (Rev 8:3).

Holy compounded oil that set apart priest, tent and vessels (Exod 30:26-30), never to be copied for common flesh (Exod 30:32); Messiah means Anointed, and Yahuah's anointing abides in His people (Isa 61:1; 1 John 2:27).
"A false balance is abomination to Yahuah: but a just weight is his delight" (Prov 11:1); men are weighed in Yahuah's balance and found lighter than vanity (Ps 62:9; Dan 5:27).

The priests washed hands and feet at the laver before service lest they die (Exod 30:20); Messiah pours water into a basin and washes the disciples' feet, "If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me" (John 13:8).

Golden bells whose sound was heard when the high priest went in and came out, "that he die not" (Exod 28:35) — the living service heard by the people; in the latter day even horse bells read "HOLINESS UNTO YAHUAH" (Zech 14:20).

Tenth breastplate stone (Exod 28:20); the wheels of the throne-chariot gleam "like unto the colour of a beryl" (Ezek 1:16), the heavenly messenger's body was like beryl (Dan 10:6), and it is the eighth foundation (Rev 21:20).

also.meaning: The wheels' appearance "like unto the colour of a beryl" (Ezek 1:16) - a stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20) and of the heavenly city's foundations (Rev 21:20).

A breastplate stone bearing a tribe's name (Exod 28:20, 21); the wheels of Ezekiel's vision had the colour of beryl (Ezek 1:16), the man in linen's body was like beryl (Dan 10:6), and it is the eighth foundation (Rev 21:20).
A body like the beryl (tarshish) ties the messenger to the wheels of Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 1:16) and to a stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20) — heavenly glory in precious-stone form.

words.meaning: Holy water with dust from the floor that tested a suspected wife (Num 5:17-27), exposing hidden unfaithfulness; Israel's own backsliding is "an evil thing and bitter" (Jer 2:19), and the unfaithful drink judgment (Rev 8:11).

Upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, joined into one wall of the dwelling (Exod 26:15-29); the assembly is likewise "fitly framed together" into a holy temple and built as living stones (Eph 2:21-22; 1 Pet 2:5).

Branches of thick trees taken at Sukkot (Lev 23:40), gathered with myrtle in Nehemiah's feast (Neh 8:15); "instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree" (Isa 55:13), and Yahuah's messenger stood among myrtles (Zech 1:8).

The square of twelve stones bearing Israel's names "upon his heart" before Yahuah continually (Exod 28:29); Yahuah's own breastplate is righteousness (Isa 59:17), given to His people as armor (Eph 6:14).

also.meaning: The high priest bore Israel's names on his heart in the breastplate of judgment (Exod 28:29); Yahuah puts on righteousness as a breastplate (Isa 59:17), and the believer the breastplate of righteousness, of belief and love (Eph 6:14; 1 Thess 5:8).
Yahuah puts on righteousness as a breastplate and "an helmet of salvation upon his head" when no intercessor is found (Isa 59:16-17) - armor later given to His people (Eph 6:14-17).

words.meaning: Linen undergarments "to cover their nakedness," so the priest bear not iniquity and die (Exod 28:42-43); shame of nakedness must be covered before Yahuah's altar (Exod 20:26; Rev 3:18).

The largest offering, required for the anointed priest's and the whole congregation's sin (Lev 4:3,14) and offered seventy times at Sukkot (Num 29:12-34); Hosea's "calves of our lips" turns sacrifice into confession (Hos 14:2).

An unclean beast (Lev 11:4) and a measure of earthly wealth; a camel through a needle's eye shows a rich man cannot enter the kingdom by his own means (Matt 19:24), and swallowing a camel shows ignoring weightier uncleanness (Matt 23:24).

The camp held Yahuah's dwelling and was kept clean "that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell" (Num 5:3); the sin offering burned without it, so "let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp" (Heb 13:13).

also.meaning: The sin offering's body burned without the camp (Lev 16:27); so Messiah suffered without the gate, "let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach" (Heb 13:12-13).

words.meaning: Cedar wood with scarlet and hyssop in the leper's cleansing and heifer's burning (Lev 14:4; Num 19:6); the righteous "shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon" (Ps 92:12), and Yahuah plants a tender cedar twig on a high mountain (Ezek 17:22).

also.meaning: The tall tree of Lebanon that lined the whole temple 'there was no stone seen' (1 Kgs 6:18); a figure of loftiness and of the righteous who flourish (Ps 92:12), and of the tender cedar twig Yahuah plants on a high mountain (Ezek 17:22-23).
Lofty royal houses and proud nations (Assyria, Ezek 31:3; David's line, Ezek 17:3); Yahuah plants a tender twig of the high cedar that becomes a goodly cedar sheltering every bird (Ezek 17:23).

words.meaning: The "continual burnt offering" morning and evening at the door of the tent (Exod 29:42), the hours of prayer (Acts 3:1); Daniel's little horn takes away "the daily" (Dan 8:11), and the priests stood daily offering what could never take away sin (Heb 10:11).
The conies are "but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks" (Prov 30:26): the weak are safe because their dwelling is in the rock (Ps 104:18).

The corner of the field left unreaped, set even within the feast law of Shavuot, "for the poor, and to the stranger" (Lev 23:22); Ruth the stranger gleaned there and entered the line of David (Ruth 2).

also.meaning: "An end is come upon the four corners of the land" (Ezek 7:2) - judgment reaching the whole land; the outcasts gathered "from the four corners of the earth" (Isa 11:12).

words.meaning: The linen-walled yard around the tent holding altar and laver (Exod 27:9); longed for by the psalmist (Ps 84:2,10), and in Revelation the court outside the temple is given to the nations to be trodden (Rev 11:2).

lexicon.title: Outer Court and the Holy City Trampled

words.meaning: The ten woven curtains of the dwelling (Exod 26:1); Zion is told to "stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations" (Isa 54:2), while torn curtains picture a ruined house (Jer 4:20; 10:20).
Head of the breastplate's second row (Exod 28:18); the rainbow round the throne is "in sight like unto an emerald" (Rev 4:3), and emerald is the fourth foundation of the city (Rev 21:19).

also.meaning: A stone of the high priest's breastplate bearing a tribe's name (Exod 28:18, 21); the rainbow round about the throne is "in sight like unto an emerald" (Rev 4:3), and it is the fourth foundation (Rev 21:19).

words.meaning: The high priest's gold-and-colors vest bearing the tribes on its shoulders (Exod 28:12); Samuel and David wore linen ephods in service, while Gideon's ephod became "a snare" (Judg 8:27).
"All the fat is Yahuah's" (Lev 3:16), the choicest part burned to Him and never eaten; Eli's sons took it for themselves (1 Sam 2:16), and "to hearken than the fat of rams" is better (1 Sam 15:22).

Fifty days counted to Shavuot (Lev 23:16) and the fiftieth year of jubilee (Lev 25:10) — the count that ends in a new beginning of liberty and harvest; Shavuot "fully come" brought the outpouring (Acts 2:1).

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: The first sheaf waved at Bikkurim on the morrow after the sabbath (Lev 23:11): Messiah risen is the firstfruits of them that slept (1 Cor 15:20), and his people are a kind of firstfruits of His creatures (Jas 1:18).

Finely ground grain of the meal offering and showbread (Lev 2:1; 24:5); "bread corn is bruised" before it becomes bread (Isa 28:28), and the grain of wheat must fall and die to bear fruit (John 12:24).

lexicon.title: Grain of Wheat Falling into the Ground

words.meaning: Where ownership and character show - Aaron's "Holiness to Yahuah" plate (Exod 28:38), Judah's whore's forehead (Jer 3:3), the prophet's hardened forehead (Ezek 3:8), and the mark on those who sigh (Ezek 9:4).

The high priest went within the veil alone on Yom Kippur (Lev 16:12-15); Messiah entered as forerunner for us, made a high priest after the order of Melchizedek, so others may follow (Heb 6:20; 10:19-20).
The altar, the breastplate and Ezekiel's holy oblation are all foursquare (Ezek 48:20) - perfect proportion of what is set apart to Yahuah; the city "lieth foursquare" (Rev 21:16).
White incense set on the showbread "for a memorial" (Lev 24:7) and on the meal offering; prayer is set forth as incense (Ps 141:2), and frankincense was laid before the child Yahushua (Matt 2:11).

also.meaning: Pure incense offered to Yahuah (Exod 30:34; Lev 2:2); prayer set forth as incense (Ps 141:2); the nations bring gold and incense (Isa 60:6), fulfilled in the wise men's gifts (Matt 2:11).

lexicon.title: Golden Bowls of Incense (Prayers of the Saints)

words.meaning: The priest's embroidered sash binding the garments for service (Exod 28:39); "righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins" (Isa 11:5), and the Son of man is girt with a golden girdle (Rev 1:13).

also.meaning: "As the girdle cleaveth to the loins... so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel" (Jer 13:11) - hidden at Euphrates it was marred, as Judah's pride would be marred (Jer 13:9).

Bound readiness and closeness: "as the girdle cleaveth to the loins... so have I caused to cleave unto me... Israel" (Jer 13:11); righteousness is Messiah's girdle (Isa 11:5), truth the believer's (Eph 6:14); a golden girdle at the paps marks the high priest (Rev 1:13).

lexicon.title: Seven Angels in White Linen with Golden Sashes

words.meaning: The corners and fallen ears were left by Torah for the poor and the stranger (Lev 23:22); Ruth the Moabitess gleaned in Boaz's field under that provision, and the remnant is pictured as gleaning grapes left after the vintage (Isa 17:6).

also.meaning: The corners and gleanings left for the poor (Lev 19:9-10); the prophets use the two or three berries left after the shaking to picture the small remnant (Isa 17:6; 24:13).

words.meaning: Straining out a gnat while swallowing a camel (Matt 23:24) pictures scrupulous care over the smallest unclean thing (Lev 11:41-43) joined to neglect of judgment, mercy and belief, the weightier matters of the Law (Matt 23:23).
The tent of goats' hair stretched over the dwelling (Exod 26:7), from the animal of the sin offering (Lev 16:15); hair-cloth is the stuff of sackcloth and mourning (Isa 50:3; Rev 6:12).

Fruit of a "goodly" (hadar, splendid) tree, the first of the four kinds taken at Sukkot (Lev 23:40); Israel was called "a green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit" (Jer 11:16), and a good tree is known by its fruit (Matt 7:17).
The ransom "for his soul" given equally by rich and poor (Exod 30:15) — every soul valued the same before Yahuah; Yahushua paid the temple shekel for Peter and himself (Matt 17:27).

words.alt: door hanging, screen of the tent
words.meaning: The outer veil at the door of the tent, closing the holy place (Exod 26:36); this outer veil was rent from top to bottom at Messiah's death (Matt 27:51), opening the new and living way (Heb 10:20).
Covenant unfaithfulness - Israel "played the harlot" under every green tree (Jer 3:6), trusting her beauty and giving herself to the nations' gods (Ezek 16:15); the great harlot (Rev 17:1).

A portion "lifted up" and set apart to Yahuah from the people's gifts — the sanctuary materials themselves began as a terumah from willing hearts (Exod 25:2), and the Levites lifted a tithe of their tithe (Num 18:26).

words.alt: most holy place, holy of holies
words.meaning: The inner room of the ark, entered once a year with blood (Lev 16:2); Hebrews shows Messiah entering heaven itself "now to appear in the presence of Elohim for us" (Heb 9:24).

lexicon.title: Temple of God (Naos) and Its Worshipers

words.meaning: The first room holding lampstand, table and incense altar (Heb 9:2); Hebrews says while that first tabernacle stood the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest — "a figure for the time then present" (Heb 9:8-9).
Elders burning incense in the dark before creeping things portrayed on the wall, "every man in the chambers of his imagery", saying "Yahuah seeth us not" (Ezek 8:12) - hidden idolatry of the heart.
Holy perfume burned morning and evening before the veil (Exod 30:7-8); Scripture interprets it as the prayers of the saints rising before Yahuah (Ps 141:2; Rev 5:8; 8:3-4).

also.meaning: "Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense" (Ps 141:2): Scripture itself makes the incense the prayers of the saints (Rev 5:8; 8:4).

lexicon.title: Golden Bowls of Incense (Prayers of the Saints)

words.meaning: Last stone of the breastplate (Exod 28:20); the enthroned one is "like a jasper" (Rev 4:3), the city's light is "like a jasper stone, clear as crystal" (Rev 21:11), and it is the wall and first foundation.

The fiftieth year proclaiming "liberty throughout all the land," every man returning to his possession (Lev 25:10); Yahushua read Isaiah's "acceptable year of Yahuah" as fulfilled in their ears (Luke 4:18-21).

The kidneys with their fat were burned to Yahuah in the offerings (Lev 3:4); Scripture makes them the seat of hidden thought — Yahuah "trieth the hearts and reins" (Ps 7:9; Jer 17:10), and Messiah "searcheth the reins and hearts" (Rev 2:23).

The swelling bud on each lampstand branch between cup and flower, part of the growth pattern Aaron's dead rod showed when it "brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms" (Num 17:8) — life sprung from what was cut off.

The light-bearer, not the source: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet" (Ps 119:105), "Yahuah is my lamp" (2 Sam 22:29); disciples' lamp must not be hidden (Matt 5:15), and the virgins' lamps need oil (Matt 25:3-8).

also.meaning: Samuel was called 'ere the lamp of Elohim went out' (1 Sam 3:3); David is 'the light (lamp) of Israel' (2 Sam 21:17) and Yahuah keeps a lamp for David in Jerusalem (1 Kgs 11:36); in the city Yahuah's glory is the light and the Lamb is its lamp (Rev 21:23).

A lamp carries light from its source: Yahuah's word and commandment are a lamp (Ps 119:105; Prov 6:23); He ordained a lamp for His anointed (Ps 132:17), the virtuous woman's lamp goes not out by night (Prov 31:18), and the lamp of the wicked is put out (Prov 24:20).
Eyes as lamps of fire show piercing, searching sight (Dan 10:6), the same eyes "like a flame of fire" in Rev 1:14 that search the assemblies.

lexicon.title: Eyes Like a Flame of Fire

words.meaning: The seven-lamped light of the holy place, fed by pure oil (Exod 27:20); Zechariah ties its oil to Yahuah's spirit (Zech 4:6), and Revelation interprets the lampstands as the assemblies (Rev 1:20).

The bronze basin where priests washed hands and feet "that they die not" (Exod 30:20) before serving; the washing of water by the word (Eph 5:26) and "bodies washed with pure water" (Heb 10:22) answer it.

Lots cast over the two goats left the choice to Yahuah (Lev 16:8); "the lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of Yahuah" (Prov 16:33), and soldiers cast lots for Messiah's vesture (John 19:24).

also.meaning: "Thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" (Dan 12:13) — the allotted inheritance of the saints in light (Col 1:12), received at the resurrection.
The lot falling on Jonah shows that "the whole disposing thereof is of Yahuah" (Prov 16:33) — the hidden runaway exposed.

words.meaning: A gift of fine flour with oil and frankincense, no leaven or honey, seasoned with salt (Lev 2:1-13); bread offered alongside the blood, as the walk follows the covering — the daily bread of the commandments.

The golden lid covering the testimony, sprinkled with blood on Yom Kippur (Lev 16:14); the place of covering where Yahuah speaks, applied to Messiah "set forth to be a propitiation" (Rom 3:25, hilasterion).
Tithing garden herbs (Lev 27:30) was right, yet the weightier matters, judgment, mercy and belief, were neglected; "these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone" (Matt 23:23).

The bronze looking-glasses of the serving women made into the laver (Exod 38:8); the word is a glass showing a man his true face (Jas 1:23-25), in which believers behold Yahuah's glory and are changed (2 Cor 3:18).

also.meaning: The women's looking-glasses became the laver (Exod 38:8); now seen as through a glass darkly (1 Cor 13:12), beholding the Master's glory as in a glass (2 Cor 3:18); the hearer who forgets his face is not a doer of the perfect law (Jas 1:23-25).

words.meaning: The high priest's linen turban bearing the gold plate (Exod 28:37); Joshua the high priest is cleansed and given "a fair mitre upon his head" (Zech 3:5), while the profane prince is told "remove the diadem (mitsnepheth)" (Ezek 21:26).

Myrrh is in the holy anointing oil (Exod 30:23) and perfumes the King's garments (Ps 45:8); the beloved is a bundle of myrrh (Song 1:13), it was given at Yahushua's birth, and it wrapped His body at burial (Matt 2:11; John 19:39).

also.meaning: The chief spice of the holy anointing oil (Exod 30:23) and of the royal bridegroom's garments (Ps 45:8); brought to the child (Matt 2:11), offered on the stake (Mark 15:23), and brought for his burial (John 19:39).

words.meaning: One separated to Yahuah by vow, refusing the vine, razor and the dead, "the consecration of his Elohim is upon his head" (Num 6:7); Israel was rebuked for giving the Nazarites wine (Amos 2:12).
Everything built "after the pattern... shewed thee in the mount" (Exod 25:40); Hebrews reads the earthly sanctuary as an example and shadow of heavenly things (Heb 8:5).

also.meaning: "Shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern" (Ezek 43:10) - Yahuah's own plan for His dwelling, the copy of heavenly things (Heb 8:5).

lexicon.title: Temple of God (Naos) and Its Worshipers

words.meaning: The fellowship offering shared at one table by Yahuah, priest and worshipper (Lev 7:15); Yahuah made "peace through the blood of his cross" (Col 1:20), and Messiah "is our peace" (Eph 2:14).

lexicon.title: Bread and Wine of the Covenant Meal

words.meaning: The pelican of the wilderness and owl of the desert are birds of desolate ruins: the afflicted psalmist is like them (Ps 102:6), and they inhabit fallen cities under judgment (Isa 34:11; Zeph 2:14; Rev 18:2).

lexicon.title: Dwelling of Demons, Cage of Unclean Birds

words.meaning: The gold plate on Aaron's forehead engraved "HOLINESS TO YAHUAH," by which he bore "the iniquity of the holy things" (Exod 28:36-38); the redeemed bear the Father's name on their foreheads (Rev 14:1; 22:4).

Woven fruit alternating with the bells on the robe's hem (Exod 28:34); a fruit of the good land the spies carried back (Num 13:23; Deut 8:8), and an image of the bride's beauty (Song 4:3) — sound and fruit together.

also.meaning: Pomegranates hung on the high priest's hem and the temple pillars (Exod 28:33; 1 Kgs 7:18); in the Song they mark the bride's beauty and fruitful orchard (Song 4:3, 13).

words.meaning: As Yahuah was the Levites' portion instead of land (Num 18:20), the psalmists say "Yahuah is the portion of mine inheritance" and "my portion for ever" (Ps 16:5; 73:26).
Royal color woven into veil and garments (Exod 26:31); worn by kings (Judg 8:26), mocked onto Yahushua (John 19:2), and stolen by the harlot (Rev 17:4).

also.meaning: The color of royalty and wealth (Judg 8:26; Dan 5:29): the soldiers clothed Messiah in purple in mockery of his kingship (Mark 15:17), and the rich man and the harlot wear purple in their luxury (Luke 16:19; Rev 17:4).
