words.meaning: A spotless red heifer "upon which never came yoke," slain outside the camp, its ashes kept for the water of separation (Num 19:2-9); Hebrews contrasts its sanctifying ashes with Messiah's blood that purges the conscience (Heb 9:13-14).

The near kinsman had the right to buy back land and raise up the name of the dead (Ruth 4:5, 10); Yahuah calls Himself Israel's Redeemer (Isa 43:14), and the Son shared the same flesh and blood as his brethren, the near kinsman (Heb 2:11-14).

Blood and oil on the right ear, right thumb and right great toe of priest and cleansed leper (Exod 29:20; Lev 14:14) — hearing, work and walk consecrated; "the Master Yahuah hath opened mine ear" (Isa 50:5).

All-blue robe with a woven, bound neck "that it be not rent" (Exod 28:32); Yahuah clothes His people with "the robe of righteousness" (Isa 61:10), and Messiah's tunic was not torn but lots were cast (John 19:23-24).

also.meaning: When Saul tore Samuel's robe the text interprets it: 'Yahuah hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day' (1 Sam 15:28); Jonathan gave David his robe in covenant (1 Sam 18:4), and David cut off the skirt of Saul's robe but spared the anointed (1 Sam 24:4).
"He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bride" (Isa 61:10) - the clothing Yahuah gives, the bride's fine linen (Rev 19:8).

words.meaning: "Living water" required for the cleansing of leper and the defiled (Lev 14:5; Num 19:17); Yahuah is "the fountain of living waters" (Jer 2:13), and Yahushua speaks of living water flowing from within (John 7:38-39).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: "Yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come" (Ezek 11:16) - Yahuah Himself the dwelling place of His exiles, apart from the stone house.

also.meaning: The sanctuary trodden underfoot is Yahuah's true place of worship and His people; "then shall the sanctuary be cleansed" (nitsdaq, set right) is His vindicating work through Messiah's own blood (Heb 9:23-24), not a 1844 judgment.

lexicon.title: Temple of God (Naos) and Its Worshipers

words.meaning: First stone of the breastplate, bearing a tribe's name on Aaron's heart (Exod 28:17,21); the one on the throne is seen "like a jasper and a sardine stone" (Rev 4:3), and sardius is the sixth foundation of the city (Rev 21:20).
Water creatures with fins and scales were clean, the rest abomination (Lev 11:9-12); the dragnet parable shows the catch sorted, good into vessels and bad cast away (Matt 13:47-48).

The live goat on which Aaron confessed "all the iniquities" of Israel and which bore them "unto a land not inhabited" (Lev 16:21-22); so far as east from west Yahuah removes transgressions (Ps 103:12).

Scarlet with cedar and hyssop in the cleansing rites (Lev 14:4,6); Hebrews names "water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop" sprinkling book and people (Heb 9:19), and scarlet sins become white as wool (Isa 1:18).

Peter's vision of unclean beasts let down by four corners is interpreted by Peter himself: "Elohim hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean" (Acts 10:28), Gentiles gathered from the four corners (Isa 11:12).
Twelve loaves set continually before Yahuah's face in the Holy Place (Lev 24:5-8); David ate it in need (1 Sam 21:6), which Yahushua cites to show mercy above sacrifice (Matt 12:4-7).
Desert acacia, the wood of ark, table, altars and boards, overlaid with gold or brass (Exod 25:10-11); Yahuah promises to plant "the shittah tree" in the wilderness (Isa 41:19).

Aaron bore the tribes' names "upon his two shoulders for a memorial" (Exod 28:12); the government is upon the shoulder of the promised child (Isa 9:6), and the shepherd lays the lost sheep on his shoulders (Luke 15:5).

also.meaning: "The government shall be upon his shoulder" (Isa 9:6) - the place where rule and the key of David are borne (Isa 22:22), as the high priest bore the tribes' names on his shoulders (Exod 28:12).

words.meaning: "Bread of the face" set before Yahuah continually (Exod 25:30), renewed every Sabbath and eaten by priests in the holy place (Lev 24:8-9); bread pictures the word lived by (Deut 8:3), and Yahushua calls himself the bread of life (John 6:35).

Offering for sins of ignorance whose body was burned outside the camp (Lev 4:12); Yahuah "hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin" (2 Cor 5:21), and Yahushua "suffered without the gate" (Heb 13:12).

Silver bases the boards stood on, cast from the half-shekel atonement money of the numbered men (Exod 38:25-27); the dwelling literally stood on ransom silver, though true redemption is "not with... silver and gold" but precious blood (1 Pet 1:18-19).
"I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight" (Ezek 4:16) - bread as life's support, withdrawn in famine judgment; the weighed ration of Rev 6:6.
Fire Nadab and Abihu offered "which he commanded them not" (Lev 10:1), worship by man's own choosing, answered by fire from Yahuah; "I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me" (Lev 10:3).

Do not put a stumblingblock before the blind (Lev 19:14); Yahuah is a stone of stumbling to both houses of Israel (Isa 8:14), Messiah crucified a stumblingblock to the Jews (1 Cor 1:23), and Balaam cast a stumblingblock before Israel (Rev 2:14).

Unclean, parting the hoof but not chewing the cud (Lev 11:7); eating it marks the rebellious (Isa 65:4; 66:17), holy things are not cast before swine (Matt 7:6), and the washed sow returns to the mire (2 Pet 2:22).

also.meaning: The swine is the unclean beast: the boar out of the wood wastes Yahuah's vine (Ps 80:13), a fair woman without discretion is a gold ring in a swine's snout (Prov 11:22), and holy things are not cast before swine (Matt 7:6).
Unclean by Yahuah's Torah (Lev 11:7); those eating swine's flesh in the end of days are consumed together (Isa 66:17) - the mark of defiled worship, and of returning to filth (2 Pet 2:22).

The unclean beast (Lev 11:7) that tramples what is holy (Matt 7:6); feeding swine marks the prodigal's lowest estrangement (Luke 15:15), and the washed sow returning to the mire pictures the apostate (2 Pet 2:22).

words.meaning: The dwelling built "that I may dwell among them" (Exod 25:8); the Word "tabernacled among us" (John 1:14), the body is an earthly tabernacle (2 Cor 5:1), and at the end the tabernacle of Elohim is with men (Rev 21:3).

The great weight of gold and silver given for the tabernacle (Exod 38:24-27); talents are what the Master entrusts to his servants to trade with until his return (Matt 25:15), and a debt of ten thousand talents is unpayable (Matt 18:24).
The two tables written by the finger of Elohim and laid in the ark (Exod 31:18); the covenant terms Yahuah later writes "in their hearts" (Jer 31:33), kept by the remnant (Rev 12:17).

"Perfections," set with the Urim in the breastplate of judgment (Exod 28:30); Moses gives "thy Thummim and thy Urim" to Levi's holy one (Deut 33:8) — Yahuah's complete and true judgment carried by the priest.
Offering for wrong done, joined to full restitution plus a fifth (Lev 6:5); Isaiah says Yahuah would "make his soul an offering for sin (asham)" (Isa 53:10).

words.alt: agate, amethyst, carbuncle, chalcedony, chrysolite, chrysoprasus, diamond, jacinth, ligure, sardonyx, topaz
words.meaning: The twelve stones set in four rows on the breastplate each bore the name of a tribe, so that Aaron carried Israel "upon his heart" before Yahuah continually (Exod 28:21, 29); the same set returns as the twelve foundations of the city, bearing the names of the twelve apostles (Rev 21:14, 19-20): one people, built on one pattern.

also.meaning: Scripture gives most of the stones no meaning of their own; their meaning is the set. The stones Scripture does use on their own (sardius, onyx, emerald, sapphire, beryl and jasper) keep their own entries.

words.meaning: One bird killed over running water and the living bird dipped in its blood and "let loose into the open field" (Lev 14:6-7) — death and release in one cleansing; Messiah was delivered for offences and raised again (Rom 4:25).

Two goats set before Yahuah and divided by lot — one slain as the sin offering and its blood brought within the veil (Lev 16:15), the other sent away alive bearing the iniquities (Lev 16:21); one covering, two pictures of it.
Two leavened loaves of new grain waved "as firstfruits unto Yahuah" at Shavuot, fifty days on (Lev 23:16-17); the people gathered then are "a kind of firstfruits of his creatures" (Jas 1:18).

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: Birds of prey and carrion named abomination (Lev 11:13-19); they haunt ruined places (Isa 34:11), and fallen Babylon becomes "a cage of every unclean and hateful bird" (Rev 18:2).

lexicon.title: Dwelling of Demons, Cage of Unclean Birds

words.meaning: "Lights," placed in the breastplate so Aaron bore "the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart" (Exod 28:30); counsel was asked of Yahuah by it (Num 27:21), and its loss left Israel waiting for a priest (Ezra 2:63).
The covering Moses put over his shining face (Exod 34:33); Paul reads it as the vail still on hearts when Moses is read, taken away "when it shall turn to the Master" (2 Cor 3:14-16).
"In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink" (Ps 69:21), fulfilled at the stake (John 19:29); a sluggard is vinegar to the teeth (Prov 10:26).

also.meaning: "In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink" (Ps 69:21), fulfilled when the sponge of vinegar was lifted to Messiah, after which he said "It is finished" (John 19:28-30).

words.meaning: Portions waved before Yahuah, as the breast of the peace offering (Lev 7:30), the firstfruits sheaf and Shavuot loaves (Lev 23:11,17); even the Levites themselves were offered "for an offering (tenuphah)" (Num 8:11).

The first sheaf of harvest waved on the morrow after the Sabbath, before any grain was eaten (Lev 23:10-14); "now is Messiah risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept" (1 Cor 15:20).

Brook willows carried at Sukkot (Lev 23:40); when Yahuah pours His spirit on Jacob's seed they spring up "as willows by the water courses" (Isa 44:3-4), but in exile harps hung silent on them (Ps 137:2).

The gold that came to Solomon in one year weighed 'six hundred threescore and six talents' (1 Kgs 10:14), in the reign whose multiplied gold, horses and wives broke Deut 17:16-17 and turned his heart (1 Kgs 11:4); Rev 13:18 calls 666 'the number of a man'.

'Trouble': the valley where Achan, the troubler of Israel, was stoned under a heap; Yahuah later promises 'the valley of Achor for a door of hope' (Hos 2:15), turning the place of judgment into an entrance.

lexicon.title: Valley of Achor, Door of Hope

words.meaning: "Go to the ant, thou sluggard" (Prov 6:6): the ant, with no ruler over her, prepares food in summer — a picture of diligence and foresight that the lazy man lacks (Prov 30:25).

"As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons" (Song 2:3): the beloved gives shade and sweet fruit; a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver (Prov 25:11).
False teachers are "trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots" (Jude 12), the opposite of the righteous tree planted by rivers of water (Ps 1:3; Jer 17:8).

The borrowed axe head sank in Jordan; Elisha cut a stick and cast it in, 'and the iron did swim' (2 Kgs 6:6), as the tree cast into Marah made the waters sweet (Exod 15:25); 'now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees' (Matt 3:10).

also.meaning: Assyria is the axe that boasts against the one who hews with it (Isa 10:15); Babylon is Yahuah's battle axe (Jer 51:20); the axe laid to the root of the trees (Matt 3:10).

The instrument of judgment in Yahuah's hand: Assyria is only the axe boasting against its hewer (Isa 10:15); now the axe is laid to the root of the trees, and every tree without good fruit is hewn down (Matt 3:10).

words.meaning: The barley cake that tumbled into Midian's camp is interpreted in the text itself: 'this is nothing else save the sword of Gideon' (Judg 7:14); barley is the first grain ripe at Pesach (Exod 9:31; Ruth 1:22) and the loaves Yahushua multiplied (John 6:9).

'In it is strength': the left-hand pillar, bearing the name of David's ancestor the kinsman-redeemer (Ruth 4:21-22); with Jachin it stood at the entrance as Yahuah's establishing and strength for the house of David (1 Kgs 7:21).
Yahuah keeps His servant's tears in His bottle, recording every wandering (Ps 56:8); a bottle in the smoke is a man dried and shriveled by trial who still holds to the statutes (Ps 119:83).

also.meaning: The skin container: worn by trial "like a bottle in the smoke" (Ps 119:83); new wine must go into new bottles, the renewed vessel needed for the new life (Matt 9:17); Yahuah keeps tears in His bottle (Ps 56:8).

Bottles filled with wine are a people filled with drunkenness and dashed together (Jer 13:12-14); the potter's bottle broken in the valley: "so will I break this people and this city" beyond repair (Jer 19:10-11).

words.meaning: The vial or box of anointing oil by which kings were anointed (1 Sam 10:1; 2 Kgs 9:3); the broken alabaster box poured on Yahushua anoints the King for his burial (Mark 14:3, 8).

In Jotham's parable the olive, fig and vine refuse to leave their fruit to rule; only the bramble accepts and threatens fire to devour the cedars, which is Abimelech, the fruitless ruler whose fire consumed Shechem (Judg 9:20, 57).
The bride is the beloved people betrothed to their husband (Song 4:8-12; Jer 2:2), adorned in garments of deliverance (Isa 61:10), and revealed at last as the holy city, the Lamb's wife (Rev 21:2).

The bridegroom is the joyful husband coming for his bride (Ps 19:5); as a bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so Elohim rejoices over His people (Isa 62:5), and Yahushua is the bridegroom whose marriage comes (Matt 9:15; Rev 19:7).

also.meaning: As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so Yahuah rejoices over His people (Isa 62:5); Messiah is the bridegroom whose friend John rejoices (John 3:29), awaited by the virgins at midnight (Matt 25:6).

words.meaning: Bit and bridle restrain a beast without understanding (Ps 32:9); the righteous bridle their own mouth (Ps 39:1; Jas 3:2), while a rod is for the fool's back (Prov 26:3).

also.meaning: Restraint of the mouth: "I will keep my mouth with a bridle" (Ps 39:1); one who bridles not his tongue has vain religion (Jas 1:26), and as bits turn horses, the tongue governs the whole body (Jas 3:3).

lexicon.title: Blood to the Horses' Bridles (1,600 Stadia)

words.meaning: Egypt is a bruised reed that pierces the hand leaning on it (2 Kgs 18:21; Ezek 29:6); the bruised reed the Servant will not break is the weak among His people (Isa 42:3; Matt 12:20).
The buckler is close, body-covering defense: "his truth shall be thy shield and buckler" (Ps 91:4), and He is a buckler to those who walk uprightly (Prov 2:7).

"Except Yahuah build the house, they labour in vain that build it" (Ps 127:1); the builders rejected the stone (Ps 118:22), Paul built as a wise masterbuilder (1 Cor 3:10), and "he that built all things is Elohim" (Heb 3:4).

In the psalm of the suffering Messiah, "strong bulls of Bashan" surround Him (Ps 22:12): powerful, well-fed oppressors closing in on the righteous one; Bashan's cattle stand for the proud rich who crush the poor (Amos 4:1).

Abigail told David his soul 'shall be bound in the bundle of life with Yahuah thy Elohim', while his enemies' souls are slung away (1 Sam 25:29): life kept with Yahuah, akin to the book of remembrance and the book of life (Mal 3:16).

Where the slain are, there the eagles gather (Job 39:30): Yahushua uses it for the certainty of judgment falling where the dead body lies (Matt 24:28), as the birds are called to the great supper (Rev 19:17).

lexicon.title: Two Wings of a Great Eagle
Great Supper of Yahuah (Feast of the Birds)

words.meaning: The Philistines sent the ark on a new cart and David copied them; Uzzah died when the oxen stumbled, and David confessed Yahuah broke forth 'for that we sought him not after the due order', for Levites were to bear it on their shoulders (1 Chr 15:13-15).

In the cave of Adullam the distressed, indebted and discontented gathered to David, anointed but not yet crowned (1 Sam 22:2); Obadiah hid a hundred prophets in caves (1 Kgs 18:4), Elijah heard Yahuah from a cave at Horeb, and the faithful wandered 'in dens and caves of the earth' (Heb 11:38).
The ungodly are "like the chaff which the wind driveth away" (Ps 1:4): light, worthless, separated from the grain at judgment and burned (Matt 3:12).

also.meaning: The wicked driven away like chaff before the wind (Ps 1:4); "What is the chaff to the wheat?" - lying dreams beside Yahuah's word (Jer 23:28); burned at the harvest (Matt 3:12).

The ungodly, worthless and driven away: "like the chaff which the wind driveth away" (Ps 1:4); the kingdoms of Daniel's image become as chaff (Dan 2:35), and Messiah burns the chaff with unquenchable fire (Matt 3:12).

The broken kingdoms become "like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors" carried away by the wind with no place found (Dan 2:35) — the ungodly whom the wind drives away (Ps 1:4) and Messiah's fan separates (Matt 3:12).

words.meaning: Bondage and its breaking: Yahuah brings prisoners out of darkness and breaks their bands (Ps 107:14; Isa 61:1); Peter's chains fall off (Acts 12:7), while fallen angels are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness (Jude 6).

lexicon.title: Key of the Abyss and the Great Chain

words.meaning: Eliashib the priest gave the enemy Tobiah a great chamber in the courts where the offerings had been stored; Nehemiah 'cast forth all the household stuff' and had the chambers cleansed (Neh 13:8-9), as Yahushua drove the traders out of the temple (John 2:15).

Drinking from one's own cistern is faithfulness to one's own wife (Prov 5:15); Israel hewed broken cisterns that hold no water in place of Yahuah (Jer 2:13), and the wheel broken at the cistern marks the end of life (Eccl 12:6).

also.meaning: "Hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water" (Jer 2:13) - man-made religion and idols that cannot hold life.

words.meaning: "As the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel" (Jer 18:6) - man formed and shaped by Yahuah, with no right to answer back to his Maker (Isa 45:9).

also.meaning: Iron mixed with miry clay is the fourth kingdom's divided last form, "partly strong, and partly broken," mingling "with the seed of men" yet never cleaving together (Dan 2:42-43); elsewhere clay is man in the Potter's hand (Jer 18:6).
Man formed of the earth and shaped by Yahuah: "we are the clay, and thou our potter" (Isa 64:8); Yahushua anoints the blind man's eyes with clay, a new forming of sight (John 9:6-7).

words.meaning: Feeding an enemy heaps coals of fire on his head (Prov 25:22; Rom 12:20); a live coal from the altar purged Isaiah's lips (Isa 6:6-7).

also.meaning: A coal from the altar laid on Isaiah's lips takes away iniquity (Isa 6:7); coals from between the cherubim scattered over Jerusalem bring judgment (Ezek 10:2) - altar fire either cleanses or consumes.

lexicon.title: Fire from the Altar Cast to the Earth

words.meaning: The scarlet line bound in Rahab's window marked the one house spared when Jericho fell, as the Pesach blood marked the doors in Egypt (Exod 12:13); the same word, tiqvah, is elsewhere rendered 'hope' (Jer 29:11).

also.meaning: Cords bind: the nations would cast away Yahuah's cords (Ps 2:3), the wicked are held by the cords of their own sins (Prov 5:22), a cord of three strands is companions standing together (Eccl 4:9-12), and Yahuah drew Israel with cords of love (Hos 11:4).
"I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love" (Hos 11:4) — Yahuah leading His son out of Egypt with human tenderness, lifting the yoke from their jaws.

words.meaning: Yahuah laid the corner stone of the earth (Job 38:6); "the stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner" (Ps 118:22), applied by Yahushua to Himself (Matt 21:42).

also.meaning: "I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone" (Isa 28:16) - Messiah laid by Yahuah as the sure foundation of His house (1 Pet 2:6).

words.meaning: A crown is honor bestowed: man is crowned with glory (Ps 8:5), Yahuah crowns with lovingkindness (Ps 103:4), a virtuous wife is her husband's crown (Prov 12:4), the hoary head a crown of glory (Prov 16:31), and the faithful receive a crown of life (Rev 2:10).

also.meaning: Honor bestowed: man crowned with glory and honor (Ps 8:5), Yahuah Himself a crown of glory to His remnant (Isa 28:5); the incorruptible crown, the crowns of righteousness, life and glory given to the faithful (2 Tim 4:8; Jas 1:12).
The crowns set on Joshua the high priest show "the man whose name is The BRANCH" who "shall be a priest upon his throne" (Zech 6:12-13) — king and priest in one, as Melchizedek.

words.alt: cruse of oil, pots of oil
words.meaning: At Elijah's word the widow's little oil did not fail (1 Kgs 17:14), and Elisha's widow poured oil into borrowed vessels until 'there is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed' (2 Kgs 4:6); the wise virgins carried oil in their vessels (Matt 25:4).

The Persian king Yahuah stirred to proclaim the rebuilding (Ezra 1:1), named beforehand 'my shepherd' and 'his anointed' though he had not known Yahuah (Isa 44:28; 45:1, 4), a gentile ruler raised to release the captives and raise the house.

also.meaning: A gentile king Yahuah calls "my shepherd" and "his anointed" (Isa 44:28; 45:1) to free the captives and order the temple rebuilt - Yahuah ruling the nations for His people's sake.

words.meaning: Ehud's dagger 'which had two edges' went in to the hilt and the fat closed upon it (Judg 3:22); Scripture makes the two-edged sword the word that pierces to the inmost parts and discerns the heart (Heb 4:12).

lexicon.title: Sharp Two-Edged Sword from His Mouth

words.meaning: The Philistine idol fell on its face before the ark and was found with head and palms cut off on the threshold (1 Sam 5:4), the false god broken in the presence of Yahuah's covenant; its house later took Saul's head (1 Chr 10:10).

lexicon.title: Idols of Gold, Silver, Bronze, Stone and Wood

words.meaning: The shadow brought back ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz (Isa 38:8) - Yahuah's sign to Hezekiah that years would be added to his life.

Naaman dipped himself seven times in Jordan 'according to the saying of the man of Elohim' and his flesh came again 'like unto the flesh of a little child' (2 Kgs 5:14), cleansing by obeying a plain word; tabal is also the priest's dipping in blood (Lev 4:6).
Dross is the waste skimmed from refined metal: Yahuah puts away the wicked like dross (Ps 119:119), and when the dross is taken from silver a vessel comes forth (Prov 25:4).

also.meaning: "Thy silver is become dross" (Isa 1:22) - a people corrupted from within; Yahuah purges away the dross in His furnace (Isa 1:25; Ezek 22:18-22).

words.meaning: The gate through which the city's refuse went out to the valley (Neh 2:13; 3:14); Yahuah 'lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes' (1 Sam 2:8), and Paul counts his former gains 'but dung' to win Messiah (Phil 3:8).

Its keeper Shemaiah repaired beside it (Neh 3:29); the glory left the temple by the east gate and returned 'by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east' (Ezek 43:4), after which that gate was shut because Yahuah had entered by it (Ezek 44:2).

also.meaning: "This gate shall be shut... because Yahuah, the Elohim of Israel, hath entered in by it" (Ezek 44:2) - the way the glory returned is sealed as holy; only the prince sits there to eat bread before Yahuah (44:3).

words.meaning: 'Stone of help', set up by Samuel after the thunder routed the Philistines: 'Hitherto hath Yahuah helped us' (1 Sam 7:12), the same place-name where the ark had been lost twenty years before (1 Sam 4:1).

Nathan's parable of the poor man's one little ewe lamb taken by a rich man was turned on David: 'Thou art the man' (2 Sam 12:7), the lamb being Uriah's wife; a parable that made the king pronounce his own sentence.
"He shall cover thee with his feathers" (Ps 91:4): the close, warm covering of Yahuah's protection, like a hen gathering her brood (Matt 23:37).

also.meaning: The king's hair grown like eagles' feathers and nails like claws mark the proud ruler brought to a beast's state (Dan 4:33), the same eagle-winged lion whose wings are plucked in Dan 7:4.

words.meaning: Built by the sons of Hassenaah (Neh 3:3), near where the men of Tyre sold fish even on the Sabbath (Neh 13:16); Zephaniah hears 'a cry from the fish gate' in the day of Yahuah (Zeph 1:10), and the disciples were made 'fishers of men' (Matt 4:19).

Love's "coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame" (Song 8:6) cannot be quenched by many waters (Song 8:7); Yahuah's voice divides flames of fire, and He makes His ministers a flaming fire (Ps 29:7; 104:4).

lexicon.title: Eyes Like a Flame of Fire

words.meaning: Gideon's fleece wet with dew while the floor was dry, then dry while the ground was wet, was a sign asked and given that Yahuah would deliver Israel by his hand (Judg 6:36-40).

The footstool is the place under the throne: the ark was Yahuah's footstool (1 Chr 28:2), the earth is His footstool (Isa 66:1), and Yahuah tells Messiah to sit at His right hand until He makes His enemies His footstool (Ps 110:1; Acts 2:35).

also.meaning: The ark as the footstool of Elohim (1 Chr 28:2); "heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool" (Isa 66:1) - no house of stone can contain Him; Zion forgotten as His footstool in wrath (Lam 2:1).

Enemies made subject: Yahuah tells Messiah to sit at His right hand until He makes his enemies his footstool (Ps 110:1; Heb 10:13); when all is subdued, the Son himself is subject to the Father, that Elohim may be all in all (1 Cor 15:28).

words.meaning: Yahuah is the fortress of His people, their stronghold in the day of trouble (Ps 18:2; 91:2); refuge is found in Him, not in walls or armies.

With Yahuah is the fountain of life (Ps 36:9), the fountain of living waters (Jer 2:13); a fountain cannot send forth sweet and bitter water, so blessing and cursing cannot come from one mouth (Jas 3:10-12).

also.meaning: "They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters" (Jer 2:13) - Yahuah Himself the source of life; a fountain opened for sin and uncleanness (Zech 13:1).
"A fountain shall come forth of the house of Yahuah" (Joel 3:18), the temple river of Ezek 47 and the river of water of life proceeding from the throne (Rev 22:1).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: Repaired with the wall of the pool of Siloah by the king's garden (Neh 3:15); Israel refused 'the waters of Shiloah that go softly' (Isa 8:6), and Yahushua sent the blind man to wash in Siloam and spoke of rivers of living water (John 9:7; 7:38).

Samson loosed foxes with firebrands into the Philistines' grain; elsewhere the fox is the spoiler: 'the little foxes, that spoil the vines' (Song 2:15), Israel's prophets 'like the foxes in the deserts' (Ezek 13:4), and Herod 'that fox' (Luke 13:32).

also.meaning: "The little foxes, that spoil the vines" (Song 2:15) are small destroyers of tender fruit; Israel's false prophets are "like the foxes in the deserts" (Ezek 13:4), and Yahushua called Herod "that fox" (Luke 13:32).
A crafty spoiler of the vine: the little foxes spoil the vines (Song 2:15), Israel's false prophets are like foxes in the deserts (Ezek 13:4), and Yahushua names Herod "that fox" (Luke 13:32).

words.meaning: Haman made a 'tree' (ets) fifty cubits high for Mordecai and was hanged on it himself (Esth 7:10): 'he made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made' (Ps 7:15); one hanged on a tree is under the curse (Deut 21:23).

"I sought for a man... that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land" and found none (Ezek 22:30) - intercession and repentance that turn wrath; false prophets never went up into the gaps (13:5).

words.alt: new garment rent in twelve pieces
words.meaning: Ahijah tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave Jeroboam ten, explaining 'I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee' (1 Kgs 11:31), one tribe kept for David's sake.

also.meaning: Righteousness given to the guest: "he hath clothed me with the garments of deliverance" (Isa 61:10), filthy garments exchanged for clean (Zech 3:4); without the wedding garment the guest is cast out (Matt 22:12).

words.meaning: 'Rolling': where the second generation was circumcised and Yahuah said 'this day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt' (Josh 5:9); Israel's first camp in the land, later a seat of idolatry (Hos 9:15).
"All flesh is grass" (Isa 40:6) - the brief life and glory of man that withers, set against the word of Elohim that stands for ever (Isa 40:8; 1 Pet 1:24-25).

also.meaning: The brevity of man: all flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower that fades, but the word of Elohim stands forever (Isa 40:6-8; 1 Pet 1:24-25); the rich pass away as the flower of the grass (Jas 1:10).
Eating grass with a beast's heart shows man exalted in pride becoming a beast (Dan 4:16, 33): "Man that is in honour, and understandeth not, is like the beasts that perish" (Ps 49:20).

words.meaning: The temple stones were finished at the quarry so 'neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron' was heard in the house (1 Kgs 6:7), as the altar was to be of unhewn stone (Exod 20:25); Yahuah's word is the hammer that breaks the rock (Jer 23:29).

also.meaning: "Is not my word like as a fire... and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?" (Jer 23:29); Babylon was the hammer of the whole earth, itself cut asunder (Jer 50:23).

words.meaning: "Thou hast made my days as an handbreadth" (Ps 39:5): man's whole life measured by the width of a hand, nothing before Yahuah.

When David played the harp before Saul the evil spirit departed (1 Sam 16:23); the Levites 'prophesy with harps' (1 Chr 25:1), at the minstrel's playing the hand of Yahuah came on Elisha (2 Kgs 3:15), and the overcomers hold 'the harps of Elohim' (Rev 15:2).

also.meaning: The harp is praise to Yahuah (Ps 33:2; 150:3); in exile Israel hung its harps on the willows (Ps 137:2), and the redeemed hold the harps of Elohim before the throne (Rev 5:8; 15:2).

words.meaning: The hart panting for water brooks is the soul thirsting for the living Elohim (Ps 42:1); Yahuah gives His people hinds' feet to stand on high places (Ps 18:33; Hab 3:19), and the lame leap like a hart at His coming (Isa 35:6).

A hedge is Yahuah's protecting boundary: He set a hedge about Job (Job 1:10) and about His vineyard, and when it is broken down the beasts devour (Ps 80:12; Isa 5:5); whoever breaks a hedge, a serpent shall bite him (Eccl 10:8).

also.meaning: Yahuah's protection set around His people; when the vineyard bears wild grapes He takes away the hedge and it is eaten up and trodden down (Isa 5:5; Ps 80:12).
Yahuah hedges the straying wife's way with thorns so she cannot find her lovers and says, "I will go and return to my first husband" (Hos 2:6-7) — correction that blocks the road back to idols.

words.meaning: Yahushua's lament that he would have gathered Jerusalem's children as a hen gathers her brood (Matt 23:37) takes up the shelter of Yahuah's wings under which Ruth came to trust (Ruth 2:12; Ps 91:4).

"He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty" (Ps 91:1): Yahuah Himself is the hiding place of His own (Ps 32:7), where the dove waits in the clefts of the rock (Song 2:14).

Yahuah answered Sennacherib's pride: 'I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest' (2 Kgs 19:28), proud kings led like beasts; so Gog is turned back with hooks (Ezek 38:4).

also.meaning: "I will put hooks in thy jaws" (Ezek 29:4; 38:4) - Yahuah leading proud kings (Sennacherib, Pharaoh, Gog) wherever He wills, to their own judgment.

words.meaning: The horseleach has two daughters crying "Give, give" (Prov 30:15): insatiable craving, set beside the grave, the barren womb and fire that are never satisfied (Prov 30:16).

David wished to build Yahuah a house, but Yahuah would build David a house, a lasting line, whose seed would 'build an house for my name' (2 Sam 7:11-13); the tabernacle of David is rebuilt (Acts 15:16), 'whose house are we' (Heb 3:6).

also.meaning: "Wisdom hath builded her house" (Prov 9:1), and "except Yahuah build the house, they labour in vain" (Ps 127:1); Yahuah builds David a house (2 Sam 7:11), and His people are His house if they hold fast (Heb 3:6).

words.meaning: 'The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of Elohim is taken' (1 Sam 4:22), the child named the day Shiloh fell; Yahuah 'forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh' (Ps 78:60), and the glory leaves the temple again in Ezekiel (Ezek 10:18).

'He shall establish': the right-hand bronze pillar of the temple porch (1 Kgs 7:21), echoing Yahuah's promise to establish David's throne (2 Sam 7:12-13); the pillars were broken and carried to Babylon (2 Kgs 25:13), and the overcomer is made a pillar in the temple (Rev 3:12).

With a fresh jawbone of an ass Samson slew a thousand at Lehi, then thirsting called on Yahuah, who split a hollow place so water came out, En-hakkore, 'the well of him that called' (Judg 15:19): a despised weapon in Yahuah's hand.

The walled city that fell flat at the shout after seven days of circuits, by belief and not by siege (Heb 11:30); Joshua's curse on its rebuilder fell on Hiel's sons (1 Kgs 16:34), and its fall pictures strongholds pulled down (2 Cor 10:4).

The river crossed dry-shod when the priests' feet touched it, the passage from wilderness into inheritance as the Red Sea was the exit from Egypt (Josh 4:23); parted again by Elijah and Elisha, the place of Naaman's cleansing and Yahushua's immersion.

Elijah sat under a juniper and asked to die; a messenger woke him to a cake baken on the coals and water, and 'in the strength of that meat' he went forty days and nights to Horeb (1 Kgs 19:8); its coals picture judgment on the deceitful tongue (Ps 120:4).

A kiss is submission and loyalty: "kiss the Son, lest he be angry" (Ps 2:12); righteousness and peace kiss each other (Ps 85:10), while the enemy's kisses are deceitful (Prov 27:6), as at the betrayal (Luke 22:48).

also.meaning: Two uses: homage, "kiss the Son, lest he be angry" (Ps 2:12), and the holy kiss of fellowship (Rom 16:16); and treachery, Joab's kiss (2 Sam 20:9), "the kisses of an enemy are deceitful" (Prov 27:6), the betrayal of Judas (Luke 22:48).

words.meaning: Worship and allegiance: seven thousand knees not bowed to Baal (1 Kgs 19:18; Rom 11:4); every knee bows at the name of Yahushua "to the glory of Elohim the Father" (Phil 2:10-11; Isa 45:23); feeble knees are strengthened (Heb 12:12).
The fading leaf of the sinful (Isa 64:6) against the unwithering leaf of the one rooted by the waters (Ps 1:3); leaves of the river trees are for medicine (Ezek 47:12; Rev 22:2).

also.meaning: Two uses: leaves without fruit as empty show (Matt 21:19; Gen 3:7); and the unwithering leaf of the righteous (Ps 1:3), the leaves of the tree of life "for the healing of the nations" (Ezek 47:12; Rev 22:2).

lexicon.title: Fig Leaves and Tunics of Skin

words.meaning: Leviathan is the great sea creature no man can master but Yahuah (Job 41); Isaiah names it "the piercing serpent... the dragon that is in the sea" that Yahuah will slay (Isa 27:1), the old serpent of Rev 12:9.

also.meaning: The crooked serpent and dragon of the sea whom Yahuah punishes (Isa 27:1) - Pharaoh is "the great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers" (Ezek 29:3); the old serpent of Rev 12:9.

words.meaning: At Mizpeh Israel drew water and poured it out before Yahuah and fasted in repentance (1 Sam 7:6); David poured out the Bethlehem water as 'the blood of the men that went in jeopardy' (2 Sam 23:17); the heart is poured out like water before Yahuah (Lam 2:19).

Lily work crowned the pillars and the brim of the molten sea (1 Kgs 7:22, 26); the beloved is 'the lily among thorns' (Song 2:2), Israel restored 'shall grow as the lily' (Hos 14:5), and Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one (Matt 6:29).

also.meaning: The lily is purity and beauty set apart: "as the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters" (Song 2:2); Israel restored grows as the lily (Hos 14:5), and the lilies of the field show the Father's care (Matt 6:28).

Beauty given rather than earned: lily work crowned the temple pillars (1 Kgs 7:19), the beloved is a lily among thorns (Song 2:2), and the lilies, which toil not, are clothed beyond Solomon's glory (Matt 6:28-29).
Restored Israel "shall grow as the lily, and cast forth his roots as Lebanon" (Hos 14:5) — beauty from Yahuah's dew, planted deep and firm.

words.meaning: The measuring line marks Yahuah's ordering and allotment: He stretched it on the earth (Job 38:5), "the lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places" (Ps 16:6), and the line of the heavens' witness went out through all the earth (Ps 19:4; Rom 10:18).

Elijah's mantle cast on Elisha was the call to the prophet's office (1 Kgs 19:19); it parted Jordan and, falling, passed the office on (2 Kgs 2:13-14); the same word is Achan's coveted Babylonish garment (Josh 7:21) and the 'rough garment' false prophets wear to deceive (Zech 13:4).

also.meaning: The prophet's garment passing a calling: Elijah's mantle cast on Elisha (1 Kgs 19:19) and taken up with a double portion (2 Kgs 2:13); John's camel's hair and leather girdle mark him as coming in the spirit and power of Elijah (Luke 1:17).

words.meaning: The Zarephath widow's barrel of meal did not waste nor the cruse of oil fail through the famine (1 Kgs 17:16), a gentile widow fed by Yahuah's word (Luke 4:26); Elisha's handful of meal healed the poisoned pot (2 Kgs 4:41).

Solid food for the mature: Job esteemed Yahuah's words more than his necessary food (Job 23:12); strong meat belongs to those who by use discern good and evil (Heb 5:14); Messiah's meat was to do the will of Him that sent him (John 4:34).

Five golden emerods and five golden mice, images of the plague that 'mar the land', were sent back with the ark as a trespass offering, 'and ye shall give glory unto the Elohim of Israel' (1 Sam 6:5); the mouse is unclean under the Torah (Lev 11:29).

'Appointment, mustering' (Neh 3:31); the same word names 'the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary' where the sin offering was burned (Ezek 43:21), outside the gate, where Yahushua also suffered (Heb 13:12).
Mire is the sinking helplessness of the afflicted: "I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing" (Ps 69:2), and Yahuah brings His servant up out of the miry clay onto a rock (Ps 40:2).

The great bronze basin, ten cubits across, 'for the priests to wash in' (2 Chr 4:6), the enlarged laver of the tabernacle (Exod 30:18-21); it answers to the sea of glass before the throne (Rev 4:6; 15:2) and the washing of water by the word (Eph 5:26).

The moth is slow, silent decay: man is crushed before the moth (Job 4:19), Yahuah's rebuke consumes beauty like a moth (Ps 39:11), and earthly treasure is moth-eaten while treasure in heaven is not (Matt 6:20).

also.meaning: The quiet consumer of earthly treasure: the wicked wax old as a garment the moth eats (Isa 50:9; 51:8); treasures on earth are moth-eaten, so lay up treasure in heaven (Matt 6:19-20; Jas 5:2).
"I will be unto Ephraim as a moth" (Hos 5:12) — Yahuah's slow, hidden judgment eating away a people before the lion's open attack (Hos 5:14).

words.meaning: Myrtle branches made the Sukkot booths (Neh 8:15), and Esther's Hebrew name Hadassah means myrtle (Esth 2:7); 'instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree' as an everlasting sign (Isa 55:13), and Yahuah's messenger stands among the myrtle trees (Zech 1:8).

also.meaning: "Instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree... for an everlasting sign" (Isa 55:13) - the curse reversed for the returning people; myrtle boughs built the booths of Sukkot (Neh 8:15).

words.meaning: Jael's tent peg ended Sisera (Judg 4:21); Scripture turns the peg into a figure of a secure place given by Yahuah: 'a nail in his holy place' (Ezra 9:8), Eliakim 'as a nail in a sure place' (Isa 22:23), the nail out of Judah (Zech 10:4).

also.meaning: Eliakim fastened "as a nail in a sure place" to bear the glory of his father's house (Isa 22:23-24) - a secure hold for Yahuah's people (Ezra 9:8); out of Judah came the nail (Zech 10:4).
The brass nails of the fourth beast "stamped the residue with the feet" (Dan 7:19) — trampling what its teeth left; Mic 4:13 gives Zion hoofs of brass for Yahuah's threshing.

A peg fastened in a sure place to bear the glory of the father's house (Isa 22:23); Messiah's hands bore the print of the nails (John 20:25), and the written charge of debt against sinners was nailed to his stake (Col 2:14).

words.meaning: The impossibly narrow opening: riches cannot redeem a brother (Ps 49:7), so entry is impossible with men, but "with Elohim all things are possible" (Matt 19:26).

The wicked spread a net for the righteous but are caught in their own (Ps 9:15; 141:10); men are taken by an evil time as fish in a net (Eccl 9:12), and the kingdom is a net gathering every kind (Matt 13:47).

also.meaning: "My net also will I spread upon him" - Zedekiah taken to Babylon, yet not seeing it (Ezek 12:13); Yahuah's capture of the proud; nets also spread for the great gathering of fish (Ezek 47:10).
The Chaldean takes men "with the angle ... in their net" and sacrifices to his net (Hab 1:15-16) — conquest made into an idol; Yahushua's dragnet gathers for judgment instead.

words.meaning: Israel kept Pesach at Gilgal and ate the old corn of the land on the morrow; the manna ceased the next day (Josh 5:12), the wilderness bread giving way to the bread of the inheritance.
Yahuah named Israel "a green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit", then kindled fire on it and broke its branches (Jer 11:16) - the tree into which the nations are grafted (Rom 11:17).

The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, breadth and height, a perfect cube overlaid with gold where the ark rested under the cherubim (1 Kgs 6:20); the New Jerusalem is likewise foursquare, length, breadth and height equal (Rev 21:16).

The burning end of the wicked: Yahuah makes His enemies as a fiery oven (Ps 21:9) and the day comes burning as an oven (Mal 4:1); grass cast into the oven shows how quickly earthly glory is consumed (Matt 6:30).

also.meaning: Israel's lust and intrigue are an oven heated by the baker (Hos 7:4-7), burning as a flaming fire; in Malachi the day of Yahuah "shall burn as an oven" against the proud (Mal 4:1).
"The day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud ... shall be stubble" (Mal 4:1) — the burning that leaves "neither root nor branch."

words.meaning: Twelve bronze oxen bore the sea, three facing each quarter, as the twelve tribes camped three to a side around the tabernacle (Num 2) and the twelve gates face the four quarters three by three (Rev 21:13); Ahaz took the sea down off them (2 Kgs 16:17).

Jezebel painted her face and tired her head at the window before she was thrown down (2 Kgs 9:30-33); Scripture makes the painted face the harlot's dress of an unfaithful people: 'though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair' (Jer 4:30).
Carved on the temple posts and walls between cherubim (Ezek 41:18) - "the righteous shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps 92:12); palms in the hands of the multitude (Rev 7:9).

The precious thing of surpassing worth, as wisdom is above all jewels (Job 28:18): the kingdom is a pearl worth all a man has (Matt 13:46), not to be cast before swine (Matt 7:6); each gate of the city is one pearl (Rev 21:21).

Elisha was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen; he slew the oxen, boiled their flesh with the instruments and followed Elijah (1 Kgs 19:21), leaving the old work behind, for 'no man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom' (Luke 9:62).

also.meaning: Committed service: Elisha left his plough to follow Elijah (1 Kgs 19:19-21); no man having put his hand to the plough and looking back is fit for the kingdom (Luke 9:62); break up your fallow ground (Hos 10:12).

words.meaning: "The plowers plowed upon my back: they made long their furrows" (Ps 129:3) is Israel's long affliction; plowing iniquity yields iniquity (Job 4:8; Hos 10:13), and no one looking back from the plow is fit for the kingdom (Luke 9:62).

Yahuah would stretch over Jerusalem 'the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab' and wipe it 'as a man wipeth a dish' (2 Kgs 21:13), measured by the same standard as the fallen north; judgment laid to the line (Isa 28:17).

also.meaning: "Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet" (Isa 28:17) - Yahuah measuring His people against His standard before He judges.

words.meaning: The entrance hall before the holy place, where the two pillars stood; between the porch and the altar the priests were to weep for the people (Joel 2:17), there men turned their backs to worship the sun (Ezek 8:16), and Yahushua taught in Solomon's porch (John 10:23).
The Levite gatekeepers kept the charge of the house of Elohim (1 Chr 9:26-27); to the shepherd the porter opens (John 10:3), and the departing Master commands the porter to watch (Mark 13:34).
A potsherd is a dry, broken piece of a clay pot: the sufferer's strength is dried up like one (Ps 22:15), and man is but a potsherd that must not strive with his Maker (Isa 45:9).

Ezra stood on 'a pulpit of wood', a migdal or tower, and read the Torah 'distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading' (Neh 8:8); the raised place served to make the Torah heard, as Yahushua stood up to read in the synagogue (Luke 4:16).

Haman cast Pur, the lot, to choose the day of destruction, but 'the whole disposing thereof is of Yahuah' (Prov 16:33); the month was turned 'from sorrow to joy' (Esth 9:22) and named Purim for remembrance.
The queen stands at the King's right hand in gold of Ophir, "all glorious within" (Ps 45:9, 13), the faithful bride; Babylon boasts the counterfeit, "I sit a queen, and am no widow" (Rev 18:7).
"Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them" (Ps 127:5): a household full of children; Yahuah's Servant is a polished shaft hidden in His quiver (Isa 49:2).

The sun rejoices as a strong man to run a race (Ps 19:5); believers run so as to obtain (1 Cor 9:24), with patience the race set before them, looking unto Yahushua (Heb 12:1-2), finishing the course and keeping the belief (2 Tim 4:7).

Rahab ("proud, boisterous") is a poetic name for Egypt: named beside Babylon (Ps 87:4), broken in pieces by Yahuah (Ps 89:10; Isa 51:9), and Egypt whose strength is to sit still (Isa 30:7); distinct from Rahab of Jericho (H7343).

also.meaning: A name for proud Egypt (Isa 30:7; Ps 87:4) - the sea monster Yahuah "cut" and wounded when He dried the sea for the ransomed to pass over (Isa 51:9-10).

words.meaning: Egypt is 'the staff of this bruised reed' that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it (2 Kgs 18:21), false trust in man; yet Yahuah's servant will not break a bruised reed (Isa 42:3; Matt 12:20).

also.meaning: Two uses: frailty, Egypt the staff of a bruised reed (2 Kgs 18:21) and the bruised reed Messiah will not break (Isa 42:3; Matt 12:20), a mock sceptre in his hand (Matt 27:29); and the measuring reed (Ezek 40:3; Rev 11:1).

words.meaning: Priests who 'sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found' were put from the priesthood as polluted (Ezra 2:62); whoever is not found written in the book of life is cast out (Rev 20:15).

"I am the rose of Sharon" is the beloved's word in the Song (Song 2:1); the same flower marks the desert blossoming when the glory of Yahuah appears and "the excellency of Carmel and Sharon" is given to it (Isa 35:1-2).

also.meaning: "The desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose" (Isa 35:1) - the barren land and people brought to life when Yahuah comes to redeem.

words.meaning: "The wicked are like the troubled sea" casting up mire (Isa 57:20); many nations come up like the sea's waves (Ezek 26:3) - "the waters... are peoples" (Rev 17:15).

also.meaning: The great sea from which the beasts rise is the restless mass of peoples; the beasts "are four kings, which shall arise out of the earth" (Dan 7:17), and the waters are "peoples, and multitudes" (Rev 17:15).

words.meaning: Yahuah answered Elijah's 'I, even I only, am left' with seven thousand who had not bowed to Baal (1 Kgs 19:18); Paul applies it: 'even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of favor' (Rom 11:5).

As the sign that Hezekiah would rise and go up to the house of Yahuah with fifteen years added, the shadow went back ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz (2 Kgs 20:11), time turned at Yahuah's word as in Joshua's day.

also.meaning: Scripture uses shadow two ways: the protecting shade of Yahuah's wings (Ps 17:8; 91:1), and the passing shortness of man's days (Ps 144:4; Job 14:2); it is also a pattern pointing to the substance (Col 2:17; Heb 8:5).
Protection under Yahuah: "the shadow of a great rock in a weary land" (Isa 32:2) and a shadow from the heat (Isa 25:4); Judah hoped to live under the shadow of her anointed king (Lam 4:20).

words.meaning: The first gate rebuilt, built and sanctified by the high priest and his brethren (Neh 3:1), where the flocks came in; by it lay the pool of Bethesda (John 5:2), and Yahushua called himself 'the door of the sheep' (John 10:7).

The word the Ephraimites 'could not frame to pronounce', so their own speech exposed them at the fords of Jordan (Judg 12:6); so Peter's speech betrayed him (Matt 26:73), and Yahuah promises to turn to the people 'a pure language' (Zeph 3:9).
"My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle" (Job 7:6): life passing fast and then cut off like a finished web (Isa 38:12).

The loosing of the silver cord is the end of a man's life: Scripture explains the figure at once — "then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto Elohim who gave it" (Eccl 12:6-7).

Jehoshaphat set singers before the army to praise 'the beauty of holiness', and when they began to sing Yahuah set ambushments against the enemy (2 Chr 20:22); when trumpeters and singers were 'as one' the house filled with the cloud (2 Chr 5:13-14).

Kanaph is both wing and garment edge - "I spread my skirt over thee... and thou becamest mine" (Ezek 16:8): covenant covering; the remnant bound in the prophet's skirts (Ezek 5:3); ten men take hold of a Jew's skirt (Zech 8:23).

Death as sleep until the resurrection: many that sleep in the dust shall awake (Dan 12:2), "Lazarus sleepeth" (John 11:11), and the dead in Messiah rise at the trump (1 Thess 4:16); also spiritual slumber, "awake thou that sleepest" (Eph 5:14).

Seven hundred left-handed Benjamites could sling at a hair 'and not miss', the verb chata, Scripture's main word for sin, missing the mark (Judg 20:16); David's sling felled Goliath, and Abigail said Yahuah would 'sling out' the souls of David's enemies (1 Sam 25:29).
Cleansing to perfect whiteness: "wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow" (Ps 51:7; Isa 1:18); the Ancient of Days' garment white as snow (Dan 7:9).

Yahuah's host has its captain (Josh 5:14); the believer is a good soldier of Messiah who does not entangle himself with this life's affairs (2 Tim 2:3-4), whose weapons are not carnal but mighty through Elohim (2 Cor 10:4).

A small fire kindles a great matter: "the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity" (Jas 3:5-6), as the contentious man kindles strife (Prov 26:21) and those who walk in sparks of their own kindling lie down in sorrow (Isa 50:11).

The smallest, cheapest bird: the sparrow finds a house at Yahuah's altars (Ps 84:3), and since not one falls without the Father, His people of more value than many sparrows need not fear (Matt 10:29-31).
The hypocrite's trust is a spider's web that will not hold when leaned on (Job 8:14); the wicked weave spider webs that cannot become garments (Isa 59:5-6).

also.meaning: The hope of the ungodly is a spider's web (Job 8:14); "their webs shall not become garments" (Isa 59:6) - flimsy works of iniquity that cannot cover.

words.meaning: "While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof" (Song 1:12): the bride's devotion poured out, as when Mary anointed Yahushua with spikenard (John 12:3).

also.meaning: The fragrance of the bride's love for the king (Song 1:12), poured out by Mary on Yahushua in costly devotion and accepted as anointing beforehand for his burial (Mark 14:3-8; John 12:3-7).

words.meaning: The sponge filled with vinegar and put on hyssop (John 19:29) carries the Psalm's offered drink (Ps 69:21) to the lips of the dying Messiah, joining the cleansing plant of Pesach to his last thirst.

"A spring shut up, a fountain sealed" (Song 4:12): the bride's purity kept for her husband alone, matching the counsel to drink from one's own well (Prov 5:15-18); a righteous man who falls before the wicked is a troubled spring (Prov 25:26).
Yahuah raises the stormy wind and makes the storm a calm (Ps 107:25, 29); Messiah rebukes the wind and sea (Mark 4:39), and the house on the rock stands when the storm beats on it (Matt 7:25).

The strange woman with smooth, honeyed lips leads to death — "her house is the way to hell" (Prov 7:27) — the counterfeit of Wisdom who also calls from the high places (Prov 9:13-18); Revelation's harlot fills the same role.
Tears are the sorrow of the faithful that Yahuah records (Ps 56:8); those who sow in tears reap in joy (Ps 126:5), and at the end Elohim wipes all tears from their eyes (Isa 25:8; Rev 21:4).

also.meaning: Sorrow Yahuah records and ends: tears kept in His bottle (Ps 56:8), sowing in tears to reap in joy (Ps 126:5); the sinful woman washed Messiah's feet with tears (Luke 7:38), and Elohim wipes away all tears (Rev 7:17).
"Yahuah Elohim will wipe away tears from off all faces" (Isa 25:8) - grief of exile and death ended; Jeremiah's fountain of tears for his people (Jer 9:1).

words.meaning: Solomon's house for Yahuah's name, which yet could not contain Him: 'the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee' (1 Kgs 8:27); Yahushua spoke of 'the temple of his body' (John 2:21), believers are Yahuah's temple (1 Cor 3:16), and in the city Yahuah and the Lamb are its temple (Rev 21:22).

also.meaning: The dwelling of Yahuah's presence, which the heaven of heavens cannot contain (1 Kgs 8:27): Messiah spoke of the temple of his body (John 2:21), and the assembly and each believer's body are the temple of Elohim (1 Cor 3:16; 6:19).

lexicon.title: Temple of God (Naos) and Its Worshipers

words.meaning: The soul's longing for Elohim (Ps 42:2): "ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters" (Isa 55:1); Messiah calls the thirsty to come (John 7:37) and himself thirsted on the stake (John 19:28).

Where barley was winnowed and Ruth sought redemption at Boaz's feet; Araunah's threshing floor became the altar and temple site (2 Chr 3:1), and Messiah's fan 'will throughly purge his floor', wheat to the garner and chaff to the fire (Matt 3:12).
The glory of Yahuah moves to the threshold, then departs from it (Ezek 9:3; 10:18) - leaving His house by stages; in the restored house living water issues from under the threshold (Ezek 47:1).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: "The likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone" (Ezek 1:26); "a glorious high throne from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary" (Jer 17:12) - Yahuah's rule, centered in His house (Ezek 43:7).

Hidden death within: "their throat is an open sepulchre" (Ps 5:9; Rom 3:13), hypocrites as whited sepulchres full of dead men's bones (Matt 23:27); Messiah's grave with the rich (Isa 53:9) was a new tomb whose great stone was rolled away (Matt 27:60; 28:2).
The high place in the valley of Hinnom where children were burned to idols, renamed "the valley of slaughter" (Jer 7:31-32; 19:6) - the place of burning for Yahuah's enemies (Isa 30:33).

lexicon.title: Lake of Fire and the Second Death

words.meaning: Hevel is a breath or vapor: every man at his best state is altogether vanity (Ps 39:5; 144:4), all labor under the sun is a breath (Eccl 1:2), and life is "a vapour, that appeareth for a little time" (Jas 4:14).
The brevity of life: "every man at his best state is altogether vanity" (Ps 39:5); "what is your life? It is even a vapour" that appears a little time and vanishes (Jas 4:14).

Borrowed empty vessels were filled until none was left (2 Kgs 4:6); the temple vessels carried to Babylon were profaned by Belshazzar and restored under Cyrus (Ezra 1:7); people are vessels 'unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use' (2 Tim 2:21).

also.meaning: The vessel marred in the potter's hand and made again (Jer 18:4) - Israel reworked by Yahuah; Coniah "a vessel wherein is no pleasure" (Jer 22:28); deeds kept in an earthen vessel for the return (Jer 32:14).

The holy vessels drunk from in praise of idols show Babylon profaning what is set apart to Yahuah (Dan 5:3-4) — the night her kingdom ended; set-apart vessels are His people kept for the Master's use (2 Tim 2:21).

A person as a container shaped and used by Yahuah: the marred vessel remade (Jer 18:4), vessels of wrath and of mercy (Rom 9:22-23), vessels of gold, silver, wood and earth, and a vessel unto honor purged for the Master's use (2 Tim 2:20-21).

words.meaning: "They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture" (Ps 22:18), fulfilled at the stake when the soldiers gambled for Yahushua's seamless coat (John 19:24).

Yahuah was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but in 'a still small voice' (1 Kgs 19:12), a quiet sound that sent Elijah back to his work; 'this is the way, walk ye in it' (Isa 30:21), and Yahushua's sheep hear his voice (John 10:27).

lexicon.title: Standing at the Door and Knocking

words.meaning: Nehemiah rebuilt the broken wall that Israel be 'no more a reproach' (Neh 2:17), each builder working with one hand and holding a weapon in the other (Neh 4:17), finished so the enemies knew 'this work was wrought of our Elohim' (Neh 6:16); Yahuah will be 'a wall of fire round about' (Zech 2:5).

also.meaning: "If she be a wall" (Song 8:9): a wall is chastity and defense, built upon with silver; a man without rule over his spirit is a city without walls (Prov 25:28), and Yahuah Himself is a wall of fire about Jerusalem (Zech 2:5).

Yahuah Himself as a wall of fire round about Jerusalem (Zech 2:5) and deliverance appointed for walls (Isa 26:1; 60:18); Messiah broke down the middle wall of partition (Eph 2:14), and the city has a great and high wall of jasper (Rev 21:12-18).

words.meaning: The watchman on the gate tower saw runners coming and cried the news to the king (2 Sam 18:24-27), and Jezreel's watchman knew Jehu by his driving (2 Kgs 9:20); Ezekiel is set as Israel's watchman, accountable to give warning (Ezek 33:7).

also.meaning: The prophet set on the wall to warn the house of Israel; if he fails to sound the trumpet, the blood is required at his hand (Ezek 3:17; 33:6); Israel's blind watchmen are dumb dogs (Isa 56:10).

words.meaning: Before the water gate the people gathered 'as one man' and Ezra read the book of the Torah from morning until midday (Neh 8:1-3), water and word joined, as the assembly is cleansed 'with the washing of water by the word' (Eph 5:26).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: Wax is what melts before heat: the sufferer's heart melts like wax (Ps 22:14), the wicked perish as wax before the fire, and the hills melt at the presence of Yahuah (Ps 68:2; 97:5).
"My soul is even as a weaned child" (Ps 131:2): quiet, humble rest in Yahuah without grasping, the childlike spirit required to enter the kingdom (Matt 18:3).

Achan's 'wedge' is literally a 'tongue' of gold, hidden with a Babylonish garment and silver from the accursed spoil; covetousness of devoted things troubled the whole camp (Josh 7:25), as Ananias kept back part of the price (Acts 5:2).

The true harvest gathered into the barn (Matt 3:12; 13:30) and the finest of the wheat Yahuah would feed Israel with (Ps 81:16); Messiah is the grain of wheat that dies and bears much fruit (John 12:24).

lexicon.title: Grain of Wheat Falling into the Ground

words.meaning: Elijah went up 'by a whirlwind into heaven' (2 Kgs 2:11); Yahuah answers out of the whirlwind (Job 38:1), 'hath his way in the whirlwind' (Nah 1:3), and His judgment goes forth as a whirlwind on the head of the wicked (Jer 23:19).

also.meaning: The whirlwind is Yahuah's overwhelming presence and judgment: He answers Job out of it (Job 38:1), "hath his way in the whirlwind" (Nah 1:3), and sweeps the wicked away while the righteous stand (Prov 10:25).
Yahuah's coming in storm - to speak (Job 38:1; Ezek 1:4) and to judge: "a whirlwind of Yahuah is gone forth in fury" on the head of the wicked (Jer 23:19).
"They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind" (Hos 8:7) — empty idolatry yields multiplied ruin, the law of sowing and reaping (Gal 6:7).

words.meaning: "The winter is past, the rain is over and gone" (Song 2:11): the hard season ended and the time of the beloved's call come; the sluggard will not plow in it and begs in harvest (Prov 20:4).

"I am a worm, and no man" (Ps 22:6): the suffering one brought to the lowest; the same word names the crimson worm used for scarlet dye, and Yahuah calls Israel "thou worm Jacob" before redeeming it (Isa 41:14).

also.meaning: Lowliness: "Fear not, thou worm Jacob" (Isa 41:14) and "I am a worm, and no man" (Ps 22:6); the undying worm of the rebels' carcasses outside the city (Isa 66:24; Mark 9:48).
The worm "prepared" to smite the gourd is Yahuah's small appointed agent removing comfort to teach mercy (Jonah 4:7); elsewhere "I am a worm, and no man" is the despised sufferer (Ps 22:6).

words.meaning: The priests "that kept the charge of my sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray" draw near to minister; the Levites who strayed bear their iniquity (Ezek 44:10-15) - faithfulness rewarded with nearness.

Zion is the hill Yahuah chose for His dwelling (Ps 132:13), where He set His King (Ps 2:6); the faithful have come to "mount Sion... the city of the living Elohim, the heavenly Jerusalem" (Heb 12:22).

The 1290 days run from the taking away of the daily and the setting up of the desolating abomination; "Blessed is he that waiteth" to the 1335 (Dan 12:11-12) — patient endurance rewarded beyond the trial's end.

lexicon.title: 1,260 Days (Time, Times and Half a Time)

words.meaning: The abomination of desolation is the defiling power set where it ought not, bringing ruin on the city and sanctuary; Yahushua points to it, and Luke reads it as Jerusalem "compassed with armies" (Luke 21:20).

Judah's sin is written "with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond" on the table of the heart (Jer 17:1); hearts made as adamant refuse the Torah (Zech 7:12); Ezekiel's forehead made adamant against them (Ezek 3:9).
Two sisters named by Yahuah: "Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah" (Ezek 23:4) - northern and southern kingdoms playing the harlot with Assyria, Babylon and Egypt.
Hope as "an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil" (Heb 6:19), fixed where Messiah has entered, like a nail fastened in a sure place (Isa 22:23).

The Ancient of Days is Yahuah the Father on His throne, white-haired, to whom the Son of man is brought and from whom he receives dominion (Dan 7:13-14) — two distinct figures, the giver and the receiver.
"He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye" (Zech 2:8) — Yahuah's people as the most guarded and tender part of Him (Deut 32:10).
The altar hearth of Ezekiel's house (Ezek 43:15); Jerusalem itself called Ariel, "the city where David dwelt", to become as an altar hearth in judgment (Isa 29:1-2).

words.alt: wages into a bag with holes
words.meaning: He that earns wages "earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes" (Hag 1:6) — labor that leaks away while Yahuah's house lies waste.

The band of iron and brass binds the stump during the seven times — Yahuah's restraint holding the humbled king until he lifts his eyes to heaven (Dan 4:34); He also draws His people "with bands of love" (Hos 11:4).
Isaiah walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign of Egypt's and Ethiopia's captives led away in shame (Isa 20:3-4); also a mark of mourning (2 Sam 15:30).

The place of gathered harvest: the wheat is gathered into Yahuah's garner (Matt 3:12; 13:30), while the rich fool's bigger barns cannot keep his soul (Luke 12:18-20); the tithe goes to the storehouse (Mal 3:10).

The bear raised up on one side is Medo-Persia, matching the ram whose higher horn "came up last" (Dan 8:3, 20) — one partner greater; Hos 13:8 shows Yahuah meeting the rebellious as a bear robbed of whelps.
A beast is a kingdom or its king: "These great beasts, which are four, are four kings" and "the fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth" (Dan 7:17, 23).
"The bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain" (Jer 6:29) - refining that fails; "reprobate silver shall men call them" (Jer 6:30).
Holiness to Yahuah written on horse bells and every pot in Jerusalem (Zech 14:20-21) — what was once only on the high priest's plate now on all common things.
"I will sweep it with the besom of destruction" (Isa 14:23) - Yahuah sweeping proud Babylon clean away.

words.alt: betroth thee unto me for ever
words.meaning: "I will betroth thee unto me for ever ... in righteousness, and in judgment" (Hos 2:19-20) — Yahuah's renewed marriage covenant with His people, the chaste virgin espoused to Messiah (2 Cor 11:2).
"Married": the land no longer Forsaken or Desolate, for "as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy Elohim rejoice over thee" (Isa 62:4-5).
Scattered bones joined bone to bone and filled with breath (Ezek 37:7-10): the assembly is one body with many members, each needed, joined under Messiah the head (1 Cor 12:12-27; Eph 4:16).
"A book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah, and that thought upon his name" (Mal 3:16) — His record of the faithful, the book of life.
Edom's city from which the treader of the winepress comes with garments dyed red (Isa 63:1-3) - Yahuah's vengeance on the enemies of His people; the rider's vesture dipped in blood (Rev 19:13).
"The breaker is come up before them ... and Yahuah on the head of them" (Mic 2:13) — the one who breaks open the way out of the fold, leading the gathered remnant through the gate.

words.alt: best of them is as a brier
words.meaning: "The best of them is as a brier: the most upright is sharper than a thorn hedge" (Mic 7:4) — a corrupt society that wounds whoever comes near.

The shining that comes from a source: the Son is the brightness of the Father's glory (Heb 1:3), the knowledge of Elohim's glory shining in Messiah's face (2 Cor 4:6), nations coming to the brightness of His rising (Isa 60:3).
Jerusalem made "a cup of trembling" and "a burdensome stone for all people" (Zech 12:2-3) — all who lift it are cut in pieces, as the stone grinds those it falls on (Matt 21:44).
"Ephraim is a cake not turned" (Hos 7:8) — burnt on one side and raw on the other, a people mixed among the nations, half-baked in devotion.
Jerusalem's rulers boast "this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh" (Ezek 11:3); Yahuah sets the pot on the fire to boil out her scum of filthiness (Ezek 24:6, 11-13).
"Ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall" (Mal 4:2) — the freed and fattened young leaping out to pasture, joy and growth for those who fear His name.

lexicon.title: The Prodigal's Robe, Ring and Sandals

words.meaning: "I will search Jerusalem with candles" (Zeph 1:12) — Yahuah's searching light exposing the complacent in every dark corner; "the spirit of man is the candle of Yahuah" (Prov 20:27).

words.alt: with bowl, seven lamps, seven pipes
words.meaning: The all-gold lampstand fed from its bowl means "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah" (Zech 4:6) — His people shining by His own supply, the lampstands that are assemblies (Rev 1:20).
The cankerworm devours what the locust leaves (Joel 1:4); in Nahum it pictures Nineveh's merchants multiplied and then flying away (Nah 3:16) — a swarm that consumes and is gone.
Over every dwelling of Zion a cloud by day and fire by night, "for upon all the glory shall be a defence" (Isa 4:5) - the bridal chamber covering of Yahuah's presence (Joel 2:16).

lexicon.title: Pillar of Cloud and Fire Reused

words.meaning: The four carpenters "are come to fray them, to cast out the horns of the Gentiles" (Zech 1:21) — agents Yahuah raises to break the powers that scattered His people.
The caterpillar finishes the work of the four devourers (Joel 1:4), the plague Solomon named in his prayer (1 Kgs 8:37) — complete loss that only Yahuah's restoration answers (Joel 2:25).
Idolaters shall be "as the chaff ... and as the smoke out of the chimney" (Hos 13:3) — gone without trace like morning cloud and dew.

words.alt: star of your god, tabernacle of Moloch
words.meaning: Chiun and "the star of your god" (Amos 5:26) are the star-idols Israel carried in the wilderness — worship of the host of heaven (Acts 7:42-43) instead of its Maker.
"I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities" (Amos 4:6) — famine sent as correction, each refrain ending "yet have ye not returned unto me."
Venomous serpent of wickedness - the wicked "hatch cockatrice' eggs" (Isa 59:5) and have poison under their lips (Rom 3:13); the weaned child at its den pictures its power broken (Isa 11:8).
"The daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers" (Isa 1:8) - Zion left lonely and frail after judgment strips the land.
"The colour of the terrible crystal" stretched over the creatures (Ezek 1:22) - the dazzling, awe-filled clarity before Yahuah's throne; the sea of glass like crystal (Rev 4:6).

also.meaning: The clear purity of the heavenly place: the firmament over the living creatures was "as the colour of the terrible crystal" (Ezek 1:22); the sea of glass, the city's light and the river of life are clear as crystal (Rev 4:6; 21:11; 22:1).

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: The daily (tamid) is Yahuah's continual service at His sanctuary (Exod 29:42); the horn takes it away and casts truth to the ground (Dan 8:11-12) — the continual priestly work set aside by a counterfeit system.
"Is this house... become a den of robbers in your eyes?" (Jer 7:11) - the temple used as a hiding place by those who sin and then trust its name; quoted by Yahushua (Matt 21:13).

also.meaning: The lions' den is the death decreed on Daniel for praying to Yahuah; he is lifted out because "he believed in his Elohim" (Dan 6:23), the pattern of deliverance "out of the mouth of the lion" (2 Tim 4:17).

words.alt: cast all their sins into the depths
words.meaning: "Thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea" (Mic 7:19) — Yahuah's complete removal of sin, buried as Pharaoh's host sank "into the bottom as a stone" (Exod 15:5).

"The desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory" (Hag 2:7) — the treasures of the nations brought and the latter house filled with glory, fulfilled when Messiah came to the temple.
"I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes" (Mal 3:11) — the locust and blight Yahuah sends or withholds, as in Joel 1:4.
Yahuah is a crown of glory to the remnant (Isa 28:5), and Zion a royal diadem in His hand (Isa 62:3); "the crown is fallen from our head" (Lam 5:16); "remove the diadem" from Zedekiah (Ezek 21:26).
"I will ... spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts" (Mal 2:3) — the refuse of sacrifices thrown back on priests who corrupted the covenant of Levi.
"Though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down" (Obad 4) — Edom's proud security in the rocks, the self-exalting heart Yahuah casts down.
"I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day" (Mal 4:5) — fulfilled in John, who came "in the spirit and power of Elias" to turn hearts (Luke 1:17; Matt 11:14).
"Israel is an empty vine, he bringeth forth fruit unto himself" (Hos 10:1) — the vine that multiplies altars instead of fruit for Yahuah; the true vine bears fruit by abiding (John 15:5).
From En-gedi to En-eglaim along the shore of the once-dead sea, fishermen spread their nets (Ezek 47:10) - the barren waters healed and teeming where the river from the sanctuary reaches.

lexicon.title: River of the Water of Life

words.meaning: The ephah going forth "is their resemblance through all the earth" (Zech 5:6) — the commerce-measure that holds wickedness, the false balances of Amos 8:5, carried off to Shinar.
The Chaldean horses are "more fierce than the evening wolves" (Hab 1:8); Zephaniah calls Jerusalem's judges evening wolves (Zeph 3:3) — predators who leave nothing till morning.
"Let them set a fair mitre upon his head" (Zech 3:5) — the restored high priest crowned again, the plate "Holiness to Yahuah" back on the forehead (Exod 28:36).
"Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns" (Jer 4:3) - the hardened heart that must be plowed before the word can take root.

also.meaning: "Sow to yourselves in righteousness ... break up your fallow ground: for it is time to seek Yahuah" (Hos 10:12) — the hardened heart plowed open for the word (Jer 4:3).

words.alt: famine of hearing the words of Yahuah
words.meaning: "Not a famine of bread ... but of hearing the words of Yahuah" (Amos 8:11) — Yahuah withholding His word from a people who refused it, so they run to and fro and do not find it.
The instrument of separating judgment: Yahuah fans His people in the gates (Jer 15:7) and Israel fans the mountains (Isa 41:16); Messiah's fan is in his hand to purge his floor (Matt 3:12).
"How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings" (Isa 52:7) - the messenger of deliverance who publishes "Thy Elohim reigneth" (Rom 10:15).

also.meaning: The walk and the message carried: "how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings" (Isa 52:7; Rom 10:15); feet shod with the gospel of peace (Eph 6:15), and Satan bruised under the saints' feet (Rom 16:20).

words.meaning: "Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings" (Nah 1:15) — news of the enemy's end and deliverance, applied to those sent with the good news (Rom 10:15).
The fiery stream issuing from before the Ancient of Days is His consuming judgment going out, before which the books are opened (Dan 7:10) and the beast is given to the burning flame (Dan 7:11).

lexicon.title: Lake of Fire and the Second Death

words.alt: though the fig tree shall not blossom
words.meaning: "Although the fig tree shall not blossom ... yet I will rejoice in Yahuah" (Hab 3:17-18) — total loss of field and fold met with trust in the Elohim of deliverance.
Joshua's filthy garments are iniquity: "I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment" (Zech 3:4) — Yahuah stripping sin off His priesthood.
"All our righteousnesses are as filthy rags" (Isa 64:6) - the soiled garment of a people's own righteousness, removed and replaced by Yahuah's clean raiment (Zech 3:3-4).

words.alt: I am like a green fir tree
words.meaning: Yahuah says "I am like a green fir tree. From me is thy fruit found" (Hos 14:8) — the evergreen source of all fruit, in place of the idols Ephraim has given up.
The fire that "devoured the great deep, and did eat up a part" (Amos 7:4) is the second threatened judgment, also turned back at the prophet's prayer (Amos 7:6).

lexicon.title: Fire from the Altar Cast to the Earth

words.alt: fig trees with the firstripe figs
words.meaning: Nineveh's strongholds are "like fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater" (Nah 3:12) — strength that drops at the first shake.

lexicon.title: Stars Falling and Sky Rolled Up

words.meaning: Where the river comes "there shall be a very great multitude of fish" of every kind (Ezek 47:9-10) - nations gathered into life; men made "as the fishes of the sea" by the Chaldean's net (Hab 1:14).

also.meaning: People gathered by Yahuah's net: men made as the fishes of the sea (Hab 1:14), the very great multitude of fish where the living waters flow (Ezek 47:9-10), and disciples made fishers of men (Matt 4:19).

words.meaning: "I will send for many fishers... and many hunters" to bring the scattered out of every hiding place (Jer 16:16); fishers stand by the healed waters (Ezek 47:10) - Yahushua's fishers of men (Matt 4:19).
"The smoking flax shall he not quench" (Isa 42:3) - a dimly burning wick, the faint and failing trust the Servant tends rather than snuffs out (Matt 12:20).

The flying roll, twenty by ten cubits, "is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth" (Zech 5:3) against the thief and false swearer — the Torah's curse entering and consuming the sinner's house.
"Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown" (Jonah 3:4) — a full span of testing given before judgment, in which a city may turn.

Yahuah lays in Zion a sure foundation (Isa 28:16): no other foundation can be laid than Messiah (1 Cor 3:11), built upon the apostles and prophets (Eph 2:20); Abraham looked for a city with foundations whose builder is Elohim (Heb 11:10).
"In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David ... for sin and for uncleanness" (Zech 13:1) — Yahuah's cleansing, opened through Messiah's pierced side (John 19:34).
The four horns "are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem" (Zech 1:19) — the nations' powers that lifted up their horn against Yahuah's land.
The four notable horns that replace the broken one are "four kingdoms" standing up out of the nation, "but not in his power" (Dan 8:22).

The fourth man walking loose in the fire is the one Nebuchadnezzar himself identifies: Elohim "sent his angel, and delivered his servants" (Dan 3:28); the picture is Yahuah's presence in the fire with those who trust Him (Isa 43:2).
"Like fullers' soap" (Mal 3:2) — the scouring that whitens garments; no lye can wash out sin (Jer 2:22), but Yahuah's cleansing makes robes white (Rev 7:14).

Gabriel is the messenger sent to make Daniel understand the vision (Dan 8:16; 9:21-22), the same who later announced John and Yahushua (Luke 1:19, 26) — the link between the 70 weeks and their fulfilment.

words.alt: as the garden of Eden before them
words.meaning: "The land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness" (Joel 2:3) — judgment reversing Eden; Yahuah's comfort reverses it again (Isa 51:3).
The glorious land is the land Yahuah gave His people, "the glory of all lands" (Ezek 20:6), and the holy mountain where the last power plants its tents and comes to its end (Dan 11:45).
