The gathered enemy that comes against Yahuah's people dwelling safely and is destroyed by fire and brimstone from Him (Ezek 38:16, 22); named again in the final assault on the camp of the saints (Rev 20:8).

Hosea's wife of whoredoms is Israel who "hath committed great whoredom, departing from Yahuah" (Hos 1:2); bought back for silver and barley (Hos 3:2), she pictures Yahuah's faithful love for an unfaithful bride.
The gourd "prepared" to shade Jonah, "which came up in a night, and perished in a night" (Jonah 4:10), shows a heart grieving for a plant while caring nothing for 120,000 souls.
Interpreted in the chapter itself: the first great eagle is the king of Babylon who crops the cedar top, the second is Pharaoh to whom Zedekiah turns (Ezek 17:12, 15).

lexicon.title: Two Wings of a Great Eagle

words.meaning: The great fish "prepared" by Yahuah is the grave Jonah enters and leaves on the third day, the sign Yahushua gives of His own burial and rising (Matt 12:40).

also.meaning: The prepared fish that held Jonah three days and three nights and gave him back alive is the one sign given to that generation: the Son of man in the heart of the earth (Matt 12:40).

lexicon.title: Sign of Jonah (Three Days and Nights)

words.alt: Yahuah hath prepared a sacrifice, bid his guests
words.meaning: "Yahuah hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests" (Zeph 1:7) — the day of Yahuah pictured as a slaughter-feast, the great supper of Rev 19:17.

lexicon.title: Great Supper of Yahuah (Feast of the Birds)

words.alt: fingers of a man's hand, writing on the wall
words.meaning: The hand writing on the plaster is Yahuah's own sentence on Babylon (Dan 5:24); the finger that wrote the Torah on stone (Exod 31:18) also writes judgment on those who lift themselves against Him.
"The rough goat is the king of Grecia" (Dan 8:21), coming from the west without touching the ground — the swift conquest of the leopard (Dan 7:6).

words.alt: bring forth the headstone with shoutings
words.meaning: The great mountain becomes a plain before Zerubbabel, and he brings forth "the headstone thereof with shoutings, Grace, grace unto it" (Zech 4:7) — the house finished by Yahuah's favor, the cornerstone of Ps 118:22.
The man who trusts in man "shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh" (Jer 17:5-6) - a dry, rootless life.
Yahuah puts on a helmet of deliverance upon His head (Isa 59:17); believers take the helmet of deliverance, the hope of deliverance guarding the mind (Eph 6:17; 1 Thess 5:8).
"The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it" (Isa 35:8) - the prepared road of return for Yahuah's redeemed, made ready by the voice in the wilderness (Isa 40:3; Matt 3:3).
"He will make my feet like hinds' feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places" (Hab 3:19) — sure footing Yahuah gives on hard heights when fig, vine and olive fail (Hab 3:17).
The paid keeper who flees when the wolf comes because he cares not for the sheep (John 10:12-13), the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves and not the flock (Ezek 34:2-3).
Holiness does not pass by touch from holy flesh in a skirt, but uncleanness does (Hag 2:12-13) — so a defiled people defile all the work of their hands (Hag 2:14).
"Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and ... thy hoofs brass" (Mic 4:13) — Yahuah's people given strength to thresh the gathered nations.

words.alt: bright beams out of his hand
words.meaning: "His brightness was as the light; he had horns (rays) coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power" (Hab 3:4) — Yahuah the light, His power veiled even as it shines.

words.alt: host of heaven, stars cast down
words.meaning: The host and stars cast down and stamped are "the mighty and the holy people" the horn destroys (Dan 8:24); the wise who turn many to righteousness shine "as the stars" (Dan 12:3).

lexicon.title: Stars Falling and Sky Rolled Up

words.meaning: The Father is the husbandman who tends the vine (John 15:1); Israel's leaders are tenant husbandmen who kill the heir (Matt 21:38); the laboring husbandman waits patiently for the early and latter rain (Jas 5:7).
The idol (worthless) shepherd that leaves the flock, with a sword on his arm and right eye (Zech 11:17), is the false leader Yahuah raises in judgment — the hireling who flees (John 10:12).

A man in linen with a writer's inkhorn marks those who sigh and cry before the slaughter begins (Ezek 9:4) - Yahuah's record of His own before judgment; "a book of remembrance was written" (Mal 3:16).
Set "for a wall of iron between thee and the city" (Ezek 4:3) - Yahuah's face set against Jerusalem, a barrier of siege that prayer will not pierce (Lam 3:44).
Beds and houses of ivory are the ease of those "at ease in Zion" (Amos 6:1, 4) who do not grieve for the affliction of Joseph — luxury that Yahuah will end (Amos 3:15).

words.alt: when I make up my jewels
words.meaning: "They shall be mine ... in that day when I make up my jewels" (Mal 3:17) — His peculiar treasure (segullah), the people He spares as a man spares his son.
Jezreel, "El sows," first names judgment on the house of Jehu (Hos 1:4), then the day Yahuah sows His people again in the earth (Hos 2:22-23).

words.alt: key of the house of David
words.meaning: Laid on Eliakim's shoulder: "he shall open, and none shall shut" (Isa 22:22) - authority over the king's house, applied to Messiah in Rev 3:7.
The kine of Bashan, fat cattle on the mountain of Samaria, are the wealthy who oppress the poor and say "Bring, and let us drink" (Amos 4:1) — fattened for slaughter.

words.alt: her that halteth, her that was driven out
words.meaning: "I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out" (Zeph 3:19) — the weak and scattered made a praise and a name among all people.

Moab "settled on his lees", never emptied from vessel to vessel, is complacent ease (Jer 48:11; Zeph 1:12); "wines on the lees well refined" are the rich fare of Yahuah's feast on His mountain (Isa 25:6).

also.meaning: Men "settled on their lees" (Zeph 1:12) are wine left undisturbed till it thickens — the complacent who say "Yahuah will not do good, neither will he do evil."

words.meaning: "Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?" (Jer 13:23) - sin grown into nature; the swift leopard watching over the cities is judgment (Jer 5:6; Dan 7:6).

also.meaning: The leopard with four fowl's wings is Grecia, the swift conqueror who "touched not the ground" (Dan 8:5, 21); its four heads are the four kingdoms out of the nation (Dan 8:22).

words.alt: lick the dust like a serpent
words.meaning: The nations "shall lick the dust like a serpent" (Mic 7:17) — the serpent's curse (Gen 3:14) falling on proud powers humbled before Yahuah.

words.alt: nation with teeth of a lion
words.meaning: The invading nation "whose teeth are the teeth of a lion" (Joel 1:6) — the locust army's devouring power, the same mark as the locusts of the fifth trumpet (Rev 9:8).
"Where is the dwelling of the lions ... the lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps" (Nah 2:11-12) — Assyria's capital filled with prey, now emptied by Yahuah.
"A man of unclean lips" (Isa 6:5) - speech defiled until touched from the altar; cleansed lips are sent to speak, and offer "the fruit of our lips" in praise (Hos 14:2; Heb 13:15).

words.alt: the just shall live by his faith
words.meaning: "The just shall live by his faith" (Hab 2:4) — steadfast trust in Yahuah over against the proud, quoted three times as the life of the righteous (Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38).
Four creatures of fire bearing Yahuah's throne-chariot, going "whither the spirit was to go" (Ezek 1:12) - identified as cherubim (Ezek 10:20); seen again about the throne (Rev 4:6).

Lo-ammi, "not my people," is the scattered house cut off; in the same place they are called "the sons of the living El" (Hos 1:10), which Paul applies to the called from among the nations (Rom 9:25-26).
Lo-ruhamah, "not having obtained mercy," is Israel's state under judgment; reversed when Yahuah says "I will have mercy upon her" (Hos 2:23), applied to believers in 1 Pet 2:10.

words.alt: day star, son of the morning
words.meaning: Spoken in a proverb against the king of Babylon (Isa 14:4) - the proud one who would ascend above the stars of El and is brought down to the pit; contrast Messiah, the true morning star (Rev 22:16).
"The ass knoweth his master's crib: but Israel doth not know" (Isa 1:3); Messiah laid in a manger is the sign by which humble shepherds knew him, while the city had no room (Luke 2:7, 12).

words.alt: without king, sacrifice, image, ephod, teraphim
words.meaning: Israel abides "many days without a king ... without an ephod" (Hos 3:4), and "afterward" seeks Yahuah and David their king in the latter days (Hos 3:5) — the scattering then return through Messiah.
The line measuring Jerusalem's breadth and length (Zech 2:2) marks Yahuah's claim on the city He will rebuild, as the reed measures temple and New Jerusalem (Rev 11:1; 21:15).
A man of brass measures the house with line and reed (Ezek 40:3) - Yahuah marking out what is His and holy, that Israel may be ashamed of their iniquities (Ezek 43:10).
Numbered, weighed, divided: "Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting" (Dan 5:27) — Yahuah counts the days of a kingdom, weighs its king, and gives it to another (Dan 5:28).

words.alt: my messenger, messenger of the covenant
words.meaning: "I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way" (Mal 3:1) is John (Matt 11:10); then "the Master, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant" — Yahushua.

Messiah the Prince appears after sixty-nine weeks and is "cut off, but not for himself" (Dan 9:26) — Yahushua, anointed by Yahuah with the holy spirit and with power (Acts 10:38), cut off for His people.
Michael, "one of the chief princes" and "the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people" (Dan 10:13; 12:1), is Yahuah's archangel (Jude 9) who fights the dragon (Rev 12:7).

"In the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease" (Dan 9:27) — Messiah's death in the middle of the seventieth week, after which the outer veil tore and the shadow offerings lost their force (Heb 10:12).
"Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream" (Amos 5:24) — what Yahuah wants instead of feasts and songs kept without justice.
"Your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away" (Hos 6:4) — devotion that vanishes by the heat of the day; idolaters pass the same way (Hos 13:3).
The Mount of Olives cleft to make "a very great valley" for flight (Zech 14:4-5) is Yahuah opening a way of escape for His remnant; from Olivet Yahushua ascended (Acts 1:12).
The mouth speaking great things is the little horn's blasphemy against the Most High (Dan 7:25), given again to the beast of Rev 13:5.

words.alt: cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer
words.meaning: Babylon's six-fold orchestra is the summons to bow to the golden image (Dan 3:5); the music of the state call to false worship, silenced when Babylon falls (Rev 18:22).

The least of seeds becoming a tree for the birds pictures the kingdom growing from a small beginning, as the tender twig Yahuah plants becomes a goodly cedar (Ezek 17:22-23); small belief removes mountains (Matt 17:20).

words.alt: man among the myrtle trees in the bottom
words.meaning: The rider among the myrtles in the low place is Yahuah's messenger standing with His humbled people (Zech 1:8, 11); myrtle replaces the brier when He restores (Isa 55:13).

The covering of death's face: Lazarus came forth with his face bound with a napkin (John 11:44), but Messiah's napkin lay wrapped in a place by itself (John 20:7), Yahuah destroying the covering cast over all people (Isa 25:7).
Moab and Ammon become "as Sodom ... the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation" (Zeph 2:9) — land reduced to Sodom's sterility.

lexicon.title: The Great City (Spiritually Sodom and Egypt)

words.meaning: Nineveh, "that great city," is the wicked Gentile city that repented at a forty-day warning (Jonah 3:5), condemning Israel's unbelief (Matt 12:41), and later fell when it returned to its blood (Nah 3:1).

lexicon.title: The Great City (Spiritually Sodom and Egypt)

words.alt: sun to go down at noon
words.meaning: "I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day" (Amos 8:9) — day turned to mourning, matched by the darkness at noon over Messiah's death (Matt 27:45).
The quarter from which Yahuah brings judgment on Judah by Babylon (Jer 1:14; 4:6) and from which Ezekiel's whirlwind of glory comes (Ezek 1:4); Zion is "on the sides of the north" (Ps 48:2).

words.alt: king of the north, king of the south
words.meaning: The kings of the north and south are the rival powers on either side of the glorious land whose wars pass over Yahuah's people (Dan 11:6-45); in Scripture the north is the quarter from which judgment comes (Jer 1:14).
The notable horn between the goat's eyes "is the first king" of Grecia (Dan 8:21), the mighty king of Dan 11:3, broken at the height of his strength (Dan 8:8).

Wild olive branches grafted contrary to nature into the good olive tree partake of its root and fatness, while unbelieving natural branches are broken off and may be grafted in again (Rom 11:17-24); one tree, Israel (Jer 11:16).

The full counted catch drawn on the right side into an unbroken net (John 21:11), echoing the fishermen spreading nets with fish "according to their kinds" (Ezek 47:10); Scripture shows a full ingathering where none is lost, and assigns no hidden code.
Yahuah decked Jerusalem as His bride with bracelets, chain, jewel and crown (Ezek 16:11-12); she made images of His gold and silver jewels and played the harlot (16:17) - gifts turned to idols.
"With an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of the place thereof" (Nah 1:8) — Yahuah's sweeping judgment, the flood that ends Nineveh as the flood ends the prince's city (Dan 9:26).
Wild creatures inhabiting judged Babylon and Edom (Isa 13:21; 34:11-15) - total desolation, "a cage of every unclean and hateful bird" (Rev 18:2).

lexicon.title: Dwelling of Demons, Cage of Unclean Birds

words.meaning: The palmerworm, the first of four devourers, leaves what the next consumes (Joel 1:4); Yahuah names them "my great army which I sent among you" and promises to restore those years (Joel 2:25).

"Ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls" (Jer 6:16) - the ancient walk of Yahuah's commandments which Israel refused; Messiah offers the same rest (Matt 11:29).

words.alt: look upon me whom they have pierced
words.meaning: "They shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him" (Zech 12:10) — Yahuah counts the piercing of His Son as against Himself; fulfilled at the tree (John 19:37).
Charms sewn by false prophetesses "to hunt souls" (Ezek 13:18) - deceit that slays souls that should not die and saves souls that should not live (13:19).
"I will ransom them from the power of the grave ... O death, I will be thy plagues" (Hos 13:14) — Yahuah's victory over death, quoted at the resurrection (1 Cor 15:55).
The plowman overtaking the reaper and mountains dropping sweet wine (Amos 9:13) picture overflowing harvest when Yahuah restores His people — sowing and reaping running together (John 4:35-36).
Swords beaten into plowshares (Isa 2:4) - weapons turned to tools of harvest when the nations learn Yahuah's Torah from Zion (Isa 2:3); reversed for the day of judgment (Joel 3:10).

also.meaning: Joel's call to beat plowshares into swords (Joel 3:10) is the nations arming for judgment; Isaiah and Micah reverse it — swords into plowshares when Yahuah's word goes out of Zion (Mic 4:3).

words.meaning: Yahuah stands on a wall with a plumbline in His hand "in the midst of my people Israel" (Amos 7:8) — His straight standard measuring a crooked people, after which He will not pass by them any more.
"Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar" — the blind, lame and sick brought to His table (Mal 1:7-8) — careless worship that despises Yahuah's name.
"We are the clay, and thou our potter" (Isa 64:8) - Yahuah's right to shape, remake or break a nation as the potter at his wheels (Jer 18:3-6).

also.meaning: The silver cast "unto the potter in the house of Yahuah" (Zech 11:13) ends in the potter's field (Matt 27:7) — Jerusalem's own rejected price buying a burial ground.

words.meaning: The thirty pieces cast "to the potter in the house of Yahuah" (Zech 11:13) bought the potter's field to bury strangers, Aceldama, the field of blood (Matt 27:7-10), echoing Jeremiah's broken potter's vessel at Tophet (Jer 19:11).
"My servant David a prince among them" (Ezek 34:24) and "their prince for ever" (37:25) - the Davidic ruler Yahuah sets over His united people.
The prince of the kingdom of Persia who withstood the messenger twenty-one days is the spiritual power behind an earthly kingdom (Dan 10:13, 20), the "principalities" of Eph 6:12.
"By the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water" (Zech 9:11) — release by covenant blood, the opening of the prison (Isa 61:1).

The plain seed-food Daniel chose over the king's defiling meat; the ten-day test shows that keeping Yahuah's clean walk in a foreign court left His servants fairer and fatter than those fed by Babylon (Dan 1:15).
"Then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Yahuah" (Zeph 3:9) — the reversal of Babel's confusion, one lip calling on His name.

Wages put into a bag with holes show labor without Yahuah's blessing (Hag 1:6); disciples are told to provide bags which wax not old, treasure in heaven (Luke 12:33), while Judas the thief carried the bag (John 12:6).
The idol to whom Judah's families baked cakes and poured drink offerings (Jer 7:18; 44:17) - household idolatry provoking Yahuah; Babylon boasts "I sit a queen" (Rev 18:7).

"Rachel weeping for her children refused to be comforted" (Jer 31:15) - the mother of Israel mourning exiled sons, with the promise "they shall come again" (31:16); fulfilled at Bethlehem (Matt 2:18).

lexicon.title: Out of Egypt Called My Son

words.meaning: The "flagons of wine" (raisin cakes) loved by Israel are offerings to other gods (Hos 3:1), the cakes made to the queen of heaven (Jer 7:18) — sweet things of idolatry.
"A razor that is hired... the king of Assyria" shaving Judah bare (Isa 7:20) - invading power bringing shame and stripping; Ezekiel's barber's razor portrays the same judgment (Ezek 5:1).

Set before pots of wine and cups, they refused for their father's command (Jer 35:5-6) - a family's obedience to a man shames Judah's disobedience to Yahuah; they will never lack a man to stand before Him (35:19).
The colored horses "are they whom Yahuah hath sent to walk to and fro through the earth" (Zech 1:10) — His patrols over the nations, the pattern of Revelation's horsemen.

"He is like a refiner's fire" sitting to "purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah an offering in righteousness" (Mal 3:2-3) — purifying, not destroying, His priesthood.

words.alt: rend your heart, and not your garments
words.meaning: "Rend your heart, and not your garments" (Joel 2:13) — turning to Yahuah inwardly rather than the outward show of torn clothes.
The three ribs in the bear's mouth are the prey already devoured, told "Arise, devour much flesh" (Dan 7:5) — the conquests of Medo-Persia pushing west, north and south (Dan 8:4).

The side of favor and life: the waters issue from the right side of the house (Ezek 47:1), the sheep stand on the right (Matt 25:33), and the net cast on the right side of the ship brings the great catch (John 21:6).
The rims of the wheels "so high that they were dreadful" and full of eyes (Ezek 1:18) - the towering, fearful majesty of Yahuah's moving throne.

words.alt: thousands of rams, ten thousands of rivers of oil
words.meaning: Rams by thousands and rivers of oil (Mic 6:7) are lavish offerings without obedience; what Yahuah requires is "to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim" (Mic 6:8).
"The lion hath roared, who will not fear? Yahuah Elohim hath spoken, who can but prophesy?" (Amos 3:8) — Yahuah's voice of judgment from Zion, the roar of Rev 10:3.

words.alt: leave them neither root nor branch
words.meaning: Neither root nor branch left (Mal 4:1) — the utter end of the wicked, nothing to sprout again, against the righteous who "grow up as calves of the stall" (Mal 4:2).

lexicon.title: Lake of Fire and the Second Death

words.meaning: Corrosion of hoarded wealth: Jerusalem is the pot whose scum is in it (Ezek 24:6); rust corrupts earthly treasure (Matt 6:19), and the rust of the rich man's gold is a witness against him (Jas 5:3).
"Saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be Yahuah's" (Obad 21) — deliverers raised by Yahuah, who alone is Savior (Isa 43:11).

A roll written within and without with lamentations, mourning and woe, eaten by the prophet (Ezek 2:9-3:3) - Yahuah's word taken inward before it is spoken; burned by Jehoiakim yet rewritten (Jer 36:23, 28).

"Burning ones" standing above Yahuah's throne crying "Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah of hosts" (Isa 6:3) - the highest emphasis on His holiness; the same word names the fiery serpents of the wilderness (Num 21:6).

Upon one stone are seven eyes, "the eyes of Yahuah, which run to and fro through the whole earth" (Zech 4:10) — His full sight resting on the stone, and "I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day" (Zech 3:9).

lexicon.title: Seven Spirits (Seven Lamps and Seven Eyes)

words.meaning: The seven times are the full measure of Nebuchadnezzar's humbling "till thou know that the most High ruleth" (Dan 4:25); seven is Yahuah's complete measure of correction (Lev 26:18).

words.alt: shake the heavens and the earth
words.meaning: "Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth" (Hag 2:6) — the removing of shaken things so the kingdom that cannot be moved remains (Heb 12:27-28).
The city's name: "Yahuah is there" (Ezek 48:35) - the end of the vision, His dwelling with His people for ever (Rev 21:3).

The gathered flock of Yahuah (Mic 2:12): whoever climbs in another way is a thief, and Messiah has other sheep not of this fold to bring, "and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd" (John 10:1, 16).
"The waters of Shiloah that go softly" (Isa 8:6) - Yahuah's quiet provision through the house of David, refused; so He brings the River, the king of Assyria, to overflow to the neck (Isa 8:7-8).
Shinar, where Babel was built (Gen 11:2) and Nebuchadnezzar stored the temple vessels (Dan 1:2), is the house built for the woman Wickedness (Zech 5:11) — Babylon as wickedness' home.
The ships of Chittim are western sea-power coming against the northern king (Dan 11:30), echoing Balaam's word that ships from Chittim would afflict Asshur (Num 24:24).
"Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe" (Joel 3:13) — the time of judgment come; the harvest is the end of the world and the reapers the angels (Matt 13:39).

words.alt: sift Israel as corn in a sieve
words.meaning: "I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall" (Amos 9:9) — scattering that separates yet loses no true grain.
"I will take thee, O Zerubbabel ... and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee" (Hag 2:23) — the chosen one bearing Yahuah's authority, reversing the signet torn off Coniah (Jer 22:24).

The waters of Shiloah that go softly, which Israel refused (Isa 8:6); the blind man washed in the pool of Siloam, "which is by interpretation, Sent" (John 9:7), and came seeing, washing in the Sent One.
"Who hath despised the day of small things?" (Zech 4:10) — small beginnings of Yahuah's work, watched by His seven eyes, growing like the mustard seed.
Not a hair singed, coats unchanged, "nor the smell of fire" on them (Dan 3:27) — the fire burned only the bands that held them; trials consume the bonds, not the faithful (Isa 43:2).

words.alt: smite the judge of Israel with a rod
words.meaning: "They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek" (Mic 5:1) — the humiliation of Israel's appointed ruler, fulfilled in Messiah struck before His accusers.
"Smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered" (Zech 13:7) — Yahuah's sword raised against the man He appointed as shepherd, fulfilled when the disciples fled (Matt 26:31).
The proverb blaming fathers for the children's punishment is overturned: "the soul that sinneth, it shall die" (Ezek 18:4, 20) - each one answers for his own sin.

words.alt: pour out my spirit upon all flesh
words.meaning: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28) — Yahuah's own power poured on sons, daughters and servants, fulfilled at Shavuot (Acts 2:16-18).

lexicon.title: Tongues as of Fire at Shavuot

words.meaning: A rod out of the stem of Jesse (Isa 11:1) - the house of David cut down to a stump, from which Messiah springs as a fresh shoot.
Sticks written for Judah and for Joseph/Ephraim become one in the prophet's hand (Ezek 37:16-19) - the two houses made one nation under one king, "David my servant" (37:22-24).

words.alt: stone cry out of the wall, beam answer
words.meaning: "The stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it" (Hab 2:11) — houses built by wrong testify against their builders.
Yahuah of hosts is "for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling" to both houses of Israel (Isa 8:14) - the same Stone that saves the believing trips the disobedient (1 Pet 2:8).
The stork, turtle, crane and swallow keep their appointed times, "but my people know not the judgment of Yahuah" (Jer 8:7) - creatures that heed their order shame a people who do not.

also.meaning: Two women with stork's wings carry the ephah to Shinar (Zech 5:9) — the unclean bird (Lev 11:19) bearing wickedness back to Babylon where it belongs.

words.meaning: The public life of a city: truth is fallen in the street (Isa 59:14), the hypocrites pray on street corners (Matt 6:5) but the street of the new city is pure gold (Rev 21:21).
"With his stripes we are healed" (Isa 53:5) - the scourging laid on the Servant became the healing of those who had gone astray (1 Pet 2:24).

The stump left in the earth is the kingdom kept in reserve: "thy kingdom shall be sure unto thee, after that thou shalt have known that the heavens do rule" (Dan 4:26); a stump with life still in it is Yahuah's pattern of restoration (Isa 6:13; 11:1).
The basket of summer fruit (qayits) means "The end (qets) is come upon my people Israel" (Amos 8:2) — ripe fruit at season's close, a nation ripe for judgment.
Abandoned Israel was "not swaddled at all" until Yahuah passed by (Ezek 16:4-6); the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes lying in a manger is the sign given to the shepherds (Luke 2:12).

The common, lowly tree (1 Kgs 10:27) that proud Israel boasted to replace with cedars (Isa 9:10); Amos the herdsman gathered its fruit (Amos 7:14), and Zacchaeus climbed one to see Yahushua (Luke 19:4).
"In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen" (Amos 9:11) — James reads it as the nations gathered to Yahuah's name through Messiah (Acts 15:16-17).
The talent of lead cast on the ephah's mouth holds wickedness shut in (Zech 5:8) — Yahuah's weight restraining evil until it is removed.
Women weeping for Tammuz at the gate of Yahuah's house (Ezek 8:14) - a heathen idol's mourning rite brought into the sanctuary, a "greater abomination" (8:15).
Tarshish is the far place of flight "from the presence of Yahuah" (Jonah 1:3); its ships are the pride Yahuah breaks (Ps 48:7) and later bring His sons home (Isa 60:9).
The fourth beast's great iron teeth that "devoured and brake in pieces" (Dan 7:7) are its crushing conquest; Joel's invader likewise has "the cheek teeth of a great lion" (Joel 1:6).

also.meaning: Devouring power of an invading people: a nation whose teeth are the teeth of a lion (Joel 1:6), the fourth beast with great iron teeth (Dan 7:7), the locusts with lions' teeth (Rev 9:8); gnashing of teeth marks the rejected (Matt 8:12).

words.meaning: Felled like a teil tree and an oak whose substance remains, "so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof" (Isa 6:13) - the remnant left alive in a cut-down nation.

words.alt: root out of a dry ground
words.meaning: "He shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground" (Isa 53:2) - Messiah's lowly, unpromising beginning from the parched stock of David.

words.alt: third part brought through the fire
words.meaning: "I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver" (Zech 13:9) — the refined remnant who call on His name: "It is my people." Three here is a share, not a godhead.
Thirty pieces of silver, a slave's price (Exod 21:32), are the "goodly price that I was prised at of them" (Zech 11:13), cast to the potter — the price of Yahushua's betrayal (Matt 27:9-10).

words.alt: three plucked up by the roots
words.meaning: The three first horns plucked up are three kings the little horn "shall subdue" to make room for itself (Dan 7:24) — not a picture of anything divine, only of kingdoms overthrown.
Days the prophet lay on his left side bearing the iniquity of the house of Israel, "according to the number of the years of their iniquity" (Ezek 4:5) - each day a year of the northern kingdom's sin.
Weak Jacob made "a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth" to thresh the mountains (Isa 41:15) - Yahuah using His humbled people to beat down proud powers.
Ezekiel portrays Jerusalem on a tile and lays siege to it - "a sign to the house of Israel" (Ezek 4:1-3); brick is also the material of Babel and of Egypt's bondage (Gen 11:3; Exod 1:14).

words.alt: many shall run to and fro
words.meaning: "Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased" (Dan 12:4) — searching through the sealed words; Amos shows the opposite famine, running to and fro seeking the word and not finding it (Amos 8:12).

The toes, part iron and part clay, are the kingdom's divided final state (Dan 2:41-42); "in the days of these kings" Yahuah sets up His kingdom (Dan 2:44), matching the ten horns that are ten kings (Dan 7:24).
The sanctuary instrument that carries the altar coal to the prophet's lips (Isa 6:6) - cleansing comes from Yahuah's own altar by His appointed means, not from the hand of man.
"His train filled the temple" (Isa 6:1) - the hem of Yahuah's robe filling the sanctuary, His glory overflowing the house; the same word names the hem of the high priest's robe (Exod 28:33).
Cropped by the eagle = Jehoiachin carried to Babylon (Ezek 17:4, 12); the tender twig Yahuah Himself plants on Israel's high mountain is the Branch of David (Ezek 17:22).
The two olive trees "are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Adon of the whole earth" (Zech 4:14), pouring golden oil into the lamp; Rev 11:4 names the two witnesses the same.
The merchant city of the seas whose pride said "I am a god" (Ezek 28:2) - its king set in Eden as a covering cherub and cast down; its fall is the pattern of Babylon's mourners (Rev 18).

lexicon.title: Tyre's Mourners: Kings, Merchants and Mariners

words.meaning: False prophets daub a flimsy wall with untempered mortar, crying "Peace" where there is none (Ezek 13:10); hail and stormy wind bring it down - a whitewashed cover over corruption (Matt 23:27).

words.alt: loins girded with fine gold of Uphaz
words.meaning: The girdle of fine gold of Uphaz marks the heavenly messenger's royal-priestly office, the golden girdle seen again on the one among the lampstands (Rev 1:13).

lexicon.title: Seven Angels in White Linen with Golden Sashes

words.meaning: The valley of Jehoshaphat, "Yahuah judges," is the valley of decision where the nations are gathered to judgment (Joel 3:2, 14) — the harvest and winepress of Rev 14.

words.alt: sit every man under his vine
words.meaning: "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid" (Mic 4:4) — the settled peace of Yahuah's kingdom, offered again in Zech 3:10.

The poisonous brood of the wicked who hatch cockatrice eggs (Isa 59:5); John and Yahushua call the hypocrites a generation of vipers (Matt 3:7; 23:33), and Paul shakes the viper into the fire unharmed (Acts 28:5; Luke 10:19).
A sign to the house of David: the virgin bears a son called Immanuel, "El with us" (Isa 7:14) - Yahuah's presence with His people in the son He gives (Matt 1:23).
"His visage was so marred more than any man" (Isa 52:14) - the Servant disfigured outwardly by the hands of men while wholly without blemish within (Isa 53:9).
"I, saith Yahuah, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her" (Zech 2:5) — the city's defense is His presence, not stone.

lexicon.title: Pillar of Cloud and Fire Reused

words.meaning: The watchers are Yahuah's holy messengers who carry His decree, "to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men" (Dan 4:17).

words.alt: stand upon my watch, set me upon the tower
words.meaning: Habakkuk stands on his watch and tower "to see what he will say unto me" (Hab 2:1) — the watchman's post of waiting for Yahuah's word.

words.alt: earth filled with the knowledge of the glory
words.meaning: "The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahuah, as the waters cover the sea" (Hab 2:14) — His glory overtaking the proud kingdoms, the earth lightened in Rev 18:1.

lexicon.title: Angel Lighting the Earth with Glory

words.meaning: The wicked are like the troubled sea whose waters cast up mire and dirt (Isa 57:20): the doubter is like a wave driven by the wind (Jas 1:6), and false teachers are raging waves foaming out their own shame (Jude 13).
"The weeds were wrapped about my head" (Jonah 2:5) — the binding of the grave, "the bottoms of the mountains" and the earth's bars, from which Yahuah brought up his life.

Seventy weeks of years were "determined" upon Daniel's people to finish transgression, make reconciliation and anoint the most holy (Dan 9:24); all seventy are complete, fulfilled in Messiah's coming, ministry and death.
"How is she become as a widow!" (Lam 1:1) - Jerusalem bereft of her people and her Husband's protection; Babylon boasts she will never sit as a widow, yet will (Isa 47:8-9; Rev 18:7).
He looked for judgment and found oppression, for righteousness and found a cry (Isa 5:7) - the bad fruit of a carefully tended people, by which a tree is known (Matt 7:16).
Daniel's open windows toward Jerusalem, kneeling three times a day, are the faithful turning to Yahuah's chosen place in exile as Solomon asked (1 Kgs 8:48) — the habit no decree could stop.
"Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse ... I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing" (Mal 3:10) — openings once for flood, now for blessing on the obedient.
Built in the vineyard for fruit (Isa 5:2), it becomes the place of wrath: "I have trodden the winepress alone" (Isa 63:3); Yahuah treads Judah as in a winepress (Lam 1:15; Rev 14:19).

also.meaning: The full press and overflowing fats are wickedness ripe for treading (Joel 3:13), the winepress of the wrath of Yahuah (Rev 14:19).

lexicon.title: Vine of the Earth and the Winepress

words.meaning: Nineveh is "the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms" (Nah 3:4), the pattern of Babylon whose sorceries deceived all nations (Rev 18:23).
The woman sitting in the ephah: "This is wickedness" (Zech 5:8) — pressed down under lead and carried to Shinar, the land of Babylon, to be set on her own base; the pattern of the harlot Babylon.
Crimson sins made "as wool" (Isa 1:18) - cleansed whiteness; the hair of the Ancient of Days "like the pure wool" (Dan 7:9; Rev 1:14).
From the sole of the foot to the head, wounds and putrifying sores (Isa 1:6) - the sickness of a rebellious nation, healed only when Yahuah binds up (Jer 30:17; Hos 6:1).

words.alt: wounded in the house of my friends
words.meaning: "What are these wounds in thine hands? ... Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends" (Zech 13:6) — wounds received from one's own house, the betrayal Messiah suffered.
